title: Creating a new tab leaves the first tab unable to accept input
description:
Opening a second tab silently kills input in the first one. The user's existing
work becomes unusable the moment they open a new tab — the highest-severity
symptom of the set.

Screenshot 2026-07-26: tab 1 (`Users/shady`) has run `ls` successfully and shows
a fresh prompt block with a cursor, but after tab 2 was created it no longer
accepts keystrokes.

Suspected area: input ownership / InputTarget registry per ADR-0004 — creating a
tab appears to move the active input target without the previous tab keeping or
regaining its own. Sibling bug: switching back to a tab needs a click into the
editor first.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the app. Type in tab 1 — works.
2. Click `+` to create a second tab.
3. Switch back to tab 1 and type.

Observed: tab 1 does not accept the typed characters.
Expected: tab 1 accepts input exactly as it did before tab 2 existed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With N tabs open, every tab accepts keyboard input when it is the active tab,
  regardless of creation order or how many tabs were opened after it.
- Creating a tab does not mutate any other tab's input state.
- A test opens two tabs, returns to the first, and asserts a typed character
  reaches that tab's input target.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged to main as 8f15a54 (fix commit e349e9d).

Root cause: _globalKeydown is registered on document by EVERY TerminalContent and was guarded only by !target.isConnected. Inactive panes use visibility:hidden rather than display:none, so a hidden tab's guard passed. Its handler saw document.activeElement outside its own containers and called focus() on its own editor, stealing the keystroke from the active tab. The guard now also requires the pane to carry the active class.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by the coordinator, not accepted from the worker's report: with the fix e2e/multi-tab-input.spec.ts passes 2/2; with the one-line guard reverted the cross-tab test fails. The test asserts observable behaviour — a typed OSC 0 command changes tab 1's title — and carries a negative control that tab 2's title must NOT change, which is what makes it a focus-theft test rather than a smoke test.

Full gate green on the merged tree: gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test -race, root prettier and eslint, tsc, vitest 26 files / 539 tests, and the full e2e suite 20/20.

TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN rather than quietly folded in:
- nocx-ifgp — the new spec flakes under full-suite load, roughly one failure in three suite runs, while passing 3/3 in isolation. Measured, not suspected. Filed rather than ignored, because reporting this as simply green would repeat the nocx-d3q failure where a suite passed while the feature was broken.
- The guard reads target.classList.contains('active') — behaviour keyed on a CSS class. Tab.setActive already holds an authoritative _active boolean one line above where it toggles that class, so the fix re-derives ownership from presentation. It also crosses the nocx-njrx migration boundary: tabs.ts sets the class and WILL be rewritten in Solid, terminal-content.ts reads it and stays imperative under AD-6. ADR-0012 says state crosses that boundary through explicit methods, not DOM inspection. Accepted anyway because TabContent has no activation hook to use — only mount, viewportChanged, focus, dispose — so the proper fix means widening that seam, which is too much to block a P0 on. Follow-up needed.

nocx-4ff.29 is NOT fixed by this and stays open; the new test clicks into the editor after the tab switch precisely to isolate the two.

title: Switching tab placement back to Horizontal does not restore the tab strip
description:
Switching Tab placement back to Horizontal does not restore the tab strip. The
only recovery is restarting the app.

Distinct from the sibling bug where vertical renders empty: this one is the
return path. Even if vertical rendered correctly, a placement change must be
reversible without a restart. Same root area — see nocx-ycet.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set Interface > Tab placement = Vertical (tabs disappear — sibling bug).
2. Set it back to Horizontal.

Observed 2026-07-26 on main: the setting reads `Horizontal` / `Default` again,
but the UI does not change — the top bar stays collapsed to a bare `+` and no
tabs return.

Expected: the horizontal tab bar returns with every open tab listed and the
active one marked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Vertical -> Horizontal restores the horizontal bar with all open tabs, no
  restart.
- Round-tripping placement N times leaves exactly one strip in the DOM (no
  orphaned strip elements accumulating).
- Tab identity and active selection survive both directions.
close_reason: Fixed by the same commit as nocx-98z6 (c28bd4d). The V→H swap carried .tabstrip-vertical (width:240px) into the horizontal strip, narrowing it and hiding tabs. The replaceStrip fix resets all container classes and ARIA attributes before re-mounting, so both directions work. Test covers V→H specifically: starts with VerticalTabStrip, replaces with HorizontalTabStrip, asserts .tabstrip-vertical gone and .tabbar present, tab count preserved.

title: Vertical tab placement renders an empty strip — no tabs at all
description:
Setting Tab placement to Vertical leaves the user with no tab list at all.

nocx-d3q closed as complete with e2e green across both placements, so this is
either a regression landed after that epic or a gap the headless e2e harness
(cmd/devharness) does not see — the failing path is likely the live swap
through `tm.replaceStrip` (frontend/src/main.ts:157-178) rather than a cold
start already in vertical mode. Confirm which before fixing: a cold start in
vertical mode is a different bug from a live swap into it.

Underlying cause is filed as the epic nocx-ycet — the strip is replaced at the
composition root while tab state lives inside TabManager, so the two disagree.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the app with one or more tabs open (horizontal, the default).
2. Open Settings (Cmd+, or the gear in the activity bar).
3. Interface > Tab placement > Vertical.

Observed 2026-07-26 on main: the top bar collapses to a bare `+` button and no
tab is listed anywhere — neither along the top nor down the left edge. The open
tab still exists (its content renders in the pane) but is unreachable.

Expected: the tabs move to a vertical strip down the left edge, per the epic's
Warp-style spec — per-row icon, title, subtitle, status indicator, `+` in the
panel header.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With N tabs open, switching to Vertical lists all N in the vertical strip,
  the active one marked active.
- Starting the app cold with placement already Vertical lists them too.
- Clicking a row in the vertical strip switches to that tab.
- An e2e test covers the live swap (not only cold start in each mode), because
  that is the case the current suite missed.
close_reason:
Root cause: TabManager.replaceStrip cleared innerHTML but left the old strip's className and ARIA attributes on the container. After H→V swap, .tabbar (height:38px; overflow:hidden) clipped vertical tabs to invisible. After V→H swap, .tabstrip-vertical (width:240px) narrowed the horizontal strip.

Fix: reset className, role, aria-label, aria-orientation before re-mounting the new strip in replaceStrip (frontend/src/tabs.ts:414-423). Tests cover both H→V and V→H directions and assert tab-count preservation.

Committed c28bd4d on shady2k/fix-nocx-98z6-vertical-tabs, pushed to origin.

title: Restore the tab bar on pr-11-boundary: undo the shell change 557e87d made in passing
description:
557e87d deleted <div id="tabbar"> from frontend/index.html, passed TabManager a display:none container, and hand-rolled a tab list in the sidebar. This is why 4 e2e tests fail on pr-11-boundary and pass on main: they click .tab-add, which now sits inside a hidden element, so Playwright resolves it and waits forever for it to become visible.

Restore the horizontal tab bar so this branch is about the credential boundary and nothing else. The redesign is deliberately deferred to epic nocx-d3q, where horizontal stays the default anyway — so this restore is not throwaway work, it is the default mode.

Keep: the Connections view in the activity bar and everything it opens (tm.newManagerTab), ProfileClient, the SSH work. Remove: the hiddenBar container, the hand-rolled sidebar session list, and the migration of the update notice into the sidebar (it belongs in the tab bar again).

Acceptance: the 4 blockers go green (activity.spec.ts:10 chromium, tabs.spec.ts:8 both projects, activity-bell.spec.ts:12 webkit) without touching a single e2e file.

Blocks the merge of PR #12.
close_reason:
Restored in e5ad9f2 (tab bar, hiddenBar removal, sidebar list removal, dead CSS) and d463fa1 (the tab.onBufferChange -> syncAltScreenClass wiring 557e87d dropped, which also fixed terminal content rendering under the macOS traffic lights during any full-screen TUI).

Verified locally on both engines: activity.spec.ts:10 and tabs.spec.ts:8 pass, having failed before. activity-bell.spec.ts:12 still fails but now identically to main — the test clicks .tab-add while alt-screen hides it by design, split out as nocx-9ci.

title: PR11-T2: harden the renderer against injection (XSS, CSP, inspector, import policy)
description:
Plan v3 Task 2, and the highest-severity item. Runs BEFORE socket auth: a token handed to an injectable renderer protects nothing, because injected same-origin code calls the binding and gets it.

Verified chain: internal/importer/tabby.go parses an untrusted YAML the user imports -> credential names from it are interpolated into HTML at frontend/src/connections.ts:472-475 with no escaping -> frontend/index.html has NO CSP -> injected code calls open and gets a PTY.

Work: replace innerHTML with textContent/element construction for anything carrying stored or imported data (audit main.ts x2, sidebar.ts, tabs.ts x2 as well); add a CSP that works under both Vite dev and a Wails production build; block untrusted navigation; ensure OpenInspectorOnStartup is off in production; decide the Tabby import policy — the YAML also carries an inline Password (importer/tabby.go:31-44) that travels through a JSON-RPC Config string, so renderer, transport buffers and frame logging all see it even though the converter drops it.
acceptance_criteria: A credential named renders as literal text and creates no element. index.html carries a CSP that forbids inline script and foreign origins, and the app still runs under Vite dev and a Wails production build. Devtools inspector off in production. Tabby import policy decided and recorded.
close_reason: connections.ts builds the credential panel with createElement/textContent; CSP added with script-src 'self' (no unsafe-inline — verified no inline script in either Vite dev or the prod build), connect-src pinned to loopback, base-uri none; prod inspector off in main.go

title: PR11-T1: stop the two active disclosures (log line + raw control frames)
description:
Plan v3 Task 1. Two live disclosures, no dependencies.

1. frontend/src/tabs.ts:560 logs JSON.stringify(this.sshOpts), which carries password and jumpPassword. Delete the line — do NOT replace with a redacted variant; T4 removes the secret from that object entirely.
2. internal/transport/ws.go:417-429 logs malformed/unparsable control frames verbatim, so a truncated credentials.savePassword puts a password in the log. Replace with size + parse-error category + request id. Transport-wide rule: any control frame may carry a secret, so none are logged verbatim.
acceptance_criteria: tabs.ts no longer logs sshOpts. A truncated credentials.savePassword frame produces a log record containing no substring of the password. Test captures logs via a slog handler over bytes.Buffer, following the existing suite's log.NewSlogAdapter construction.
close_reason: ws.go logs len+category via errors.As (never err.Error(), never raw bytes); tabs.ts sshOpts log line deleted; -race test asserts no 'data' key for truncated credentials.savePassword and non-object frames

title: PR11-T4: move the wire to profile IDs — one atomic commit
description:
Plan v3 Task 4. Backend contract, frontend migration and removal of the plaintext-lookup RPCs land TOGETHER — split across commits leaves an intermediate state where SSH cannot connect at all.

Use the seam the PR author already built: ssh.WithCredentials(store, identity) (ssh.go:139-146), forwarded by session.go:274, resolves the password inside the SSH package at ssh_auth.go:117-118. The resolver maps profileID -> {host, credential.Identity, non-secret options}. Nothing in transport/session/connection holds plaintext.

GET THE MODEL RIGHT: SSHProfile is Base + Options (profile.go:71-74); host/port/user/auth/jump live under Options. Options.CredentialID references a reusable Credential, and when set, username/auth/keyPath come from the CREDENTIAL not the profile (profile.go:49-56, :95-108). Secrets saved by credential ID key on Identity{User: credentialID} (ws.go:1030-1035); inline mode keys on {user,host,port}. Handle both.

JUMP NEEDS AN SSH-LAYER CHANGE: ConnectConfig carries ONE Credentials/CredIdentity pair, for the target (ssh.go:66-70), and connectToJumpHost builds jumpCfg with Password: cfg.JumpPassword and never forwards Credentials (ssh_dial.go:109-116). Add JumpCredentials + JumpCredIdentity, forward them, and surface through session.sshOptionsFromConfig (session.go:246-278).

Wire removals include jumpAuthMode. Frontend: password resolution happens TWICE in connections.ts (:273-319 and :565-611); ProfileClient.lookupPassword at profiles.ts:278-280; tabs.ts declarations and callers around 129-142, 909-916, 944-958, 1009-1021. Delete TestCredentialsRPC_SaveLookup (ws_profiles_test.go:144).

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE in fe6e614 — held open only by the nocx-hl3 dependency, not by remaining work here.

Landed: client sends profileId only; internal/connection.Resolver maps it to host + credential.Identity + non-secret options on the backend; the secret resolves inside internal/ssh via ssh.WithCredentials. ConnectConfig lost Password/JumpPassword. lookupPassword and lookupKeyPassphrase removed from the transport (the surviving lookupKeyPassphrase is a private method inside internal/ssh — the intended design). credentials.savePassword still accepts a password inbound, which is correct: the boundary is about outward travel. All gates green including go test -race ./... and vitest 381/381.

Guarded by TestNoPlaintextSecretsOnWire: two canaries (target + jump credential), four RPCs (profiles.list, credentials.list, open target, open jump), assertion on RAW RESPONSE BYTES rather than decoded fields so a secret-bearing field added later fails it. Verified live by mutation — repointing the canary at a value the response does contain makes it fail — so it is not passing vacuously.

Correctly blocked by nocx-hl3: routing secrets behind a profile ID is worth little while the socket carrying that ID is not authenticated in a release build. hl3's code is done; what remains is capturing the production Origin from CI's macos-latest runner. Close hl3 first, then this.
acceptance_criteria: Password auth, public-key auth (Credential.KeyPath -> WithKeyFile) and jump connections all work; jump passes its own store and identity, never a password. Unknown profile ID errors naming the ID. lookupPassword/lookupKeyPassphrase return -32601; hasPassword still works. No frontend type crossing the socket has password/jumpPassword; tsc clean. A test exercises the real auth-chain construction for BOTH hops, not just the returned options. Quick-connect behaviour decided and recorded.
close_reason: Implementation landed in fe6e614; the blocking dependency nocx-hl3 is now closed. See that commit and the bead description for detail.

title: PR11-T3: authenticate the local WebSocket (subprotocol capability + origin/host policy)
description:
IMPLEMENTED but NOT DONE — do not close on a green CI.

Landed: per-launch crypto/rand token in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, constant-time compare, selected subprotocol echoed, Start fails closed on entropy error, OriginPolicy interface with LoopbackOriginPolicy (default) and PinnedOriginPolicy (empty = deny all), authorize() before Upgrade, WithListenAddr, GetWSToken binding + regenerated wailsjs, devharness WSTOKEN, e2e harness requiring the token with no bypass, e2e/auth.spec.ts. All gates green including go test -race ./... .

OUTSTANDING, and it is the reason this stays open: the production Origin is uncaptured. PinnedOriginPolicy is therefore unused, so a release build runs on LoopbackOriginPolicy, which accepts only http/https schemes. A packaged Wails app sends a wails:// Origin and would be rejected by our own check — the app refusing itself.

CI cannot reveal this: the e2e job runs 'wails dev', which serves http://localhost:34115, i.e. a loopback http origin that passes. So green CI is not evidence.

Next step: capture Origin and Host from a real build on CI's macos-latest runner (log them at the upgrade in a temporary step), pin the value in PinnedOriginPolicy, wire it for the production runtime mode, and only then close.

CORRECTION on how to capture the production Origin — the obvious plan does not work.

The coordinator initially assumed the existing e2e CI job could capture it by logging the Origin header at the upgrade. It cannot. ci.yml says so itself: 'Playwright drives its own Chromium against :34115, so the app's webview engine (WKWebView here, WebKit2GTK on Linux) is never what these tests observe.' In that job Playwright talks to the dev server, so the header would read http://localhost:34115 — the dev-server origin, not the shipped webview's. Worse, that value is plausible enough to be mistaken for the real one and pinned by accident, which would reject the real client at release time and look like a token bug.

The Origin is only observable when the BUILT app runs with its own WKWebView. Capturing it needs a dedicated step on macos-latest: wails build, run the binary (a macOS runner has a window server), and read what it sends on the WebSocket upgrade. Small, but a separate piece of work rather than an addition to the e2e job.

Until then PinnedOriginPolicy stays empty and unused, the default remains LoopbackOriginPolicy, and a release build would reject its own webview because that policy accepts only http/https schemes. Green CI is not evidence here — see above for why.
acceptance_criteria: No token, wrong token, hostile Origin and wrong Host each fail BEFORE upgrade; open is unreachable in every case. Correct token+origin+host succeeds with behaviour unchanged. Token fresh per launch, never logged or persisted. Entropy failure fails closed. e2e authenticates for real and a case asserts unauthenticated access fails. Production Origin captured from a real build, not guessed.
close_reason:
Complete in e106b72. The production Origin is captured, not guessed: origin=wails://wails.localhost:34115, host=127.0.0.1:49308, read off the CI e2e job on macos-latest where wails dev runs the real WKWebView alongside Playwright.

That capture also corrected two coordinator errors recorded on this bead. It does NOT need a dedicated macOS build job — the value was in the log all along, withheld by this task's own decision to omit attacker-controlled headers from the rejection log. And the self-rejection was not a release-only risk: the app was being refused 32 times per CI run against zero on main, and those failures were provisionally written off as suite flakiness across four runs before the log was read.

Landed overall: per-launch crypto/rand token in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol with constant-time compare and the selected subprotocol echoed; Start fails closed on entropy error; OriginPolicy interface with LoopbackOriginPolicy (now accepting the wails:// webview by scheme+hostname, port ignored because a packaged build has none) and PinnedOriginPolicy (empty = deny all); authorize() before Upgrade; WithListenAddr; GetWSToken binding and regenerated wailsjs; devharness WSTOKEN; e2e harness requiring the token with no bypass; e2e/auth.spec.ts.

The rejection log now carries Origin, Host and path, with the reasoning for that reversal in the code: a rejection nobody can diagnose is worse than one that quotes what it rejected, and production is the one environment where you cannot attach a debugger. Runtime-mode gating and rate limiting split out as nocx-49v.

title: PR11-T5: bind a stored credential to its resolved target host
description:
Plan v3 Task 5. Credential.Host is optional and empty means 'works for any host' (profile.go:105-107). The same authenticated renderer can create profiles AND call open, so it can point a victim credential at a host it controls and have the backend submit that password — even though T4 stops the password being returned. Strict known_hosts limits which hosts answer; it is not credential authorization.

POLICY, decided in the plan, not delegated: a stored password credential must carry a bound host and effective port; an unbound credential is refused at connection time. The approval-record alternative was rejected because the approval UI would live in the renderer — the actor this task constrains.

ENFORCEMENT POINT MATTERS: resolveConfig is an unexported method on RealClient (ssh_config.go:26-28) merging ~/.ssh/config with precedence explicit > config > default, so the authoritative host/port exist only inside internal/ssh. Enforce there, immediately after resolveConfig, before any authentication attempt. internal/connection passes the ALLOWED host/port and does not decide — a second resolution implementation that disagrees is exactly how a credential binds to the wrong target.

Existing unbound credentials need a migration path; choose during implementation and record it.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE in 6b6a166 — held open only by the dependency chain (nocx-gfh, itself held by nocx-hl3), not by remaining work here.

Enforcement lives in internal/ssh after resolveConfig, before any dial, and matches the RESOLVED hostname and effective port. Never the alias: ~/.ssh/config can map Host->HostName, so a check on the alias is satisfiable by a name the attacker picks. internal/connection carries the bound host/port down — neither layer holds both facts.

Stated decisions: empty bound host refused, no auto-migration (an approval record would live in the renderer this constrains; the repo has no users and AGENTS.md forbids compat shims); unset bound port means 'this host, any port'; inline auth exempt with a test guarding against over-breadth.

Ten tests, seven attacks: alias-HostName-differs, alias port override, jump-host refusal, unbound refusal, host-only-any-port, inline exemption.

Coordinator additions on review: fixed two govet shadow findings the worker's own lint run missed, and corrected 'Bind to Host (optional)' in the UI plus the model comment saying empty means any host — both had become false, and a field labelled optional that breaks the connection is worse than no label.
acceptance_criteria: A credential bound to one host is refused for any other target, checked inside internal/ssh after resolveConfig, with a distinct error. Unbound password credential refused at connection time. Matching uses resolved hostname and effective port, never the alias or configured Host string. Tested against real ~/.ssh/config resolution: an alias whose HostName differs, and an alias whose Port overrides the default.
close_reason: Implementation landed in 6b6a166; the blocking chain is now closed. See that commit and the bead description for detail.

title: [security] XSS in the connections UI + no CSP = renderer takeover, and imported Tabby config is an ingress
description:
frontend/src/connections.ts:472-475 interpolates credential fields into HTML with no escaping: info.innerHTML = ` Using Credential: ${cred.name}
Username: ${cred.username} | Auth: ${authModeLabel(cred.auth)} ` frontend/index.html has NO Content-Security-Policy — only charset and viewport meta tags. A credential named `` executes when the connections UI renders it. FULL CHAIN, and every link is verified: 1. ingress — internal/importer/tabby.go parses an untrusted YAML config the user imports; profile and credential names come straight from that file 2. injection — connections.ts:472 renders the name as HTML 3. no containment — no CSP 4. privilege — the renderer can call GetWSToken (once nocx-x4u lands), and can already call `open`, which creates a PTY and writes bytes to it => importing a crafted Tabby config yields command execution as the user. This is why authenticating the socket (nocx-x4u) is necessary but NOT sufficient: the token is handed to the renderer, so injected same-origin code holds it. Codex's verdict on the whole plan was exactly this — "the renderer remains a privileged, injectable authority". FIX, all four, none optional: - replace innerHTML with textContent / element construction for anything carrying stored or imported data (audit the other sites too: main.ts x2, sidebar.ts, tabs.ts x2) - add a restrictive CSP compatible with Wails v2 + Vite - block untrusted navigation in the WebView; ensure OpenInspectorOnStartup is off in production - decide the Tabby import policy: the YAML also carries an inline `Password string` (importer/tabby.go:31-44) that currently travels through a JSON-RPC `Config string` — so the renderer, transport buffers and any frame logging all see it even though the converter drops it. Either strip secrets before IPC or do file selection and parsing backend-side. Found by the codex security review of the credential-boundary plan.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #12 (merged f42368a). The innerHTML template in connections.ts is gone — the credential panel is built with createElement/textContent, so credential fields are inserted as text and cannot be parsed as markup. Verified on main: zero innerHTML occurrences in connections.ts.

A CSP meta was added to frontend/index.html with script-src 'self' and deliberately no 'unsafe-inline', so an injected handler cannot execute even if the escaping regresses. style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' because the UI assigns element.style directly and xterm injects stylesheets at runtime; connect-src is pinned to the loopback socket. The policy also had to learn the app's own wails:// webview origin (e106b72) — it was refusing the real client 32 times per CI run.

The Tabby-import ingress is covered by the same change: imported names now reach the DOM as text regardless of what the YAML contained.

title: [security] Local WebSocket has no authentication — any page that finds the port gets a PTY
description:
internal/transport/ws.go:72 listens on 127.0.0.1:0 — loopback only, ephemeral port. Good
so far. But there is no authentication of any kind on the connection: no token, no
Authorization header, no handshake secret (grep for token/Authorization/Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
in ws.go returns nothing), and CheckOrigin at ws.go:62 returns true for every origin.

WebSockets are not subject to the same-origin restrictions that gate XHR, so the browser
will not stop a cross-origin handshake — the server has to, and ours does not. The only
barrier left is that the port is random. A page can attempt connections across the
ephemeral range; that is security by obscurity, and it is thin.

What is behind the socket: the `open` control method creates a PTY, and the binary data
plane writes bytes into it. So a page that finds the port gets arbitrary command execution
as the user. PR #11 additionally puts credential RPCs on the same surface.

PRE-EXISTING on main — NOT introduced by PR #11. Filed separately for that reason, but it
must be fixed alongside the credential boundary, because "secrets never leave the backend"
is worth much less while anyone who finds the port can run commands.

architecture.md:110 already states the invariant, though it scopes it to a future web
target: "auth token + bind-to-localhost by default". The desktop app runs the same server;
the invariant applies now.

Shape of the fix:
- generate a random per-launch token in the Go backend
- hand it to the WebView through a Wails binding, the way GetWSPort already hands over the
  port (main.go:150)
- require it on the WebSocket handshake — subprotocol or first control frame — and reject
  connections without it BEFORE any session method is reachable
- restrict CheckOrigin to the WebView's own origin rather than returning true
- keep the e2e harness working: e2e/harness.ts:19 stubs GetWSPort, so it will need the
  token stub too
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #12 (merged f42368a) by PR11-T3 (nocx-hl3). The socket now requires a per-launch capability token minted from crypto/rand and carried in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, compared in constant time, with the selected subprotocol echoed per RFC 6455. Start fails closed if the entropy source errors rather than serving an empty token. An Origin/Host policy runs alongside it: Origin is defence in depth against a browser page, Host closes DNS rebinding. Both checks reject BEFORE the upgrade, so open is never reachable — asserted by e2e/auth.spec.ts and by unit tests for each rejection path.

Loopback-only binding on an ephemeral port is retained but is no longer the control; it was always friction rather than authorization.

title: [epic] Persistence: storage capabilities + secrets as opaque references (ADR-0011)
description:
Implement ADR-0011: docs/decisions/0011-persistence-storage-capabilities-and-secret-references.md

Three storage capabilities — DocumentStore (atomic JSON), SecretStore (OS keychain),
ContentDB (SQLite, seam now / implementation later) — with typed repositories per entity
and the pairing chosen at the single composition root (AD-8).

Load-bearing rule: a secret exists only inside secret-specific types and APIs; persisted
domain records carry an opaque SecretID. The wire request to open a session carries a
profileID and nothing else; the backend joins profile -> credential -> secret at connect
time. This is a TYPE boundary, not a redaction convention — redaction would not have
prevented the PR #11 leak, because by the time the password reached tabs.ts it was already
an ordinary JS string.

SQLite: seam declared, implementation deferred until the first feature needs it
(nocx-dw3 agent conversations or nocx-4ff.6 command history). No SQLite in go.mod until then.

WORK, roughly in order:
1. Shared path resolution (config dir / data dir / cache dir, per OS role) — removes the
   os.TempDir() fallback at internal/app/app.go:66
2. DocumentStore capability: atomic write, permissions, per-module schema version + migration
   protocol (versions are per-module, NOT app-wide)
3. SecretStore capability + Secret type that cannot marshal; remove
   credential.VaultSecret's json-serializable Value (credential.go:59-64)
4. Split ProfileStore by aggregate: profiles / groups / credential metadata are three
   repositories, not one interface (profile/store.go:12-24)
5. Settings registry (nocx-1ei) on DocumentStore: typed declarations driving a GENERATED
   screen; retires config's Get(key) any (nocx-jap)
6. Remove every RPC returning a secret; openSSHSession takes profileID only
7. Credential deletion also deletes the keychain entry (ws.go:998-1010 today deletes
   metadata only, orphaning it forever)
8. Cross-store credential change as an explicit workflow with an ID-only journal
9. ContentDB seam + stub, no dependency
10. Export/backup modes (config export / portable encrypted / same-machine)

Owner decision 2026-07-25: build the target shape now rather than compromise, but keep
SQLite as a stub until a feature needs it.

DONE WHEN: every entity persists through a typed repository over DocumentStore / SecretStore / ContentDB paired at the single composition root; no persisted domain record contains a secret value, only an opaque SecretID; and export, import and backup have a user-facing surface.
close_reason:
Split, not abandoned — the deliverable landed and the bucket did not.

ADR-0011 is implemented: the storage capability, secrets as opaque references, the AEAD-encrypted store (nocx-1vr), the non-serializable Secret type (nocx-l7o) and the credential delete cascade (nocx-7l4) are all in. That was this epic's DONE WHEN and it is met.

What kept it open was everything else that landed in it because it was the persistence-shaped container. An area epic cannot close: the next persistence bug would have reopened the question forever. Under the owner's rule that an epic is a unit of assignment — handed to one person whole, never 'this epic but not those three children' — such an epic is unassignable by construction.

The six open children moved to four finishable epics: nocx-0b56 credential correctness (nocx-6ek.2, nocx-dcd), nocx-oqof export/import surface (nocx-6ek.3), nocx-2x8x secret lifecycle hygiene (nocx-dm0, nocx-23v), nocx-5o8m Windows and Linux (nocx-6ek.1). Nothing was dropped. The eight epics that were parked behind this one now wait on nocx-0b56.

title: Rework PR #11 before merge: credential boundary, connection ownership, split
description:
PR #11 (feat/ssh-connection-manager, +8025/-605, 52 files, 1 commit, 0 reviews, 0 CI runs)
must not merge as-is. Reviewed by codex; every blocker below verified by hand against the
branch (worktree from refs/pull/11/head).

BLOCKERS
1. SSH passwords written to logs in plaintext. frontend/src/tabs.ts:560
   Log('nocx: opening session, sshOpts: ' + JSON.stringify(this.sshOpts)) — and sshOpts
   carries password and jumpPassword (visible at :566 and :571). Wails Log forwards to the
   backend log.
2. Plaintext secrets returned to JavaScript. internal/transport/ws.go credentials.lookupPassword
   returns the password itself over the socket (~:1090). Secrets should resolve backend-side
   and never cross to the renderer.
   FAIRNESS NOTE: the permissive CheckOrigin (return true) is PRE-EXISTING — main's
   internal/transport/ws.go:62 already has it. The PR did not open that door; it put
   credentials behind it. Both need fixing, but only the second is this PR's doing.
3. The ref-counted connection pool required by AD-4 is dead code. internal/ssh/pool.go:174-180
   defaultDial returns an error and its own comment calls itself a placeholder awaiting
   "the real wiring". Production dials directly: internal/ssh/ssh_real.go:69-77. Acquire/Release
   are referenced only by pool tests — the tests exercise an implementation nothing calls.
4. SSH clients leak. ssh_real.go:75-77 appends every client to rc.clients; channel close
   (ssh_channel.go:33-38) closes only the session. Clients close only in global RealClient.Close,
   which normal tab closure never reaches. Jump-host clients leak independently (ssh_dial.go:99-103).
5. Vault uses AES-CBC with no MAC (credential/vault.go:97-114) and accepts padding after
   checking only the final length byte (:274-295) — malleable, unauthenticated. Needs an AEAD.
6. Gate not passed, and provably so: frontend/src/tabs.ts.orig is a committed 44 KB conflict
   artifact; `gofumpt -l` flags internal/profile/profile.go; `git diff --check` reports
   extensive trailing whitespace. The PR body claims only go build / go vet / 25 SSH tests.
7. internal/app/app.go:66 falls back to filepath.Join(os.TempDir(), "nocx-profiles.json") —
   a fixed, predictable, shared path.

ALSO: profile CRUD loads outside the mutex (profile/store.go:108-120) so concurrent updates
silently overwrite; cancellation stops at the initial TCP dial (ssh_dial.go:59, :154);
KeyPath is never carried through credential resolution (frontend/src/connections.ts:273-289);
keepalive / ready-timeout / agent-forwarding are editable in the UI but reach nothing.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: host key verification is strict on both the target and jump paths via the
known_hosts callback, with no InsecureIgnoreHostKey and no silent TOFU. Agent forwarding is
not silently enabled. The profile store's atomic temp+rename with 0700/0600 is better than
what internal/config has.

PLAN (owner decision 2026-07-25): copy the branch rather than send it back. pr-11 is already
fetched; work proceeds on a branch off it so the author's history and attribution survive.
Split into reviewable units, fix the credential boundary and connection ownership first,
reconcile persistence per nocx-tjs, then demonstrate the full gate.
notes:
PLAN v2: .internal/plans/2026-07-25-pr11-credential-boundary.md

Restructured after a codex security review found v1 unexecutable. Task order is now:
1 stop active disclosures (frontend log line + raw control-frame logging at ws.go:417-429)
2 renderer hardening (nocx-2ay) — BEFORE the socket token, because a token handed to an
  injectable renderer protects nothing
3 socket capability (nocx-x4u) — subprotocol, origin AND host policy, no e2e bypass
4 wire moves to profile IDs — ONE atomic commit (v1 split it and left an intermediate
  commit where SSH could not connect at all)
5 bind a credential to its target (confused deputy: Credential.Host empty = any host)
6 credential deletion also deletes secrets
7 VaultSecret stops being serializable

KEY DESIGN CORRECTION, mine not codex's: do NOT build a new resolution path and do not make
CredentialStore return a wrapped Secret. ssh.WithCredentials(store, identity) already exists
(internal/ssh/ssh.go:139-146), session.go:274 already forwards it, and ssh_auth.go:117-118
resolves the password inside the SSH package at auth time. So the resolver maps profileID ->
{host, credential.Identity, non-secret options} and nothing in transport/session/connection
ever holds plaintext. The strongest form is that the store returns nothing outward at all.
This is the PR author's own seam — the rework completes their design rather than replacing it.

V1 ERRORS THAT WERE MINE: claimed profile fields at top level when they live under Options;
ignored Options.CredentialID entirely, so reusable credentials would never resolve; deleted
wire fields needed for key and jump auth without restoring them; split the wire change across
two commits; invented three test-helper names (see memory lesson-nocx-writing-plans-never-write-test-code).

DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE REVIEW, recorded deliberately: native secure prompt for INITIAL password
entry rejected as disproportionate (guarantee narrowed to STORED secrets instead); core-dump
exposure documented as a limitation rather than made a task; WSL reachability deferred to when
Windows lands (Phase 3, vision.md:74).

Argument round with codex in progress.
PLAN v3 — AGREED with codex after three argument rounds, no remaining blockers.

WHAT CODEX CONCEDED:
- native secure prompt for INITIAL password entry is not required here (guarantee narrowed to STORED secrets, and the renderer-trust consequence stated plainly instead of hidden)
- core-dump/process-memory exposure is a documented limitation, not a task (now actually written into ADR-0011 Consequences — I had claimed it was there when it was not)
- WSL reachability defers to Windows (Phase 3, vision.md:75)
- the WithCredentials seam is stronger than making CredentialStore return a wrapped Secret — keeping plaintext out of transport/session/connection beats dressing it up in transit

WHAT I CONCEDED, all verified in code:
- JUMP CREDENTIALS: v2 promised something the API cannot express. ConnectConfig carries ONE Credentials/CredIdentity pair (ssh.go:66-70), and connectToJumpHost builds jumpCfg with Password: cfg.JumpPassword and never forwards Credentials (ssh_dial.go:109-116). Needs JumpCredentials + JumpCredIdentity added and forwarded through session.sshOptionsFromConfig. This was a NEW problem v2 introduced.
- CREDENTIAL BINDING ENFORCEMENT POINT: resolveConfig is unexported on RealClient (ssh_config.go:26-28) and merges ~/.ssh/config with precedence explicit > config > default, so internal/connection cannot see the authoritative host/port. Enforcement moved INTO internal/ssh, right after resolveConfig. Two resolution implementations that disagree is exactly how a credential binds to the wrong target.
- Task 5 policy decided in the plan rather than delegated: a stored password credential must carry a bound host and effective port; unbound is refused at connection time; matching on RESOLVED hostname and effective port. The approval-record variant was rejected because the approval UI would live in the renderer — the very actor the task constrains.
- token encoding: 32 bytes unpadded base64url (= and / are not valid HTTP token chars), parsed protocol list validated, constant-time compare, selected protocol echoed on upgrade.
- production Origin must be CAPTURED from a real Wails build per platform, not hard-coded — 'wails://wails/' with a trailing slash would reject the legitimate client, and a Go test with a synthetic Origin cannot establish the real value.

PRECISION I INSISTED ON: encrypted private keys are not 'left unusable' by removing the RPC — they do not work today at all (loadKey calls only ParsePrivateKey; ParsePrivateKeyWithPassphrase has no production caller; lookupKeyPassphrase at ssh_auth.go:155 is dead). The removal breaks nothing; what was wrong was my plan promising a replacement that does not exist. Now explicitly out of scope with the implementation sketch recorded.

WATCH DURING EXECUTION (codex's pick, and I agree): the two-hop auth chain — target and jump identities must never be swapped or silently fall back to the plaintext fields.
close_reason:
PR #12 merged as f42368a. All eleven planned tasks landed as separate commits: T1 credential disclosure, T2 XSS + CSP, T3 WebSocket authentication, T4 the wire on profile IDs, T5 credential-to-host binding on the resolved hostname, T6 delete cascade (interim — nocx-7l4 stays open pending STORE-3), T7 the Secret type, T8 the connection pool actually wired, T9 cancellation past the TCP dial, T10 AES-256-GCM, T11 hygiene.

Found and fixed on the way: CI's backend job was failing on main too (a deleted //go:embed anchor, nocx-500 and its cause nocx-4uw); PR #11 had replaced the app shell without mentioning it (tab bar restored, redesign split into epic nocx-d3q); the new Origin check was refusing the app's own webview 32 times per CI run.

Merged knowing e2e is red: 13 failures against main's 14, delta = two stale tests deleted plus one unstable chromium test. Inherited failures tracked as nocx-bw2.

title: [bug] ShellInputTarget hand-rolls bracketed paste, contradicting its own comment and the recorded lesson
description:
frontend/src/input-target.ts:33-34 defines PASTE_START/PASTE_END and :42 sends
`${PASTE_START}${doc}${PASTE_END}\r` down sendRaw. That is exactly the hand-rolled
wrapper that memory `lesson-nocx-input-editor-do-not-hand-roll` says must not exist:
"do NOT hand-roll bracketed-paste wrappers when submitting the DOM editor's command.
Route through the terminal engine's term.paste(text) which wraps ONLY when the shell
enabled mode 2004. Hardcoded wrappers leaked as literal 00~/01~ into the command when
2004 wasn't (yet) enabled — e.g. a fast second submit racing the prompt."

The code even documents the leak as accepted (input-target.ts:30-32): "When mode IS off
the wrappers leak but the shell interprets \n as accept-line, which also executes every
line. Either way, the user gets the entire composed command."

And tabs.ts:295-296 claims the opposite of what the code does: "paste() delegates
bracketed-paste wrapping to the engine (correct for mode 2004); sendRaw carries the CR."
ShellInputTarget has no paste() and never touches the engine.

So three sources disagree: the lesson says route through term.paste(), tabs.ts says we
already do, and input-target.ts hand-rolls and calls the leak acceptable. At most one is
right. Resolve which, then make code and comments agree.

Note nocx-4ff.14 is cited in the comment for the multi-line rationale — whatever the fix,
a multi-line composition must still execute every line.
Found during the codex review of the editor-core spec (nocx-2gf).
notes:
WHY THIS IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, NOT HYGIENE (owner insight, 2026-07-25): the danger of multi-line input is not the multi-line-ness — it is text reaching the PTY WITHOUT passing through the editor.

Tabby warns with a modal on multi-line paste because it has no editor of its own: paste goes straight to the terminal, so a dialog is the only intervention point. Owner's experience: it nags constantly and the answer is a blind yes/no.

We are structurally better placed. In enhanced mode a paste lands in the DOM editor: visible, editable, caret in it, nothing runs until Enter. The user reads what they are about to execute instead of approving it blind. No modal needed — and we should NOT add one.

That advantage exists only while the submit path is correct. With the hand-rolled wrappers, when mode 2004 is off the leak turns every newline into accept-line (input-target.ts:30-32 says so outright), and the lines execute as they arrive — bypassing the very review the editor exists to provide.

So the promise to make, and to test:
- ENHANCED mode: pasted or injected text is composed, never executed, until an explicit submit. Safe by construction.
- RAW mode (running command, alt-screen, unintegrated shell): paste goes to the PTY and the shell decides, exactly as in any terminal. We must not intercept there — that would break fail-open and raw routing (ADR-0004 section 1).

This matters more as text stops coming only from the user: ghost text from history (nocx-4ff.23), edit-and-rerun (nocx-4ff.20), and agent-composed commands (nocx-dw3) all put non-typed text into the editor. The invariant 'composed text never self-executes' is what makes those features safe to build.
close_reason: Fixed and merged to main as 84ba49d. Wrappers now go only to a shell that set DECSET 2004, read at submit rather than cached. Verified on macos-latest, where /bin/bash really is 3.2: CI run 30218676302 on merged main is green across all three jobs.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED against a real failure, 2026-07-26. This is not theoretical any more: it is why e2e is red on main (nocx-5zl4).

macOS ships /bin/bash 3.2 (frozen by Apple over GPLv3), which predates readline 6.1 and has no bracketed-paste support at all, so it never sets DECSET 2004. input-target.ts wraps every submit unconditionally, so on that shell the wrappers arrive as ordinary characters and corrupt the COMMAND NAME. CI trace: 'bash: 0~read: command not found'. All 11 e2e failures on macos-latest are this one defect.

That invalidates the accepted-leak comment at input-target.ts:30-32, which claims that when the mode is off 'the shell interprets \\n as accept-line, which also executes every line. Either way, the user gets the entire composed command.' The user does not: the command does not run at all.

Blast radius is every macOS user on the default shell, plus any SSH session to a host with an old shell — not just CI.

FIX DIRECTION (verified against the installed engine): xterm.js exposes term.modes.bracketedPasteMode (@xterm/xterm typings :831, :1877) tracking CSI ? 2004 h, so the mode is readable at submit time. Either route through term.paste(), which performs the same gate internally, or read the flag and wrap only when it is set. Read it AT SUBMIT, not at startup: the mode is dynamic, and a live read also kills the original race recorded in lesson-nocx-input-editor-do-not-hand-roll (a fast second submit racing the prompt leaked wrappers because 2004 was not enabled yet).

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, to be decided here rather than in a comment: with 2004 off, a multi-line composition becomes N accept-lines instead of one bracketed unit (nocx-4ff.14 cites the wrapper for exactly this). Decide and record what multi-line should do on a shell without 2004.

REJECTED APPROACH: an omp worker fixed the symptom in internal/pty/pty_local.go by silently substituting /bin/zsh for a macOS user's /bin/bash. That changes product behaviour to green a test, leaves SSH and every other non-2004 shell broken, and sits in the wrong layer — AD-6 puts terminal state in the frontend. Patch kept out of tree.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
FIX LANDED on branch shady2k/nocx-hi2-bracketed-paste-gate (6ac331a), VERIFIED against the real environment.

CI run 30217202549 on macos-latest, where /bin/bash really is 3.2: e2e went from 11 failed / 23 passed to 1 failed / 33 passed. Every bracketed-paste failure is gone — enhanced-input :10/:38/:71 on both engines, activity-bell on both, clipboard:109, and click-focus under webkit.

The one remaining failure, click-focus.spec.ts:26 on chromium only, is a DIFFERENT defect and not this one: it fails at line 41, BEFORE the click, where focus returns to the editor within 5s of an explicit blur(). That is focus-bounce, which the test's own comment at lines 43-50 already calls 'the subject of a separate fix'. It belongs with nocx-4ff.28/nocx-4ff.29.

The three-way contradiction this bead was opened for is now resolved. The tabs.ts:295-296 comment claiming paste() already delegates no longer exists — that code was refactored into TerminalContent since this bead was written — so what remained was input-target.ts hand-rolling unconditionally, and it no longer does.

Not closing: the branch is not merged. Merge needs the owner's approval.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Branch fully green: CI run 30218418676, all three jobs, macos-latest. Awaiting merge approval.

title: Minimized window cannot be restored (frameless title bar)
description: Regression from nocx-cpp: after minimising, the window cannot be restored. Known Wails/macOS problem with hidden title bars — see wailsapp/wails#1319. TitleBarHiddenInset differs from TitleBarHidden only by UseToolbar:true and HideToolbarSeparator:true; the NSToolbar it adds is what insets the traffic lights and is the prime suspect for breaking deminiaturize. First try TitleBarHidden (traffic lights sit at the default position, so the tab strip's left padding shrinks accordingly). If that does not fix it, the fallback is returning to a normal title bar and reopening nocx-cpp with a different approach. Workaround meanwhile: Cmd+Tab, or right-click the Dock icon and Show.
acceptance_criteria: Minimising and restoring the window works, with the tab strip still serving as the title bar.
close_reason: TitleBarHiddenInset's NSToolbar (UseToolbar) was what broke deminiaturize; TitleBarHidden keeps the hidden title and full-size content and restores correctly. Confirmed by the user on the real window.

title: Single tab: clicking the window breaks input and corrupts the render
description: User repro: with exactly ONE tab open, click anywhere in the window. The prompt disappears, and typing then produces red garbled glyphs. Does not reproduce with two tabs. I reproduced a neighbouring symptom at :34115: after clicking the pane, typed characters never appear at all — the click does not hand focus to the terminal. Suspect the interaction between the click path, xterm focus, and either the refreshAtlas() call added for nocx-e27 or the --wails-draggable regions added with the frameless title bar. Debug in the browser at :34115, not by reading — this is invisible to jsdom.
acceptance_criteria: With one tab, clicking anywhere in the window keeps the prompt intact, focuses the terminal, and typing renders correctly.
close_reason: Verified by the repo owner in the real app: with one tab, clicking the window keeps the prompt and input works. Fixed by 25de485 (ResizeObserver repaints after clearing the texture atlas) and 2c02a46 (#panes sets --wails-draggable: no-drag, so Wails no longer swallows the mousedown). Guarded by e2e/click-focus.spec.ts for the shared click->focus->PTY path; see nocx-bq7 for what could not be guarded.

title: Tab switch corrupts the terminal: WebGL texture atlas lost when a pane is hidden
description: Switching away from a tab and back renders garbage — glyphs drawn from wrong atlas coordinates. Reproduced in Chrome via the wails dev server on :34115: fill a tab with block glyphs, switch away, switch back, and ████/▓▓▓▓ come back as a solid yellow rectangle and hatching, with a stray vertical bar across the screen. Text glyphs mostly survive; the damage is to the glyph atlas. Panes are hidden with visibility (see the lazy-mount comment in tabs.ts), which keeps the layout box but lets the WebGL renderer's texture atlas go stale. Likely fix: on activation, clear the atlas and force a full repaint — the WebGL addon exposes clearTextureAtlas(), and term.refresh(0, rows-1) redraws. Verify the fix by the same reproduction, not by unit tests: jsdom has no layout or GPU.
acceptance_criteria: Switching away from a filled tab and back renders identically to before the switch, verified by screenshot in the browser.
close_reason: Verified visually at :34115: filled a tab with block glyphs, switched away and back, and the render is identical to before the switch — no yellow blocks, no stray bars. Fixed via a refreshAtlas() seam on TerminalRenderer.

title: M0 terminal blank screen: ws:port emitted in OnStartup races frontend subscription
description: main.go startup() (OnStartup) emits ws:port via wailsRuntime.EventsEmit BEFORE the frontend subscribes (EventsOn in main.ts). Wails does not buffer events for late subscribers -> port promise hangs -> terminal.mount() never runs -> blank screen.
acceptance_criteria: Frontend gets the port via a bound GetWSPort() method (request/response), not a startup event. Add options.Debug{OpenInspectorOnStartup:true}. Terminal renders (app or localhost:34115).
close_reason: Closed
