title: Spike: verify ghostty-web OSC 7/133 + scrollback/selection/resize APIs and WASM perf
description: TOP architectural risk (docs/architecture.md AD-5/AD-6). Verify whether ghostty-web exposes OSC 7 (cwd) AND OSC 133 (prompt) handlers/events, plus scrollback/selection/resize APIs; measure WASM parser throughput with representative agent TUIs (Claude Code / aider) inside WKWebView. If OSC handlers are absent, evaluate patching ghostty-web vs backend-parses-OSC (which would break AD-6).
acceptance_criteria: Documented: does ghostty-web expose OSC 7/133 + scrollback/selection/resize? Perf numbers for a representative TUI. Recommendation recorded as an ADR in docs/decisions/. AD-5/AD-6 confirmed or revised.
close_reason: RESOLVED against ghostty-web. API surface: xterm.js exposes parser.registerOscHandler/registerCsiHandler/registerDcsHandler/registerEscHandler; ghostty-web exposes NO OSC handler registration at all — only OSC 8 hyperlinks, and its own types note the URI is 'not yet exposed in simplified API'. Verified empirically on xterm.js, not from docs: registered handlers for OSC 7 and OSC 133 and wrote real sequences — OSC 7 returned 'file://wemosd1/Users/shady/Documents/repos/nocx', OSC 133 returned all five markers A, B, C, D;0, D;127 including exit codes. So AD-5/AD-6 hold on xterm.js with no backend sniffing; on ghostty-web they would require patching the library.

title: ADR number collision: two branches claim 0013
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

    git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/feat/adr-0013-credential-trusted-endpoints -- docs/decisions/ | grep 0013
    ls docs/decisions/ | grep 0013

Observed: two different ADRs numbered 0013 — 'credential-trusted-endpoints' on that branch, 'plain-css-with-semantic-custom-properties' on ui-shell-kit-tokens.
Expected: one ADR per number.

## Detail

Noticed at merge time on 2026-07-27. ui-shell-kit-tokens lands first and takes 0013 and 0014 (component kit foundation), so the free numbers start at 0015. The credential branch is the one that renumbers, not because its work is lesser but because renumbering an unmerged branch costs one rename while renumbering a merged ADR breaks every reference already written against it.

Both branches were authored in parallel against a main that had 0012 as its highest, so neither did anything wrong. The lesson is that 'next free number' read from main is a race whenever two branches are open at once.
acceptance_criteria: docs/decisions/ contains exactly one ADR per number. The credential-trusted-endpoints ADR is renumbered to the next free number and every reference to it — commits, beads, code comments, the branch's own prose — points at the new one.

title: Forbid inline markup and CSS that duplicates a component
description:
Asked for by the owner 2026-07-27, after Page was found rendering .ui-page__body and .ui-page__rail inline while PageBody and PageRail sat unused (nocx-vxqj.9). A rule that only rejects raw <button> does not catch that: the duplication was a div with a class, and it happened inside the kit itself.

The generalisation the owner stated: no inline markup or CSS without using the component. Enforce it by deriving ownership from the kit rather than maintaining a list — a class rendered by ui/page-body.tsx is PageBody's, so any other file rendering it is bypassing the component. That check would have failed on Page the day it was written.

Pairs with the raw-controls guard (nocx-vxqj.6) and the colour grammar (nocx-xrrl.4): same baseline mechanism, same negative-fixture requirement, same rule that the baseline may only shrink.
acceptance_criteria: A check fails the build when an application surface, or another kit component, renders markup or styling that a kit component already owns. Ownership is derived, not hand-listed: for each frontend/src/ui/*.tsx the classes it renders belong to it, and that class appearing anywhere else is a violation. Inline style props are rejected in application surfaces — layout and colour belong in CSS, and the colour half is already covered by the grammar check. A negative fixture proves the rule fires by name in lint-fixtures/gate.sh. Current violations are baselined per-violation, may only shrink, and the baseline must be empty before nocx-vxqj closes.
close_reason: nocx/no-inline-markup rejects kit-owned classes duplicated outside their component and inline style props in surfaces. Ownership derived by scanning ui/*.tsx at config-load, not hand-listed, so it survives renames and new components. Verified against the motivating case: <div class="ui-page__body"> in settings.tsx fires by name and the message names the component to use. Baseline 8 across settings/connections/update-notice, growth-guarded, must be empty before the epic closes. Ten rules now fire from the negative fixture.

title: The kit contains four components nothing uses
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run, from frontend/:

    for c in PageBody PageRail Field EmptyState; do
      grep -rlE "<$c([ />]|$)" src --include=*.tsx | grep -v '^src/ui/' | grep -v '\.test\.'
    done

Observed: no output for any of the four — every consumer is a test or the component's own file.
Expected: every kit export has a production consumer, because a kit is a set of components that are used.

## Detail

PageBody and PageRail are the worst of the four: Page renders .ui-page__body and .ui-page__rail inline instead of composing them, so the same markup exists twice — once as an unused component, once by hand. That is precisely the duplication this epic exists to prevent, occurring inside the kit itself.

Field does not fit the two-column settings rows it was written for. EmptyState sits unused while connections.tsx hand-rolls 'No connections yet'.

Cause, and it is the coordinator's: the wave-1 kit brief listed which components to build from the epic's prose rather than from call sites, and the Page primitives were each commissioned separately without requiring Page to compose them. The rule this epic was founded on — do not create a component per need, check who will call it first — was broken by the brief that created the kit.

Supersedes the framing of nocx-vxqj.7 and nocx-vxqj.8: there is no 'two categories' question. A component nothing uses is a defect; a consumer the kit does not serve is a missing component. Both are fixed by making the inventory equal the consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Every component exported from frontend/src/ui/ has at least one production consumer, verified by a check that fails otherwise — the same shape as the raw-controls guard. No surface and no kit component renders markup a component already owns: Page composes PageBody and PageRail rather than rendering their divs inline. Field either fits the settings row it was written for or is replaced by a component that does, and that component is used everywhere it fits. EmptyState is adopted by every surface that currently hand-rolls an empty state. Components are not deleted to satisfy this — consumers adopt them.
close_reason: All three baselines empty. Field gained orientation and is adopted by settings rows; Button gained a close variant and rest-props and the chrome buttons in banner/sidebar/tab-strip/update-notice are kit components; Radio added for the connections auth group; EmptyState adopted. Every kit export now has a production consumer. The ui- namespace is documented as reserved for component-owned classes, with kit-scope as the consumer-applied marker.

title: Quick-connect: a modal picker from the caret beside +
description:
Decided by the owner 2026-07-27 after weighing the activity bar, a dropdown on +, an overflow menu, and integration into the command editor. See design spec section 2.4 for the reasoning, in particular why a modal beats a dropdown here: it needs no Menu or Popover primitive (which ADR-0014 declines to build for want of a consumer), the platform supplies focus trap and Escape, it scales past a handful of hosts, and it is the seed of the command palette rather than a single-purpose surface.

Depends on the overlay work in nocx-vxqj.5 because the native <dialog> wrapper, the focus-return-to-xterm path and the Wails drag-region guard all belong there.
acceptance_criteria: A caret beside the tab strip's + opens a modal built on native <dialog>, listing the local shell and every SSH profile, filtered as the user types, opening a tab on Enter or click. Keyboard: the filter input has focus on open, arrows move the selection, Escape closes and returns focus to the caret. It reaches tm.newSSHTab() by the same path the old Connections surface used, proved end to end. A keyboard shortcut opens it without the mouse. The component is written so that connections are ONE SOURCE of its list, not the whole of it — the command palette reuses it.
close_reason: Quick-connect modal on the native dialog, opened from a caret beside + and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P. The list is a provider interface returning {id,label,detail,run} so a command palette adds a second source without touching the component. 12 e2e pass in both engines. Coordinator: the guard rejected the caret as a new raw button and the regeneration script refused to grow the baseline, so Button gained a tabIndex prop and the caret became a kit component — the first evidence that the kit CAN cover chrome controls, which informs nocx-vxqj.8.

title: Export section speaks the same page and section vocabulary
acceptance_criteria: The export section renders through PageSection and kit components with no raw interactive controls and no st-export-* rules duplicating kit styling. Its 25 local signals are reviewed against the ownership table: transient state stays local, anything accepted and shared moves. Existing export/import behaviour is unchanged, proved by the existing tests.
close_reason: Export renders through PageSection and the kit; all 11 raw-control violations gone, 25 createSignal collapsed into 5 local stores (nothing shared, per the ownership table), 256 lines of dead st-export-* rules deleted. Guard baseline 21 to 10. No assertion changes needed. No e2e covers export, stated rather than invented.

title: Delete the standalone Connections surface
acceptance_criteria: SURFACE_CONNECTIONS, SINGLETON_CONNECTIONS, connections-content.ts and the connections tab registration are gone, along with cm-* rules superseded by kit and page classes. The reachability test from .3 still passes. No SSH capability is lost: profiles, groups, credentials and Tabby import are all still reachable and tested.
close_reason: Standalone surface removed: connections-content.ts, SURFACE_CONNECTIONS, SINGLETON_CONNECTIONS, SURFACE_ID_CONNECTIONS and its registration, the wrapper-only test, and the .cm-header/.cm-keys-list rules that existed only for it. connections.tsx survives as the Settings page. Verified: exactly two classes lived only in the deleted stylesheet and neither is used by the surviving page. tsc clean via the local binary (npx cannot resolve tsc in worktrees — a brief defect, now fixed in the skill), 777 unit tests, 69 e2e pass. Worker retracted its own worker_done over the npx gate, which was correct behaviour on a requirement I wrote wrong.

title: Connections added as a Settings sub-page, every entry path exercised
acceptance_criteria: A Connections page is reachable from the Settings rail and covers profile CRUD, groups, credentials and Tabby import. An end-to-end test walks from the activity-bar gear to a created SSH tab through tm.newSSHTab(). Draft lifetime, request cancellation and observer ownership on sub-page navigation follow the state ownership table from nocx-82l9.7. Nothing is deleted in this bead: the standalone surface still works.
close_reason: Connections is a page in the Settings rail via the typed registry; nothing deleted yet (nocx-imkb.4 owns that). e2e walks gear to a created SSH tab and passes in WebKit. Guard baseline 29 to 21, connections.tsx 10 raw controls to 2, both window.confirm calls now the kit dialog. Worker correctly raised a decision gate rather than touching main.tsx; the one-line wire applied inside the factory so a fresh SettingsContent gets it before mount. Coordinator repaired: unparsable JSX (missing nav/ul opening tags), a page registry typing a component page as a bare Component when it needs props, an orphaned handleSectionClick, and the worker's own e2e asserting .cm-header which its migration had replaced with a kit Toolbar.

title: Settings on Page and the kit, with a typed page registry
acceptance_criteria: Settings renders through Page plus kit components with no raw interactive controls left. The rail is a typed registry of generated pages (one per Go-declared section) and explicit component pages. The generated-screen invariant holds inside generated pages: adding a Go setting still costs zero frontend changes, proved by a test that adds a declaration and asserts it appears. scrollToKey uses PageScroller.scrollToElement, not row.scrollIntoView. The settings screen scrolls at a short window height in WebKit.
close_reason: Settings composes Page, PageRail, PageScroller and PageSection, takes every control from the kit, and its stylesheet has zero colour literals. The rail is a typed registry of generated and component pages — the seam Connections needs. Generated-screen invariant proved by a test that adds a declaration and asserts the nav entry. scrollToKey uses PageScroller.scrollToElement. Coordinator repointed the e2e selectors that the migration invalidated, including ones in specs the worker did not own, and widened Button's children to JSX.Element. Finding kept: Field does not fit two-column settings rows, which is a gap in the kit.

title: Page primitives and the two named scroll owners
acceptance_criteria: Page, PageHeader, PageBody, PageRail, PageScroller and PageSection exist with the CSS contract from spec section 6.1. PageScroller is the single content scroll owner and exposes scrollToElement(); PageRail scrolls only as a bounded rail and does not scroll independently at the narrow breakpoint. A test asserts a page subtree contains no computed overflow auto/scroll node other than those two. SidebarView provides the same header/filter/body composition for panel views.
close_reason: Page, PageHeader, PageBody, PageRail, PageScroller, PageSection and SidebarView exist with the height contract; PageScroller exposes scrollToElement. Scroll ownership is two named owners with a test that fails on a third overflow container. KNOWN LIMIT, recorded honestly by the worker: the invariant test runs in jsdom, which applies CSS from style elements but computes no layout, so it catches a structural violation and cannot prove the chain holds under WebKit. Follow-up filed.

title: Frozen scrollback is snapshot-themed, and keeps its algorithmic colour conversion
acceptance_criteria: ANSI 0-15 come from the theme; indices 16-255 and truecolor stay algorithmic content conversion in scrollback/serializer.ts. The active palette is injected at capture time so a later theme change does not recolour already-frozen blocks. Tests cover a theme change before a block freezes and after.
close_reason: TerminalSnapshot (palette + defaultFg + defaultBg) threaded through the serializer; blocks.ts captures it at freeze so a later theme change does not recolour frozen output. ANSI 0-15 from the theme, 16-255 and truecolor algorithmic and byte-identical. Colour literals live only in DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT. This is the redo — the first attempt reported 82 passing tests while the file did not compile, and was reverted; tsc --noEmit now exits 0 and is required by every brief since.

title: xterm reads the same tokens, with the startup race closed
acceptance_criteria: One adapter builds xterm's ITheme from the resolved --terminal-* properties; the literal palette at renderers/xterm.ts:152 is deleted. A synchronous bootstrap resolver runs before the Solid render and before any terminal is constructed: it applies data-theme, validates that every required property resolves non-empty, and falls back atomically to the built-in theme otherwise. A concrete ITheme is passed into terminal construction, never read opportunistically afterwards, and theme-change subscription is registered before construction or reapplied immediately after. applyTheme is a terminal-controller operation that also performs whatever refresh or atlas invalidation xterm needs; ADR-0005's refresh pump stays inside the controller and is never driven from reactive state. A Linux WebKitGTK test asserts a live terminal repaints in the new palette with no user input.
close_reason: One adapter builds ITheme from --terminal-* tokens; the literal palette in renderers/xterm.ts is deleted. Synchronous bootstrap resolver runs before the Solid render with atomic fallback; concrete ITheme passed into construction; subscription registered before mount. applyTheme is a controller op that forces the refresh, with ADR-0005's pump untouched. CRITICAL finding from the worker: all 21 --terminal-* tokens were absent from the theme file — nocx-xrrl.2 never wrote them and the coordinator's brief asserted they existed. Added here from the shipped palette and all 21 verified in WebKit. reconcileThemeFromGo is wired but uncalled: ui.theme is not declared in internal/settings yet.

title: State and derived colour tokens: hover, active, selected, disabled, focus ring, overlay
acceptance_criteria: Every interaction state has a token, defined per theme or derived centrally once in tokens.css; no component defines its own hover shade and none uses opacity on a whole element as a substitute. Focus-ring, scrim/overlay and translucent-selection tokens exist. If color-mix() is used, the WebKit floor from the ADR is respected and a fallback is present.
close_reason: Satisfied by the state-colour correction in nocx-xrrl.2: every interaction state — hover, active, selected, disabled, focus-ring, scrim, translucent selection — is a token assigned in the theme. No component defines its own hover value; all reference var(). color-mix() is not used for these, so the WebKit floor does not apply and no fallback is needed. ADR-0013 §3.1 records why derivation was abandoned.

title: The colour grammar check: a parser, not a hex denylist
acceptance_criteria: A CI check parses CSS declarations and permits, outside themes/, only var(--token), currentColor, transparent, inherit, and color-mix() whose every colour operand is one of those — so named colours, oklch(), lab(), color(), gradient stops and box-shadow colours are all caught, and color-mix laundering a literal is rejected. It also scans JSX style props and SVG fill/stroke attributes. Current violations are enumerated in a baseline that may only shrink and must be empty before nocx-xrrl closes.
close_reason: ESLint rule for JSX style props and SVG attributes plus a css-tree scanner for CSS declarations; permits only var(), currentColor, transparent, inherit and color-mix over those, and blocks the color-mix(..., red 20%) laundering case. Its first act falsified the token migration's 'zero literals outside themes/': ten exist — six in overlay.css inside var() fallbacks, four in connections.tsx inline styles, both invisible to a CSS-file grep. Baselined, not fixed. Coordinator declared css-tree, which was present only transitively.

title: styles/ split: tokens.css plus tokyo-night extracted from the existing 27 colours
acceptance_criteria: frontend/src/styles/ contains tokens.css, themes/tokyo-night.css, base.css, components/ and surfaces/. The 27 unique colours currently in style.css are expressed once in the theme file and referenced by token everywhere else. The rendered application is pixel-identical to before, proved by screenshot comparison in WebKit. style.css no longer carries a palette.
close_reason: styles/ now matches ADR-0013: tokens.css, themes/tokyo-night.css, base.css, components/, surfaces/. 265 colour literals became var() references; zero remain outside themes/. Coordinator ran a computed-colour diff in WebKit that the worker could not, and it found five real changes hiding in a refactor advertised as mechanical — tab bar, vertical strip, settings rail, clipboard banner and active tab had been collapsed into shared tokens. All five restored as their own tokens. The remaining diff is color-mix() serialisation only. ADR-0013's surface-hover derivation was proven wrong (the real hover is darker than the surface) and the ADR is corrected.

title: ADR: styling architecture — plain CSS with semantic tokens
acceptance_criteria: An ADR in docs/decisions/ records: plain CSS with semantic custom properties in frontend/src/styles/, with Tailwind and CSS Modules weighed and rejected for stated reasons; the token layers (semantic UI colour, control metrics, terminal); the allowed colour GRAMMAR outside themes/ rather than a literal denylist; the policy for colours that never appear in a CSS file (Go settings, xterm's injected stylesheet, serializer output, SVG assets); and the minimum WebKit version supported for any color-mix() derivation, with the fallback if that floor is not met.
close_reason: ADR-0013 records plain CSS with semantic tokens; Tailwind and CSS Modules declined with reasons; allowed colour grammar instead of a hex denylist; color-mix floor WebKitGTK 2.40 / macOS 13.1 with a generated @supports fallback. Coordinator fixed two self-contradictions (white/black mix anchors, rgba scrim) and settled the theme bootstrap-cache rule in 8.1.

title: The guard: raw controls and direct Kobalte imports rejected, with a baseline that only shrinks
acceptance_criteria: An ESLint rule rejects raw button, select, textarea and checkbox/radio inputs, and any @kobalte/* import, in application surfaces; frontend/src/ui/ and terminal-owned files are exempt by explicit path list, never by surface-wide waiver. A machine-readable baseline enumerates every current violation by file and control; CI fails if the baseline grows. nocx-vxqj cannot close while the baseline is non-empty.
notes: Reframed 2026-07-27. The guard must not blindly reject native controls now that the ADR may deliberately adopt <select> and <dialog> inside kit wrappers. The rule stands for APPLICATION SURFACES — raw button/select/textarea/checkbox/radio there is still a violation — but frontend/src/ui/ is where native implementation details are allowed to live, by path exemption rather than by surface-wide waiver. The @kobalte/* import clause only applies if a library is adopted at all; if none is, drop it rather than leaving a rule against a dependency that does not exist.
close_reason: Custom ESLint rule nocx/no-raw-controls rejects raw button/select/textarea/checkbox/radio and innerHTML in application surfaces; ui/ and terminal-owned files exempt by explicit path. Per-violation baseline, growth-only failure, deliberate regeneration script. Negative fixture proves all 8 rules fire by name via gate.sh. Coordinator regenerated the baseline after the Settings migration: 39 to 29, and the 10 that went are exactly Settings' — the guard and the migration agree independently.

title: Kit wave 2: overlay primitives behind wrappers, with the Wails portal contract
acceptance_criteria: Select, Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tooltip and Combobox are exposed as nocx components; no app surface imports @kobalte/* directly. The wrappers own the portal root element, the z-index layer scale, --wails-draggable:no-drag on that root, the dismissal policy and focus return to the invoker. Packaged WKWebView and WebKitGTK tests open every overlay type from the title-bar region and from a terminal-adjacent surface and assert the control activates rather than dragging the window.
notes: Reframed 2026-07-27. The original criteria treated all six primitives as equivalent portaled overlays behind one library; they are not. Per primitive now: modal dialogs use native <dialog> + showModal(), which renders in the browser top layer and is therefore EXEMPT from the portal-root and z-index assertions while still bound by the drag-region, focus-return and xterm-textarea clauses; Popover, Menu and Tooltip are custom overlays sharing one portal root AND one overlay stack, so Escape closes only the topmost; Combobox is NOT built until a real consumer defines its contract (editable vs select-only, local vs async, free-form values, grouping, virtualisation, form semantics). Add explicit keyboard and ARIA acceptance for Menu: roving focus, Arrow/Home/End, typeahead, disabled items, submenu direction and delay, focus return, context-menu coordinates. Packaged drag/focus tests remain required for every custom overlay.
close_reason: Native <dialog> behind a kit wrapper plus an overlay core: stack (Escape closes topmost only), portal root, focus return, --wails-draggable no-drag guard. terminal-content.ts's paste confirm migrated; connections.tsx:166/:178 and settings.tsx:610 left for their file owners with exact replacements listed. Coordinator fixed floating promises, test typings, and pointed tabs.test.ts at the kit helper. NOT verified and recorded as such: packaged Wails drag interaction and xterm focus-return in a real webview.

title: Kobalte spike: pinned version, measured gzip, portal behaviour in a packaged webview
acceptance_criteria: Reports the exact @kobalte/core version, its publication date, maintenance status and declared peer range against solid-js 1.9.14. Reports the MEASURED raw and gzip delta against the real production build: shared-core cost once, plus incremental cost per primitive for Select, Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tooltip and Combobox. Reports a packaged WebKitGTK run opening each overlay type from the title-bar region and from a terminal-adjacent surface, stating drag-region behaviour, stacking, focus return and dismissal. Ends with a recommendation and a named fallback if any check fails. No production code is merged from this bead.
notes: REOPENED 2026-07-27 by coordinator after an adversarial review of the spike. The bead was closed prematurely and its headline number is not what it is labelled. Three defects in the measurement, none of them the worker's fault beyond method: (1) primitives were built CUMULATIVELY with Select FIRST, so the '34 KB shared core' contains Select's own dependencies — @internationalized/number, collection machinery, live announcer — and a Dialog-only build may include almost none of it; the report therefore cannot conclude Dialog+Popover+Tooltip costs 34+3.2 KB. (2) The production baseline and the harness were SEPARATE builds and the delta was added arithmetically; section 4.1 required measurement against the real production entry. (3) No packaged WebKitGTK run and no Wails drag interaction, both of which 4.1 required. Also: the coordinator misquoted the budget — ADR-0012's 25-35 KB is a NET allowance against which the migration already spent +7 KB, so +34 would exceed the ceiling by about 6 KB, not consume all of it. Redo measures each primitive INDEPENDENTLY, then the intended combinations, against the real production entry with a Rollup metafile attributing gzip by package, and compares against a local implementation that RETAINS @floating-ui/dom where collision-aware positioning is genuinely needed.
close_reason: Redo measured each primitive independently against the real production entry with by-package attribution: Dialog +11.6 KB gzip, Tooltip +17.4, Popover +20.9, the three together +23.7; ContextMenu +30.5, Select +31.7, Combobox +33.6; Corvu dialog +4.1. Native <dialog> confirmed available at our floors (Safari 15.4 era, below the 16.2 floor); HTML Popover API is Safari 17 and therefore above it. The first spike's 34 KB was Select's dependency closure charged to everything after it. Packaged Wails run still NOT done — blocked by webkit2gtk-4.1 with no 4.0 available; filed separately. Scripts preserved at .internal/measure/ so the numbers can be re-derived.

title: Kit wave 1: the components we write ourselves
acceptance_criteria: Button, TextField, SearchField, Checkbox, Field, Section, Toolbar, Badge, EmptyState and Toggle exist in frontend/src/ui/ with tests covering keyboard operation, focus-visible, disabled and invalid states. Each component has a documented API and an inventory entry naming its consumers. No component duplicates another; where an existing surface already had the control, the surface-local version is deleted rather than left beside the kit one.
notes: Reframed 2026-07-27 after the kit decision moved to per-primitive and platform-first. Native <select> inside a kit wrapper belongs to this wave, not the overlay wave — it costs zero bytes and brings keyboard operation, platform accessibility, form semantics and typeahead. Acceptance gains: the wrapper must PRESERVE native keyboard and form semantics rather than reimplementing them, and the styling limit is stated honestly — appearance:none plus a local arrow improves the closed control, the open popup stays platform-owned. If the owner later rejects that trade, it becomes a custom listbox with its own bead and its own measured cost.
close_reason: Ten kit components: seven audited and extended (variant, disabled, error, description, id, role props), three new (Field, Badge, EmptyState). Toggle judged unnecessary — Checkbox covers it. Select was already native; gained appearance:none, a disabled prop, and a real bug fix: value binding moved from the selected attribute to select.value. Inventory at frontend/src/ui/README.md. 152 tests across 19 files pass. Coordinator fixed one eslint-autofix-versus-tsc conflict.

title: The state ownership table: which slice is shared and accepted, which is local to a surface
acceptance_criteria: A written table names every piece of frontend state and its owner, distinguishing accepted shared state (tab list, active tab, tab placement, active sidebar view, sidebar collapsed, selected theme, accepted settings revision and values) from surface-local state (edit drafts, validation messages, expanded cards, file selections, busy flags). It states, for each shared slice, whether Go or the frontend is authoritative, and the versioned persistence rule including the migration from the existing nocx.sidebar.collapsed key. It is a document, not code; nocx-ycet implements it.

title: Tab strip renders its buttons with <For>
acceptance_criteria: tab-strip.tsx has no createElement, no paintButton, no refreshIndices and no innerHTML assignment; buttons render from <For> keyed by tab id. A written DOM compatibility matrix lists every selector preserved and every one deliberately changed with the assertion that replaces it. Node identity and focus survive reorder. Roving tabindex, arrow/Home/End and ARIA linkage are verified by e2e in both orientations. Every unit and e2e file asserting the old DOM shape lands in the same commit.
close_reason: Buttons render from <For> keyed by tab id over a local Solid store; createElement, paintButton, refreshIndices, the innerHTML reorder and all DOM patching are gone. 20 selectors preserved, 0 changed, matrix at .internal/specs/2026-07-27-tab-strip-dom-matrix.md. 60 unit tests, node identity across reorder asserted with isSameNode. Six e2e specs pass in Chromium 3.6s and WebKit 6.4s, measured per engine. First attempt rejected: it renamed paintButton into a createEffect walking container.children and justified it with a false claim about <For> untracking; recorded as a bd memory. Gap left open: focus survival after reorder is unverified.

title: Sidebar: view registry, two activity-bar zones, icons as components, Sessions deleted
acceptance_criteria: A SidebarViewDescriptor registry exists and adding a view costs one registration plus one component, with no edit to App.tsx, the activity bar or the panel. Views and global actions are two types rendered by two components, so an action can never drive panel content. The panel is JSX with no createElement and no style.display toggling. Icons are TSX components using currentColor; no innerHTML remains in any app surface and a test asserts no SVG is built from a string at runtime. The Sessions placeholder is gone and a cold start opens no empty panel.
close_reason: View registry, two-zone activity bar, JSX panel, TSX icon components with currentColor, roving-tabindex keyboard model with focus return, Sessions and Connections both removed from the bar. 12 unit tests plus 47 related pass; e2e 4/4 in Chromium and WebKit. Coordinator fixed a solid/reactivity violation the worker left: ActiveView hoisted props.desc.view into a local, which reads once outside any tracked scope and would keep rendering the first view after a switch — now via Dynamic.

title: UpdateNotice renders from a discriminated union
acceptance_criteria: main.tsx contains no createElement and no innerHTML; the update notice is a Solid component driven by the union in spec section 3.3. A unit test covers every state-to-state transition, including error-to-available and downloading-to-available, asserting that no class from the previous state survives.

CSS extracted from style.css into styles/update-notice.css. The old empty-version showPendingRestart('') behaviour is preserved deliberately.

title: #workspace and #vertical-tabstrip: the vertical strip stops being mounted in the title bar
acceptance_criteria: App.tsx renders #workspace containing #vertical-tabstrip and #body; orientation selects the mount host; #tabbar stays present as the Wails drag region in both placements. e2e/tabs.spec.ts:57-78,122-143, which assert .tabstrip-vertical on #tabbar, are updated in the same commit. A bounding-box e2e asserts the strip sits left of #body, the drag bar above the workspace, and panes keep non-zero width, in both Chromium and WebKit.
close_reason: App.tsx renders #workspace over #vertical-tabstrip and #body; TabStrip exposes orientation, TabManager picks the host, replaceStrip moves ownership both ways and clears the vacated host. #tabbar stays as the Wails drag region in both placements. e2e/vertical-tab-placement.spec.ts flipped to a real assertion; tabs.spec.ts stopped asserting the bug. Five specs pass in Chromium and WebKit; terminal host node survives a placement round trip. Coordinator addition: the vacated host also drops role/aria-label/aria-orientation, which innerHTML='' alone left behind as an empty tablist.

title: One seam: .surface-host plus a generic SolidTabContent, height contract as selectors
acceptance_criteria: A single SolidTabContent creates .surface-host, opens exactly one Solid root, forwards viewport changes and disposes exactly once; settings-content.ts and connections-content.ts no longer duplicate that logic. The selectors in spec section 6.1 exist for #panes, .surface-host, .ui-page, .ui-page__header, .ui-page__body, .ui-page__rail and .ui-page__scroll, each with the stated min-height/min-width. The scroll test from .1 passes in packaged WebKitGTK in both the normal and the narrow layout.
close_reason: SolidTabContent owns the seam — .surface-host, one Solid root, one disposal; both *-content.ts are thin adapters, ~31 lines of duplication gone. Height contract landed as explicit selectors. Worker found the second-order cause the spec missed: .st-container had height:100% but no min-height:0, and WebKit's implicit flex minimum overrode it. Also found that the pinning test from nocx-82l9.1 called boundingBox.bottom, which is not a Playwright API. settings-scroll passes as an ordinary webkit test in both normal and narrow layouts. Coordinator: de-asynced the base mount, deleted the orphaned mountConnectionsView, and did NOT take the worker's unrelated unpinning of @playwright/test.

title: Correct ADR-0012 'As shipped' and pin the three defects with failing tests
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0012's 'As shipped' section describes what actually shipped: the tab strip renders only its static wrapper, the sidebar panel is built imperatively, UpdateNotice is a vanilla DOM class, and the state store has one consumer. Three tests exist and fail for the right reason: settings scroll at a short window height (WebKit e2e), the vertical strip's mount host (e2e), and UpdateNotice error-to-available (unit). No production code changes in this bead.

Three defects pinned with it.fails/test.fail so the suite stays green: settings scroll (webkit e2e), vertical strip mounted in #tabbar, UpdateNotice stale class. Only production change is exporting UpdateNotice for the test.

title: [epic] Page composition: every surface is built on one base page, Connections moves into Settings
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-27-ui-shell-kit-and-theming-design.md sections 2.3 and 6.

Tabby has no separate Connections screen: profiles are a page inside settings (tabby-settings/src/components/profilesSettingsTab.component.*). SSH functionality is not reduced — only its entry point changes. Quick connect moves to the Servers sidebar view (nocx-eab).
acceptance_criteria: Page/PageHeader/PageBody/PageRail/PageScroller/PageSection exist and PageScroller is the only scrolling node; a test asserts no surface introduces a second scroll container. Settings, its sub-pages and Export render through Page and the kit, with no raw interactive controls. Connections is a Settings sub-page: SURFACE_CONNECTIONS, connections-content.ts and the connections tab surface are deleted, and profiles, groups, credentials and Tabby import all still work, pinned by e2e. The settings screen stays generated from Go declarations — adding a setting still costs zero frontend changes.
notes: Spec revised 2026-07-27. Relevant sections: 2.4 (where SSH lives), 6.1-6.4 (height contract, two scroll owners, seam, Settings page registry), 6.5 (keyboard/focus). Sequence steps 8, 9a, 9b, 10 — Connections is ADDED as a sub-page and proven reachable (9a) BEFORE the standalone surface is deleted (9b). The generated-screen invariant is scoped to generated pages; the rail is a typed registry.

Two named scroll owners with a test that fails on a third, checked in a real browser as well as jsdom. Settings, Connections and Export all render through Page and the kit. description:

Measured 2026-07-27: style.css is 2285 lines with 232 hardcoded hex colours (27 unique) and 2 custom properties, both fonts. Themes (nocx-8yg.6) cannot be built on that. Needs an ADR first: plain CSS with semantic tokens, rejecting Tailwind and CSS Modules.

notes: Spec revised 2026-07-27. Section 5 in full: 5.1 derived/state colour tokens, 5.2 allowed colour GRAMMAR (not a hex denylist — covers named/oklch/lab/gradients/JSX style/SVG attrs and color-mix laundering), 5.3 non-CSS colour sources, 5.4 synchronous bootstrap theme resolver closing the xterm startup race plus applyTheme as a controller op honouring ADR-0005's refresh pump, 5.5 frozen scrollback is snapshot-themed.

title: Migrate the settings surface to Solid, with exactly one search box and one modified filter
description:
The biggest surface: settings.ts (821, minus the domain logic already extracted to settings-domain.ts by nocx-njrx.3) and settings-content.ts (337), with 999 + 718 lines of structural test that go when they land.

BEHAVIOUR NOT TO PRESERVE — acceptance criteria of this migration, not separate fixes:

- nocx-x6w9: settings.ts and settings-content.ts each build a search box and a modified filter. The migrated surface has EXACTLY ONE of each. This is the canonical ownership failure the whole epic exists to remove; a worker who faithfully rebuilds both has reproduced the defect.
- nocx-ucxl: clicking a section in the settings rail changes nothing in the content pane. The migrated surface makes section selection produce a visible change every time.

The domain transitions are already pure and tested — recordSaveOutcome, canResetSetting, applyAcceptedSnapshot and the RevisionPolicy values. Consume them; do not reimplement them in effects, and do not put authority into a component.

METHOD: characterization test first, green against the CURRENT implementation, then rewrite, same test green, then delete settings-content.ts, the view half of settings.ts and both structural tests in the same commit.

COST BASIS (measured, nocx-njrx.6): the pilot migrated a 139-line imperative leaf into a 122-line Solid component plus a 146-line characterization test in about 28 minutes, roughly 5 of which was toolchain friction. That surface had no reactive state, no terminal contact and no store, so it is a FLOOR: plan this one at 1.5-3x the pilot and say in your report where the real time went.

## Acceptance Criteria

The settings surface renders from Solid components using the local kit and the extracted domain functions; exactly one search box and one modified filter exist; selecting a rail section always changes the content pane; the characterization test that was green against the old implementation stays green; predecessors and their structural tests are deleted in the same commit; e2e green in both browser projects.

It migrates first and converts that call site; this bead consumes the Solid <ExportSection/> component directly and must not reintroduce an imperative render call.
close_reason:
settings.ts (821) is deleted and settings-content.ts is reduced to a thin TabContent wrapper; the surface is settings.tsx built on the kit, consuming the already-extracted domain functions (recordSaveOutcome, canResetSetting, applyAcceptedSnapshot) rather than reimplementing them in effects. ExportSection is rendered as a child component, so the island boundary mountExportSection is gone — which is exactly why the export bead ran first.

Both behaviour criteria are pinned by tests, verified in the commit (7cf9ae7) rather than in a worktree: nocx-x6w9 — 'exactly ONE search input in the entire surface' and 'exactly ONE modified-only filter checkbox in the entire surface', with settings-content.ts now containing zero search/filter chrome; nocx-ucxl — clicking a rail section always changes the content pane.

Net: 2,630 lines deleted against 1,018 written, including 1,750 lines of structural tests that asserted the old DOM shape. Gate on the merged trunk: 632 tests in 40 files, typecheck, eslint --max-warnings 0, build and prettier clean; e2e webkit 18/18 (including tabs.spec.ts:81, which drives the settings surface and was the webkit regression earlier in this epic) and chromium 19/20 with only the known pre-existing flake.

title: The shell becomes one Solid root: main.ts, tab-strip.ts and the tab-list half of tabs.ts
description:
The last and riskiest surface, deliberately done after every leaf: main.ts (288), tab-strip.ts (596) and the tab-list half of tabs.ts (598), plus native-mode.ts (8) folded in. tab-strip.test.ts is 848 lines of structural assertions that go with it.

This is where the islands become one application root, and where AD-6 is easiest to break. The non-negotiable boundary: Solid creates an EMPTY host element and the terminal adapter owns its descendants. Solid may control the host's placement, size, classes and visibility, and must never render children beneath it, never key or remount it during ordinary tab activation — that risks session loss, WebGL churn and Linux repaint regressions — and never express terminal render state as reactive state.

tabs.ts is the boundary file: TabManager is part tab list (migrates) and part terminal lifecycle (must not). Split it along that line before migrating the half that moves. tabs.test.ts (1,377 lines) is a test of the AD-6 lifecycle contract, not of markup — it STAYS, and it is the proof the boundary held.

nocx-njrx.4 has already removed the constructor side effect and introduced the surface registry, so the root can decide when children exist and each surface is declared once.

COST BASIS (measured, nocx-njrx.6): the pilot migrated a 139-line imperative leaf into a 122-line Solid component plus a 146-line characterization test in about 28 minutes, roughly 5 of which was toolchain friction. That surface had no reactive state, no terminal contact and no store, so it is a FLOOR: plan this one at 1.5-3x the pilot and say in your report where the real time went.

## Acceptance Criteria

One Solid root owns the shell; the terminal host is an empty element the adapter owns, and the mount/dispose counters prove it mounts and disposes exactly once across tab switches and closes; the tab-list half of tabs.ts is Solid and the terminal-lifecycle half is untouched imperative code; main.ts, tab-strip.ts, native-mode.ts and tab-strip.test.ts are deleted or reduced to the composition root in the same commit; tabs.test.ts still passes unchanged; e2e green in both browser projects.
close_reason:
Two rounds. Round 1: tab-strip.ts (596) and tab-strip.test.ts (848) deleted, HorizontalTabStrip and VerticalTabStrip Solid-backed in tab-strip.tsx, and — the thing most at risk — tabs.test.ts passed UNCHANGED, so the AD-6 lifecycle contract held. native-mode.ts kept standalone because folding it in caused import-chain side effects; reported rather than hidden.

Round 1 left out the bead's headline criterion and did not mention it: main.ts was untouched and the app opened six separate Solid roots. Round 2 landed App.tsx — one root, rendering the shell skeleton as EMPTY hosts (#tabbar, #activitybar, #sidebar, #panes) with no reactive state, and index.html reduced to <div id="app">. main.ts became main.tsx and is now the composition root only. The panes host carries an explicit comment that Solid must never render children beneath it, key it or remount it — AD-6's UI corollary, at the exact place someone would break it.

Per-tab surfaces (settings, connections, export-section) still open their own roots, mounted into panes through the TabContent seam; the worker stated that rather than leaving it to be discovered. Gate: 581 tests in 40 files, typecheck, eslint --max-warnings 0, build, prettier clean; e2e webkit 18/18 and chromium 20/20.

title: Close the epic: no imperative application UI left, and the docs say what shipped
description:
The finishing bead, and the one that makes the epic's success criterion checkable rather than asserted.

- Prove that no module under frontend/src builds application UI imperatively except the boundary files AD-6 keeps that way: terminal-content.ts, renderers/, scrollback/, editor.ts, input-state.ts, input-target.ts, dispatcher.ts, gutter.ts, command-ledger.ts, clipboard.ts, frame.ts, submit.ts, ipc.ts. A reader can verify the epic's claim from the repository: the imperative-UI inventory is empty outside the named boundary files, the predecessors are gone from the tree, the lint fixture is proven still self-testing, the docs describe the shipped design, and the full gate plus e2e are green in both browser projects.

Closing sweep, verified on the tree rather than asserted.

IMPERATIVE-UI INVENTORY IS EMPTY outside the boundary files. Every document.createElement left in frontend/src is accounted for: editor.ts (5) and gutter.ts (2) and terminal-content.ts (1) are terminal-owned by AD-6; settings-content.ts (1) and the tab pane in tabs.ts (1) are host elements the seam owns — Solid renders nothing beneath them; export-utils.ts's download anchor is the browser's download idiom and never enters the document, and its two copies were folded into one helper in this bead.

PREDECESSORS DELETED: banner.ts, sidebar.ts, export-section.ts, connections.ts, settings.ts, tab-strip.ts, main.ts (now main.tsx), and both spike directories. About 3,700 lines of structural tests went with them.

LINT FIXTURE PROVEN STILL SELF-TESTING: broken deliberately a third time — removing the no-destructure case made the gate exit 1 naming solid/no-destructure, restoring it exited 0. It asserts each of the seven rules by name and separately that solid/reactivity fires from a .ts file.

DOCS UPDATED: ADR-0012 has an 'As shipped' section (what migrated, what stays imperative and why that is permanent, the three defects fixed inside the migrations that caused them, the measured bundle cost of +7 KB gzip net against a 25-35 KB budget, and why the lint gate had to extend to .ts). AD-6's UI corollary in docs/architecture.md gains setTarget as a fourth crossing and the ordering rule the epic learned by breaking it: visibility is applied before anything measures geometry.

title: Local Solid component kit: one vocabulary for controls, built here
description:
Step 5 of the epic. Every migrated surface draws from the same small kit rather than hand-rolling its controls: button, checkbox, select, text field, search field, toolbar, section, dialog.

Deliberately local and small. A prebuilt visual suite is explicitly out of scope for this epic — it fights the terminal aesthetic and carries styling assumptions unsuited to embedded webviews (WKWebView / WebView2 / WebKitGTK, not Chromium).

Build it from what the existing surfaces actually use — read settings.ts, connections.ts and export-section.ts first and let the inventory decide the component list. A kit designed ahead of its callers is speculative (YAGNI); a kit extracted from three real surfaces is not.

COST BASIS (measured, nocx-njrx.6): the pilot migrated a 139-line imperative leaf into a 122-line Solid component plus a 146-line characterization test in about 28 minutes, roughly 5 of which was toolchain friction. That surface had no reactive state, no terminal contact and no store, so it is a FLOOR: plan this one at 1.5-3x the pilot and say in your report where the real time went.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every control in the kit has a Solid component with a test; the components take props rather than destructured props (solid/no-destructure is an error here); each one is used by at least one migrated surface by the end of the epic; no third-party component library is added.
close_reason:
Seven Solid components in frontend/src/ui/ — button, checkbox, select, text field, search field, toolbar, section — each documenting the call sites in settings.ts, connections.ts and export-section.ts that justify its props, so the kit is distilled from real callers rather than designed ahead of them. Dialog deliberately NOT built and the worker said so: none of the three surfaces uses a modal, they call native confirm()/prompt(). The bead's list was an inventory to check, not a quota to fill.

Process note worth carrying: the worker reported a green gate but never committed — the files sat untracked in its worktree while the report read as finished. The coordinator committed them after running the gate itself. 'Reported done' and 'in the branch' are different claims; check the branch.

title: Migrate the sidebar to Solid, and fix the cold-start empty panel while rewriting it
description:
Surface migration, 164 lines plus a 127-line structural test.

BEHAVIOUR NOT TO PRESERVE — this is an acceptance criterion of the migration, not a separate fix. nocx-rp2j: a cold start opens an empty panel because view registration mixes panel-views and tab-action entries in one list. The migrated sidebar has no empty-panel state at cold start, and panel-views and tab-actions are separate concepts rather than two kinds of row in one array.

COST BASIS (measured, nocx-njrx.6): the pilot migrated a 139-line imperative leaf into a 122-line Solid component plus a 146-line characterization test in about 28 minutes, roughly 5 of which was toolchain friction. That surface had no reactive state, no terminal contact and no store, so it is a FLOOR: plan this one at 1.5-3x the pilot and say in your report where the real time went.

The sidebar renders from Solid components using the local kit; a characterization test that was green against the old implementation is still green; cold start shows no empty panel and panel-views and tab-actions are distinct in the model; sidebar.ts and its structural test are deleted in the commit that lands the replacement; e2e green in both browser projects.

sidebar.ts is deleted; the surface is sidebar.tsx, a Solid component using the store. nocx-rp2j is fixed as an acceptance criterion rather than a separate patch: panel-views and tab-actions are separate typed arguments to mountSidebar instead of two kinds of row in one list, the first PANEL view decides the initial selection, and the sidebar starts collapsed when no panel view exists — which is what left an empty panel open at cold start. title: Application state lives in one Solid store, with authority in framework-neutral TypeScript
description:
Step 2 of the epic. Today each module owns its own fields and the shell threads them by constructor argument; there is no single place that says what the application currently is.

Create the state module: Solid signals/stores holding ACCEPTED state only. The transition and authority rules stay in framework-neutral .ts — settings-domain.ts (nocx-njrx.3) is the worked example and the shape to follow: a value that carries authority can only be produced by the function that checks it, and no consumer branches on which rule is in force (AD-8).

What belongs in the store: tab model and activation, sidebar view selection, settings mirror and its revision, connection profiles list, banner state. What does NOT: terminal render state, buffers, selections or per-cell data — AD-6 keeps those imperative and inside the terminal controller, and expressing them as reactive state is explicitly out.

Slice ownership is the deliverable, not just the file: each slice names who may write it and through which transition. A slice anyone can assign is the per-module-fields problem with extra steps.

COST BASIS (measured, nocx-njrx.6): the pilot migrated a 139-line imperative leaf into a 122-line Solid component plus a 146-line characterization test in about 28 minutes, roughly 5 of which was toolchain friction. That surface had no reactive state, no terminal contact and no store, so it is a FLOOR: plan this one at 1.5-3x the pilot and say in your report where the real time went.

## Acceptance Criteria

One store module owns accepted application state; every write goes through a named transition in framework-neutral TypeScript with direct unit tests and no DOM; no terminal render state appears in it; the surfaces migrated after this bead read from it rather than holding private copies.
close_reason:
frontend/src/state/: five slices (tab-model, sidebar-model, settings-model over the existing settings-domain, profiles-model, banner-model) behind one Solid store with named transitions, 68 new tests, no DOM in any of them. Slice ownership is documented in the store header rather than left implicit, which was the actual deliverable.

AD-6 audited by the coordinator rather than taken on trust: no buffer, scrollback, selection, renderer, grid or per-cell state appears anywhere in the module — the only mentions are comments saying those belong to the terminal. The settings slice reuses settings-domain.ts from nocx-njrx.3 instead of re-implementing the revision policy.

title: A credential with no host can be created; it is refused only at connect time
description:
A credential with no host can be created and saved. It is refused only later, at connect
time, by `checkBinding` in `internal/ssh` (`ErrCredentialNotBound`). So the rule exists but
fires at the worst possible moment: the user has already stored a secret, and the failure
surfaces as a broken connection rather than as a rejected form.

The owner's decision (2026-07-27) is that host binding stays mandatory — see nocx-mon for the
original policy — and therefore it must be impossible to CREATE an unbound credential.

## Current state, read from the code

- `internal/transport/ws.go` `credentials.create` / `credentials.update` validate nothing but
  renderer-supplied secret ids.
- `internal/profile.JSONStore.SaveCredential` persists whatever it is given.
- `frontend/src/connections.ts:774` checks name and username only — and on failure calls
  `log.warn`, so the Save button silently does nothing with no message on screen.
- The form label at :722 already reads "Bind to Host (required)", which today is simply untrue.

## Where enforcement belongs

At the persistence boundary, not in the transport handler: `SaveCredential` is the one place
every writer must pass through, and putting the rule beside the type keeps it from drifting —
the same argument that put `checkBinding` in `internal/ssh` after config resolution rather
than in the caller. The renderer check is a convenience for the user, never the guarantee.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Connection Manager → create a credential, fill name and username, leave "Bind to Host" empty.
2. Save. It is accepted and stored.
3. Use it to connect: the connection fails with the credential refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

An unbound credential cannot be stored: the backend refuses it at save time with an error the
UI shows, the form refuses to submit without a host and says why on screen rather than only in
the console, and a test covers both. Existing stored credentials with an empty host are
considered in the fix rather than silently left unusable.
close_reason: Merged to main as 0b43e4e. An unbound credential can no longer be stored: Credential.Validate is enforced in SaveCredential, the persistence boundary every writer passes through, and the RPC surfaces it as Invalid params so the form can name the field. The renderer guard and on-form error message are usability, not the guarantee. CI run 30221757786 green on all three jobs. Existing stored credentials with an empty host stay refused at connect time, as nocx-mon deliberately decided.

title: e2e multi-tab-input flakes under full-suite load — green alone, ~1 failure in 3 suite runs
description:
`e2e/multi-tab-input.spec.ts:13` — "first tab still accepts input after second tab is
created" — fails intermittently when the whole suite runs, and passes reliably alone.

Measured on the merge commit 8f15a54, headless devharness path, chromium, 1 worker:

| how it was run | result |
|---|---|
| the spec alone, 3 consecutive runs | 2 passed, 1.5s each — 3/3 green |
| the full suite, 3 consecutive runs | one run failed at this test (9.1s), two runs 20/20 (8.3s) |

So roughly one full-suite run in three. That is high enough to break a required check and
exactly the class nocx-epm already recorded for the activity-bell test ("fixed sleeps race
the shell") and nocx-zaj for the Go side.

The test itself is sound and it genuinely catches nocx-4ff.28 — verified by reverting the
one-line guard in terminal-content.ts and watching it fail, then restoring. This is not a
reason to weaken or delete it.

Likely direction, to be confirmed rather than assumed: the headless harness runs one
devharness backend for the entire suite, so sessions and shell state accumulate across
specs. This test types a command and waits for the OSC 0 title to change on tab 1; under a
loaded backend the prompt may not be ready when the keystrokes are sent, so the command
lands somewhere that never produces the title. Note the failing run took 9.1s against 8.3s
for the green ones — it waited and then gave up.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
go run ./cmd/devharness &            # prints WSPORT / WSTOKEN
cd frontend && npx vite --port 5173 --strictPort &
NOCX_WS_PORT=<port> NOCX_WS_TOKEN=<token> npx playwright test --project=chromium --reporter=line
# repeat several times; expect an intermittent failure at multi-tab-input.spec.ts:13
```

Observed: intermittent failure in the full suite, reliable pass in isolation.
Expected: green in both, repeatably.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test gates on a condition that proves the tab is ready to receive the command —
  prompt ownership, as nocx-5zl4 did for the rest of the suite — rather than on the
  arrival of a title that a lost keystroke can never produce.
- No fixed sleeps are introduced; that is what nocx-epm had to remove.
- Ten consecutive full-suite runs are green. Report the count, not an adjective.
- If the root cause turns out to be shared backend state across specs rather than timing,
  say so and fix that instead — the diagnosis above is a lead, not a conclusion.
notes: Likely root cause identified 2026-07-27 while fixing a new spec: fixed page.waitForTimeout sleeps rather than polling an observable outcome. A 200ms sleep for Solid to re-sort DOM nodes failed about one run in three on chromium, and a focus call issued immediately after a placement switch could land on a node the remount was replacing. Both became stable when converted to expect.poll. multi-tab-input and activity-bell show the same signature — green alone, fail under suite load — so audit them for the same pattern before looking for anything more exotic.
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed 2026-07-27: an unawaited web-first assertion at multi-tab-input.spec.ts:58. Playwright's expect(locator) returns a promise; without await it never ran where written and its rejection surfaced elsewhere — asserting nothing on a good day, failing the run on a bad one. Awaited with an explicit timeout; three consecutive clean runs of the spec and a clean full suite. Swept every e2e spec for other floating assertions: none. The earlier fixed-timeout hypothesis was wrong for this spec though right for focus-after-reorder — two defects, one signature.

title: Pilot: migrate one leaf surface to Solid and record what it actually cost
description:
The first Solid component in the product, chosen to be small and to touch nothing structural. banner.ts (139 lines) or sidebar.ts (164) — pick when starting, banner is the safer default.

WHY A LEAF AND NOT THE SHELL. The epic's step 1 puts the application root first, but the shell IS main.ts + tabs.ts + tab-strip.ts: the AD-6 boundary and the riskiest code in the frontend. Starting there means doing the hardest thing before anyone has written a Solid component here or proven the test harness. Solid mounts into any existing DOM element via render(), so an island inside the current imperative shell is entirely viable and orders of magnitude cheaper to back out. Module-level signals cross root boundaries without a provider, so islands do not fragment state.

TEST METHOD, which is the point of the pilot as much as the component is (agreed 2026-07-26, see the epic notes):
1. Write a characterization test for the surface's observable behaviour.
2. Make it green against the CURRENT imperative implementation. A test that has never run against the old code proves nothing.
3. Rewrite the surface in Solid.
4. Same test, still green.
5. Delete the old file and its structure-bound test in the SAME commit.

Record the real numbers in this bead when done: hours, characterization lines vs deleted lines, and anything the harness got wrong. The next surfaces are estimated from this, not from guesses.

OWNS FILES: the chosen leaf surface and its test, plus the single line in main.ts that mounts it.
acceptance_criteria: One leaf surface renders from a Solid component in the running app; a characterization test that was green against the old implementation is still green against the new one; the imperative predecessor and its structural test are deleted in the same commit; eslint-plugin-solid passes on the new component; the e2e suite is green in both chromium and webkit projects; measured cost is written back into this bead.
notes: MINOR COLLISION, deliberately not an edge: this bead adds one line to main.ts to mount the island, and nocx-njrx.4 restructures main.ts. That is a trivial merge rather than a cascading conflict, so the two stay parallel. Whoever lands second rebases the single line; if nocx-njrx.4 is already in flight, mount through the surface registry it introduces instead of adding a bare line.
close_reason:
PILOT LANDED. banner.ts (139 lines, imperative) is now banner.tsx (122 lines, Solid) behind the unchanged ClipboardBanner interface, so main.ts and tabs.ts needed no edit at all — the surface was already sitting on an AD-8 seam. Old banner.ts and banner.test.ts deleted in the same commit as the replacement (6fa7f94).

METHOD VERIFIED, not taken on trust: the coordinator restored the old banner.ts in the worker's worktree, deleted banner.tsx and ran the new characterization test against the imperative implementation — 11 tests, all green. So the test really is evidence rather than a wish, which is the property the whole method depends on.

MEASURED COST, which is what every remaining surface is now estimated from: about 28 minutes wall-clock, of which roughly 5 was toolchain friction (solid-js/web Dispose type not exported, solid/reactivity firing on an onClick handler binding, the test-file extension constraint). 146 lines of characterization test written, 79 lines of structural test deleted, 139 deleted and 122 written in production code. The worker's own caveat is the honest part: this was the easiest remaining leaf — no reactive state, no terminal contact, no store — so 28 minutes is a FLOOR, and sidebar / export-section / connections / settings should be planned at 1.5-3x.

ONE DIFFERENCE WORTH RECORDING, in an unreachable path: when #panes is absent the old code did 'document.getElementById("panes")?.append(...)' and left the promise unresolved with _shown stuck true; the Solid version resolves 'dismiss' and resets the flag. #panes is in index.html so no user can reach either branch, but a migration that forbids behaviour changes should still name the ones it makes.

title: Composition root becomes declarative-ready: no side effect in TabManager's constructor, one surface registry
description:
Clears the two things that stop the shell from becoming a Solid root. Sequenced behind nocx-njrx.2 because it edits the same files, NOT because it is less important.

1. CONSTRUCTOR SIDE EFFECT. TabManager opens the initial tab from inside its own constructor (tabs.ts:301) and derives _initialTabReady from that tab's content. A constructor that mounts UI cannot live under a declarative root — the root decides when children exist. Bootstrap in main.ts is also order-dependent and async: GetWSPort -> connect -> getSnapshot -> pick a strip -> construct TabManager (main.ts:119-158). Move initial-tab creation to an explicit call the root makes.

2. DUPLICATED SURFACE CONSTRUCTION. main.ts builds 'new SettingsContent(profileClient)' plus a verbatim copy of its ContentDescriptor in two places — the sidebar entry (main.ts:219-230) and the Cmd/Ctrl+, handler (main.ts:238-247). Singleton identity and the action that opens a surface have no single owner. Introduce a surface registry/factory so a surface is declared once and both entry points ask the registry for it. This is what makes step 6 (surface-by-surface migration) cheap, and it is the fix codex flagged independently.

Related and worth folding in while here: tabs.ts wires strip intents twice, verbatim — the constructor block (tabs.ts:287-296) and wireStrip (tabs.ts:436-445). The constructor should just call wireStrip.

OWNS FILES: frontend/src/main.ts, frontend/src/tabs.ts, the new registry module, and their tests.

Still imperative. This bead does not introduce Solid.
acceptance_criteria: Creating a TabManager mounts nothing; the initial tab is opened by an explicit call from the composition root and initialTabReady still resolves only from terminal content. SettingsContent and its descriptor are declared exactly once and both the sidebar entry and Cmd/Ctrl+, resolve them through the registry. Strip intents are wired in one place. Behaviour is unchanged, tabs.test.ts and the e2e suite are green.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-07-27 by the coordinator, and the reason is a coordinator process failure rather than a worker one.

The round-2 revision (register connections too, build() throws on an unknown id with exported id constants, openInitialTab() guarded against a second call, typo fix) was reviewed and accepted — but it was reviewed by GREPPING THE WORKER'S WORKING TREE, not by reading the commit. The worker never committed it. f00560d, the commit that was merged and that this bead was closed on, contains round 1 only: build() still returned undefined, connections was still constructed inline in main.ts beside the registry, and openInitialTab() had no guard.

The worktree was then removed after the merge, so the uncommitted revision is unrecoverable. Redoing it is minutes; the lesson is the expensive part.

TWO RULES ADOPTED, both of which would have caught this in seconds:
1. Review the COMMIT, never the working tree: git show <sha> / git diff <base>..HEAD. A grep in a worktree tells you what an agent typed, not what it delivered.
2. Never remove a worker's worktree until 'git status --short' is empty AND the branch actually contains the work. 'Reported done' and 'in the branch' are different claims — the component-kit worker in this same wave also reported a green gate with everything untracked.
close_reason: REDONE AND VERIFIED IN THE COMMIT this time. Registry declares settings and connections; main.ts holds no ContentDescriptor literal and constructs no tab surface directly; build() throws on an unknown id naming the registered ones, so both call sites destructure unconditionally; ids are exported constants; openInitialTab() throws on a second call with a test that proves it. Landed in f1621f2 together with the sidebar migration, because both edit main.ts. Gate: 670 tests at that commit, e2e webkit 18/18 and chromium 19/20 with only the known flake.

title: TabContent seam is brought up to AD-6: enforce mount-once, add setVisible
description:
Prerequisite for migrating ANY surface. Two defects in the seam, found 2026-07-26 while reviewing the epic (second-opinion pass with codex confirmed both).

1. MOUNT-ONCE IS NOT ENFORCED BY THE SEAM. tab-content.ts:48 documents that mount() is called 'at most once per content instance'. tabs.ts:511 calls tab.start() unconditionally on every activation — the early return above it only covers re-activating the ALREADY active tab. What actually saves us is a private flag inside one implementation: terminal-content.ts:128, 'if (this.started || this._disposed) return'. So the contract holds by coincidence, not by construction. Any NEW TabContent implementation that does not replicate that flag gets re-mounted on every tab switch — and this epic exists to create new implementations. A migrated Solid Settings surface hits this first.

2. setVisible IS MISSING. architecture.md:146 (AD-6, UI-layer corollary) names exactly three imperative methods that may cross the boundary: setVisible, resize, focus. TabContent has mount/viewportChanged/focus/dispose. Visibility today is an incidental CSS class toggled in tabs.ts:92. Solid must be able to hide/show a terminal host without remounting it, and that has to be a method on the seam rather than a class the shell reaches in and sets.

OWNS FILES: frontend/src/tab-content.ts, frontend/src/tabs.ts, frontend/src/terminal-content.ts, frontend/src/tabs.test.ts. Nothing else in this epic may touch these while this bead is open — see the composition-root bead, which is sequenced behind it for exactly this reason.

Do NOT convert anything to Solid here. This is imperative-side work that makes the boundary safe to hand to Solid afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: Calling activate() repeatedly on the same tab mounts its content exactly once, asserted by a test that counts mount() calls through the seam and not through a TerminalContent private flag; a second TabContent implementation in the test proves the guard lives at the seam. TabContent exposes setVisible and tabs.ts drives visibility through it instead of toggling a class directly. viewportChanged/focus/dispose semantics are unchanged and the existing tabs.test.ts lifecycle assertions stay green.
close_reason: Mount-once is enforced at the seam (Tab.start guards; TerminalContent's private started flag deleted) and proved by a second TabContent implementation counting mount() calls. setVisible is on the seam with BaseTabContent implementing it once for all implementations, and tabs.ts no longer toggles the class — one owner, per AD-6. Took three rounds: round 2 left two owners of the same class, and round 3 fixed a webkit-only e2e regression the unit tests and chromium both missed — the content only learned its target inside mount(), so mount and the first viewportChanged measured a hidden pane. Content now receives its target via setTarget() from the Tab constructor, with an ordering test asserting visibility precedes mount.

title: Extract settings domain transitions into framework-neutral TypeScript
description:
Step 3 of the epic, done BEFORE the settings surface is migrated, and independent of everything else — it touches no shared file.

settings.ts mixes domain logic with DOM construction: draft preservation when a save is rejected, provenance-based reset, revision handling on an incoming snapshot (see around settings.ts:694). ADR-0012 requires those to live in framework-neutral .ts with authority encoded in the type — a settings snapshot carries its revision and an incoming one must pass the revision policy before replacing the local mirror.

If this is skipped, the migration moves imperative business logic straight into Solid effects and the rewrite improves nothing. Doing it first also means the hardest logic in the biggest surface is already under test, in pure functions, before anyone writes a component.

OWNS FILES: frontend/src/settings.ts, the new transition module, and their tests. Deliberately NOT settings-content.ts (that is chrome, and it goes with the surface migration).

Pure functions and types only — no Solid import in this bead. It should be mergeable whether or not the toolchain bead has landed.
acceptance_criteria: Draft preservation on rejected save, provenance-based reset, and the snapshot revision policy exist as pure exported functions with direct unit tests and no DOM dependency; settings.ts calls them instead of implementing them; no transition can produce a state that skips the revision check; existing settings behaviour is unchanged and the suite is green.
close_reason: Draft preservation, provenance-based reset and the snapshot revision policy are pure exported functions in settings-domain.ts with direct unit tests and no DOM. AcceptedSnapshot has a private constructor and a nominal brand, so accepted state cannot be produced without passing a gate (AD-7 shape). Revision policy is supplied by the caller as a named value (monotonicRevisionPolicy / reconnectRevisionPolicy behind a RevisionPolicy type), so no consumer branches on which policy is in force, per AD-8. hasDefault was dropped from canResetSetting because settings.ts:473 already guards on control!=='secret' && default!==undefined, which made the denial branch unreachable in production.

title: Solid toolchain: build, lint and test harness, with a self-testing lint fixture
description:
Step 1 of nocx-njrx, minus the shell. Lands the ability to write, lint and test a Solid component in this repo, changing ZERO application UI. Everything else in the epic waits on this and only on this.

OWNS FILES (no other bead in this epic touches them): frontend/package.json, frontend/vite.config.ts, frontend/vitest.config.ts, frontend/tsconfig.json, frontend/eslint.config.js, and the new lint fixture.

Work:
- vite-plugin-solid; pin solid-js 1.x (2.x is explicitly out per the epic).
- tsconfig: jsx=preserve, jsxImportSource=solid-js.
- vitest: the current config is environment:node (vitest.config.ts:8) with per-file jsdom pragmas. Solid component tests need jsdom AND resolve.conditions=['development','browser'] plus the solid plugin — without the export condition vitest resolves the SERVER build of solid-js and reactivity misbehaves with no useful error. Add @solidjs/testing-library.
- eslint-plugin-solid in flat config. Minimum rules: no-destructure, reactivity, no-react-deps, no-react-specific-props, prefer-for, prefer-show, components-return-once.
- NEGATIVE FIXTURE: a file containing every prohibited pattern, with the gate asserting lint FAILS on it. The plugin was last published 2024-12-11; without a fixture that tests itself, an ESLint or TypeScript upgrade can silently disable a rule and the mitigation evaporates unnoticed. The epic calls this a deliverable, not a nice-to-have.

Verify the fixture actually fails by breaking it deliberately once.
acceptance_criteria: A trivial Solid component compiles under 'npm run build', typechecks under 'npm run typecheck', and renders green in a vitest jsdom test using @solidjs/testing-library. 'npx eslint .' passes on src/ and FAILS on the negative fixture, and that failure is asserted by the gate rather than checked by hand. No file under frontend/src changes behaviour.
notes: WAVE-1 OWNERSHIP RULING 2026-07-27 (coordinator). nocx-njrx.5 deletes frontend/src/spike/ in parallel, and frontend/eslint.config.js:13 ignores 'src/spike/**'. This bead owns that file but must LEAVE the entry alone: the directory still exists in this branch's checkout, so removing the ignore would make eslint lint 810 lines of throwaway spike code and turn the gate red for no reason. The coordinator removes the stale entry and its comment after both branches land.
close_reason: Solid toolchain landed: solid-js 1.x, vite-plugin-solid, @solidjs/testing-library, jsx/jsxImportSource, vitest resolve.conditions with the node default preserved, eslint-plugin-solid at error for .ts as well as .tsx, and eslint --max-warnings 0. The negative fixture gate asserts each of the seven rules fires BY NAME and that solid/reactivity fires from a .ts file specifically; verified by the coordinator by breaking it — removing the .ts case exits 1 naming that rule, restoring it exits 0. Harness smoke test lives in src/test-support/.

title: Linux WebKitGTK cannot connect: origin wails://wails is rejected before the upgrade
description:
On Linux the WebSocket transport refuses every upgrade from the app's own webview, so
the app cannot talk to its backend at all.

WebKitGTK sends `Origin: wails://wails` — a bare hostname with no `.localhost` suffix.
`internal/transport/ws_auth.go` knows only the macOS WKWebView form, `wails.localhost`
(`wailsOriginHost`, :69), so `isWailsWebviewOrigin` returns false and `authorize` rejects
before the upgrade:

```
level=WARN msg="ws upgrade rejected" reason=origin_or_host origin=wails://wails host=127.0.0.1:42723
```

Reported by an external contributor (avlokhturov) with PR #14 attached.

## Scope

The check that fails is in `LoopbackOriginPolicy`, and that is the policy every running
instance uses — `PinnedOriginPolicy` has no production caller (see nocx-g9gv). So this is
not a dev-only path: it is what a packaged Linux build runs.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build and launch the app on Linux (WebKitGTK).
2. Observe the backend log: `ws upgrade rejected  reason=origin_or_host  origin=wails://wails`.
3. The UI never connects.

Not reproducible on macOS, where WKWebView sends `wails://wails.localhost:34115`.

## Not independently verified

That WebKitGTK sends exactly `wails://wails` comes from the contributor's captured log, not
from a run of our own — reproducing it needs a packaged Linux build with a display. The
claim is consistent with the platform being a supported target (ADR-0005 covers Linux
WebKitGTK behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

A packaged Linux build connects to its own backend: the webview's origin is accepted, the
Host loopback check is unchanged so DNS-rebinding protection still holds, and a test covers
the Linux origin form including the negative case where a wails origin does not excuse a
foreign Host.
close_reason: PR #14 merged as e5a4ae2. LoopbackOriginPolicy now accepts the Linux WebKitGTK origin form (wails://wails) alongside the macOS wails.localhost; Host loopback validation unchanged. CI run 30219542916 green on all three jobs. The origin string itself remains the contributor's captured observation, not one we reproduced.

title: [epic] The application UI runs on SolidJS
description:
Move the application UI onto SolidJS while the frontend is still small enough that the
