- nocx-6ek.2: an encrypted private key's stored passphrase is written, referenced and threaded into ConnectConfig, then never read. lookupKeyPassphrase has no caller, so a passphrase-protected key simply cannot be used.
- nocx-dcd: the vault inlines its own PBKDF2 to avoid a dependency that is already in go.mod. Hand-rolling a crypto primitive for a reason that does not hold.

Scoped together because they are the same file neighbourhood and the same risk class; splitting them would put two workers in internal/credential and internal/ssh at once.

DONE WHEN: a passphrase-protected key connects end to end with the passphrase taken from the store, the vault derives its key with golang.org/x/crypto/pbkdf2 instead of an inlined loop, and both paths have tests that fail if the wiring is removed again.
close_reason:
Epic complete: both children landed at 02ca0cc on shady2k/credential-hygiene and were verified against the diff, not the report. nocx-dcd replaced the hand-rolled PBKDF2 with x/crypto/pbkdf2 under a permanent three-way byte-equality proof (the original loop is preserved in pbkdf2_test.go precisely so the assertion outlives the swap). nocx-6ek.2 wired lookupKeyPassphrase so a stored passphrase is actually used, with ParsePrivateKeyWithPassphrase executing inside Secret.Use so the plaintext never becomes a string (ADR-0011 §2); two further findings in the same class were fixed — jump-host SecretID propagation, and a test that leaked the passphrase into assertion output.

Owed before anyone claims this works in the field: an end-to-end check against a real SSH server with a passphrase-protected key. Both beads are verified only at unit level with an encrypted ed25519 key.

Gate, coordinator-run: gofumpt clean, golangci-lint clean, go test -race clean, tsc clean, vitest 395 passed (21 files). Not merged — this branch is one of three awaiting integration.

title: Backlog sequencing: make 'what's next' deterministic for agents
description:
bd ready returns 68 of 99 open issues, so an agent asked to 'continue' has no basis to choose and takes whatever sorts first. The hierarchy is fine (15 root epics, zero orphans); what is missing is order INSIDE an epic: only 30 blocks-edges exist across 99 open issues, and nearly all of them sit in the three epics designed on 2026-07-26. The older epics are bags — nocx-4ff has 23 children in one ready wave, nocx-k0xk 15, nocx-8yg 13.

Four invariants, recorded in AGENTS.md:
1. An epic is a DAG, not a bag: bd swarm validate <epic> must show max parallelism <= 3.
2. Epics are never workable: --exclude-type epic everywhere.
3. The active track is an epic in status in_progress, WIP limit 3. Nothing else marks focus — not labels, not priority, not defer (defer is already taken by knowledge beads).
4. Claims are atomic and unassigned-only: -u --claim. That is what lets two agents work two tracks without coordinating.

'Continue working' then resolves to one documented command that loops bd ready --parent over the in_progress epics. Measured on the live DB: 68 candidates collapse to 5.

DONE WHEN: AGENTS.md documents the four invariants and the next-work command; docs/vision.md states the current freeze and the active tracks; and nocx-6ek, nocx-d3q and nocx-k0xk each pass bd swarm validate with max parallelism <= 3.
notes:
OUTCOME — the mechanism changed mid-implementation, for the better.

The original plan was a wrapper: loop bd ready --parent over the in_progress epics, because I assumed blocking an epic did not reach its children. The owner pushed back — 'my current work should block the rest' — and testing proved the assumption wrong. Beads propagates a blocked parent down to its children: of 20 non-ready issues, 7 were non-ready for that reason alone (nocx-d3q x4, nocx-w7h x2, nocx-dw3 x1), none of which has a blocks edge of its own.

So parking is expressed directly as epic-level blocks edges and the wrapper is unnecessary — bare 'bd ready --exclude-type epic -u' is the queue. Fewer moving parts than the design it replaced.

MEASURED, before -> after: ready non-epic 59 -> 7. Ready fronts: nocx-6ek 3, nocx-k0xk 3, nocx-8v51 1, nocx-v1pr 0. Epics appearing as ready: 0.

WHAT WAS WIRED: 25 epic-level parking edges (8 root epics x the 3 rewrite epics, plus nocx-d3q on nocx-6ek); nocx-w7h and nocx-dw3 inherit parking transitively through nocx-2gf. 12 ordering edges inside nocx-k0xk and 4 inside nocx-6ek. nocx-k0xk moved to in_progress — quality gates stay active deliberately, since the e2e suite is how the rewrite gets verified and parking it would land the rewrite on a suite nobody can trust. bd dep cycles: clean.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE INVARIANT AS FIRST WRITTEN:
1. 'bd swarm validate max parallelism <= 3' does not work as a gate — it counts closed children in its waves, reporting 7 for nocx-6ek whose real front is 3. The gate is 'bd ready --parent <epic> --exclude-type epic --json | jq length'.
2. blocked is computed, not stored. bd query 'status=blocked' returns nothing while bd stats counts 23. You cannot set the status, only add the edge that causes it.

NOT DONE HERE: prettier rejects AGENTS.md and docs/vision.md, but it rejected both on main too — root-level files are outside every format gate, which is nocx-0fx. Reformatting them here would bury a 94-line docs change under a whole-file reflow. Left for nocx-0fx.
close_reason: Done. bd ready --exclude-type epic -u returns 7 issues across 4 active tracks, down from 68. Every active epic's front is <= 3 (6ek 3, k0xk 3, 8v51 1, v1pr 0), no epic appears as workable, no cycles. AGENTS.md documents the four invariants and vision.md section 0 states the freeze and the active tracks. Shipped in 4da1738.

title: [epic] Quality gates, test infrastructure and operability
description:
The backlog had no milestone for the work that makes the project verifiable and operable, so 13 tasks sat unparented and invisible to any roadmap view. This epic is that milestone.

Scope: the e2e suite and its rot (13 tests fail on main and Playwright is not in the per-commit gate), Go and vitest flakes, CI on PRs and branch protection, files that sit outside every format/lint gate, the pre-commit hook checking the wrong snapshot, the headless devharness, mutation-testing evaluation, and transport runtime modes (verbose auth logging, rate-limited rejections).

Not features. This is the epic that decides whether any other epic can be trusted when it says it is done.

DONE WHEN: the full local gate and CI agree, the e2e suite is green and in the gate, and no source file is outside a format/lint gate.
close_reason:
Split, not abandoned. Same reason as nocx-6ek: this was an area, not a deliverable.

It held 17 children spanning e2e rot, CI configuration, formatting gates, mutation testing and transport logging — work with four different owners and four different definitions of done. Under the owner's rule that an epic is handed to one person whole, this was unassignable, and in practice it was being cherry-picked one bead at a time.

The 13 open children moved to four finishable epics: nocx-rdkh the test suite is green and stays green (nocx-bw2, nocx-qkp, nocx-9ci, nocx-heq, nocx-epm, nocx-zaj), nocx-xx56 a PR shows a required green check (nocx-q36, nocx-63l), nocx-ckoy gate coverage (nocx-0fx, nocx-4iy, nocx-5vi, nocx-u4b), nocx-d1zq transport runtime modes (nocx-772). Nothing was dropped.

Its two closed process children stay here as the record of why the backlog is shaped the way it is: nocx-k0xk.1 (backlog sequencing) and nocx-lg6r / nocx-mqav (the roadmap page, closed won't-do).

title: TABS-C: Settings as a dedicated tab — Warp-style two-pane, Cmd+comma, deep links
description:
Settings becomes a dedicated tab, as in Warp.

- SettingsContent implementing TabContent; singleton registered at the composition root.
- The activity-bar gear changes from action:panel to opening the singleton tab; Cmd+, opens or focuses the same tab.
- Width-responsive two-pane layout: rail clamp(240px, 28vw, 360px) with search, section list, modified-only filter and count; content column scrolls INDEPENDENTLY. Narrow viewport collapses the rail to a category picker.
- The rail is structurally PERMANENT. With one declared section it renders one item and looks sparse — accepted. Count-driven appearance is REJECTED: four more declarations are already filed and unblocked (nocx-8yg.5/.6/.7 and copy-on-select), so a count mode would be exercised for weeks and then rot, and the screen would change shape as the product grows.
- Deep link: opens or focuses the tab, clears a hiding filter, scrolls the row into view, focuses the control, briefly highlights it.
- Inactive Settings stays mounted, so query, section and scroll survive tab switches.

This is what fixes the reported defect. The panel could never host this screen: #sidebar is 240px with overflow:hidden (style.css:701-708), .st-view adds 16px 24px padding leaving 192px, and .st-label-col is flex: 0 0 200px (style.css:1507) — a fixed column wider than its container, so the control column is pushed out and clipped.

Depends on TABS-B (the seam) and SETTINGS-4 (the generated state UX it hosts).

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md Part C.
close_reason:
Accepted at c30cea5 with two gaps recorded as follow-up beads rather than glossed over. The reported defect is fixed: settings no longer live in the 240px panel where .st-label-col (flex: 0 0 200px) overflowed 192px of content width and the control column was clipped by overflow:hidden. SettingsContent implements TabContent, is registered as a singleton surface at the composition root, the activity-bar gear switched from action:'panel' to opening that tab, and Cmd/Ctrl+, opens or focuses it. Two-pane layout with an independently scrolling content column. My carry-forward was respected: rerenderRow resolves rows via getElementById rather than interpolating a key into a CSS selector, which matters because encodeURIComponent leaves '.' unescaped.

GAP 1 (follow-up filed): the integration tests the brief listed were not written — singleton dedup, Cmd+, focus from alternate-screen state, deep-link reveal-and-focus, and the rest. Coverage gap, not a defect; the gate is green.

GAP 2 (follow-up filed): the modified-only filter is absent because 'overridden' does not exist on this branch — it lives on the settings branch. That is a consequence of how I sequenced the work, not a worker error, and it becomes possible after integration.

COORDINATOR FIX: while repairing a truncated SVG string the worker substituted a Feather 'sun' glyph for the activity-bar cog — a silent visual regression that only the diff caught. The original settings cog is restored and the icon line is now identical to origin/main.

Gate on the combined tree (TABS-C plus the wterm removal): prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 427 passed (22 files), gofumpt clean, go test -race clean.

title: TABS-B: TabContent seam with cancellable lifecycle; extract TerminalContent; delete managerView
description:
Introduce the TabContent seam and move terminal machinery behind it. Tab remains a SINGLE class with NO subclasses.

Interfaces (design section B.4):
  TabContent  { mount(target, host, signal): Promise<void>; viewportChanged(v: ContentViewport): void; focus(): void; dispose(): void }
  TabHost     { setTitle(t); requestAttention(); requestClose() }
  ContentViewport { width; height; devicePixelRatio }

- TerminalContent takes renderer, session, editor, shellTarget, scrollback, ledger, inputState, _markers, cols/rows, resizeTimer, _cwd, _host, _lastExitCode, _bufferType.
- Connections migrates onto the seam. managerView is DELETED — no shim. With it go the early return in Tab.start() (284-290) and isManager in activate() (1096).
- requestAttention() not setActivity(boolean): activation clears activity today (tabs.ts:171), so content reports an event and chrome derives the boolean.
- setBufferType is NOT on the host. It toggles global app layout on alt-screen (tabs.ts:1050), which is not tab chrome.
- The host is scoped to one mounted tab and INERT after disposal.

Lifecycle guarantees (B.6): mount at most once; dispose idempotent; dispose cancels an in-flight mount via the AbortSignal; host callbacks inert after disposal; focus only after successful mount or safely queued; defined mount-failure policy; inactive content STAYS MOUNTED until closed.

Geometry (B.5): placement measures and pushes the CSS-pixel rectangle; the renderer converts it to cols/rows from real cell metrics; TerminalContent owns PTY resize policy and keeps its debounce. Content NEVER interprets container geometry itself. Coalesce observer callbacks per animation frame; no callback before mount; replay the latest viewport after async mount; nothing after disposal; never send a zero rectangle to a hidden tab; deliver the real rectangle before focus on activation.

Identity (B.7): branded strings SurfaceType and SingletonKey, REGISTERED at the composition root, not generated. Symbols are rejected — restore (nocx-8yg.3) and deep links need identity that survives a restart. TabManager compares optional singleton keys and never asks whether content is Settings.

View-tab policies become model state, not comments (B.8). Four sites assume every tab is a terminal: getTabs() substituting Terminal (861-863), closing the last tab spawning a terminal (1077-1079), Cmd+1..9 addressing all tabs (1172-1177), and _initialTabReady gating updater health via main.ts:168 (847-851). THE LAST ONE IS THE TRAP: application health means "the initial TERMINAL renderer mounted and the PTY opened" and must stay owned by TerminalContent — do not redefine it as "the first tab mounted". View tabs are not restored, and have no cwd, exit code, activity bell or SSH badge.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md sections B.2, B.4-B.8.
close_reason:
Accepted at e0d0a49 after one rejected round. The acceptance question — who calls viewportChanged — now answers correctly: tabs.ts:238 delivers from the presentation layer, and 'presentation layer calls viewportChanged on pane resize' fails if it stops. Verified rather than taken on report: terminal-content.ts now holds zero ResizeObserver and zero getBoundingClientRect and calls renderer.fitViewport instead; TerminalRenderer gained fitViewport as the missing entry point the previous worker had correctly identified; Tab owns the pane and observes it with per-rAF coalescing, equal-rect suppression, mount/dispose gating, zero-rect rejection and post-mount replay, each with a named test. XtermRenderer reads real cell metrics from the same internal render-service dimensions FitAddon uses — a single narrowed cast with structural access and a .xterm-char-measure-element fallback, so an internal shape change degrades instead of breaking.

Coordinator fixes: the worker reported 'format/lint/typecheck clean' but prettier --check failed on tabs.test.ts and eslint flagged two unused eslint-disable directives. Fixed in that file only. That is the third gate claim on this programme that did not match the tree.

Also delivered by the earlier round and kept: TabContent/TabHost seam, cancellable lifecycle with AbortSignal and inert host, TerminalContent and ConnectionsContent, managerView deleted outright, branded SurfaceType/SingletonKey, restoreDescriptor as model state, application health still owned by TerminalContent.ready.

Gate: prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 427 passed (22 files), gofumpt clean, go test -race clean.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE BLOCKER found by coordinator review of commit 21fd7f6 — the B.5 geometry authority is a facade.

viewportChanged() at terminal-content.ts:534 is a no-op: it stores the value and returns, and its own comment says "The renderer observes its own container for resize". Its ONLY non-test call site anywhere is terminal-content.ts:517 — TerminalContent replaying to itself. Nothing calls it from outside.

ResizeObserver and getBoundingClientRect appear ONLY in terminal-content.ts. tab-strip.ts and tabs.ts contain neither, so the presentation layer measures nothing and delivers nothing.

Content therefore still interprets its own container geometry, which B.5 forbids ("Content MUST NOT interpret container geometry itself"), and the placement layer does not hold the authority the extraction exists to give it. nocx-d3q depends on exactly this, so shipping as-is means reopening the seam later — the outcome the design was ordered to prevent.

An unused no-op typechecks and breaks no test, which is why the gate is green and an interface-level check passes. It is only caught by asking who CALLS it.

Revision pass must: have the presentation layer measure the allocated rectangle and push ContentViewport down; remove ResizeObserver/getBoundingClientRect from TerminalContent; leave the renderer authoritative only for converting the given rectangle into cols/rows via cell metrics; implement the delivery rules (no callback before mount, coalesce per animation frame, replay the latest after async mount, silence after disposal, never a zero rectangle to a hidden tab, real rectangle before focus on activation).

The worker disclosed none of this — its worker_done never mentioned having done TABS-B at all.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
COORDINATOR CORRECTION — retracting part of my previous comment on this bead.

My previous comment ended with "The worker disclosed none of this — its worker_done never
mentioned having done TABS-B at all." Both halves of that are FALSE, and I retract them.

What actually happened: TABS-B was a separately dispatched task (task_62d626db8749) with its own
worker (pane term_db671041), created by someone other than me. It sent a proper worker_done which
disclosed the gap explicitly and gave the technical reason I had missed:

  "Renderer-facing viewport fitting (fit()) is not implemented: the renderer API has no method
   for external viewport delivery; viewportChanged stores and replays the value but relies on the
   renderer's internal ResizeObserver."

I never read that report. My wave-1 supervisor looped check --wait exactly twice because I assumed
two workers were in flight; five had been dispatched, so three reports sat unread. The skill
warns about precisely this: check --wait returns one message at a time, so loop once per worker
that may finish.

The technical finding stands and is unchanged: the geometry authority is not implemented, content
still measures its own container, and nocx-d3q depends on the authority being real. What changes
is the cause and therefore the fix. The blocker is that TerminalTerminalRenderer has no entry
point accepting an externally supplied rectangle, so the revision must extend
frontend/src/renderers/types.ts with a fit-to-viewport method, implement it for xterm, and report
honestly what wterm can honour (see nocx-au6, which already records TerminalRenderer advertising
capabilities wterm lacks). The revision brief has been amended with this.

Also retracted: the same false "beyond its assigned scope" attribution appears in the commit
messages of 608ad61 (settings branch) and 21fd7f6 (tabs branch). Both were normal assigned tasks,
not scope overruns. The messages will be corrected at the integration step — not now, because
workers are actively editing both worktrees and amending would run the pre-commit hook over a
tree mid-edit.

One more thing I failed to do: worker term_aa01bb19 (SETTINGS-2, task_cff7ab6269c5) sent an
escalation, "Blocked: settings.test.ts needs one-line change". That is exactly the tsc --noEmit
break I later found and fixed myself. It asked and I never answered, because I was not reading the
mail. The fix is in; the process failure is mine.

title: TABS-A: horizontal TabStrip presentation port — TabManager stops owning tab DOM
description:
Extract ALL tab chrome and DOM placement out of TabManager and Tab into a TabStrip presentation port. Ship the horizontal implementation, reproducing current behaviour exactly.

Why now and not in the placement epic: TabManager constructs the tab-list container itself (tabs.ts:808) and directly reorders button DOM (tabs.ts:1127). That is precisely the coupling nocx-d3q.1 exists to remove. Leaving it would make the placement epic refactor what this epic just built.

- Tab becomes state + lifecycle. It does NOT own tab-button DOM.
- TabStrip creates, places and styles chrome and emits intents: activate, close, new-tab, reorder.
- TabManager owns the ordered tab model and activation rules and consumes intents.
- The click/close/middle-click/dragstart/dragend/dragover/drop wiring currently exists in TWO near-identical copies (newManagerTab 937-969, createTab 1006-1040). It ends up in ONE place.
- Keyboard and ARIA belong to the port and are done HERE, not retrofitted: roving tabindex, Left/Right horizontal, Up/Down vertical, Home/End, focus-visible, stable tab<->tabpanel relationship, and a recorded decision on whether drag-reorder gets a keyboard equivalent. The tab button is a div today (tabs.ts:64).
- Adopt MRU activation from Orca: closing the active tab activates the PREVIOUSLY ACTIVE tab, not the visual neighbour as tabs.ts:1086-1088 does.

Do NOT introduce TabContent or Settings in this task. Tab still holds terminal machinery temporarily.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md section B.3.
close_reason: Landed as 6031e89 on shady2k/tab-presentation-foundation. All tab chrome and DOM placement extracted into a TabStrip port with HorizontalTabStrip as the first implementation; Tab publishes display state via a TabView contract + onDisplayChange and no longer touches the tab button; TabManager consumes activate/close/new-tab/reorder intents. Verified by diff: the click/close/middle-click/drag wiring is now zero copies in tabs.ts and one in tab-strip.ts (it was two), managerView is untouched so the follow-up nocx-hklg has a clean base, MRU close activates the previously-active tab, and ARIA role=tablist/role=tab/aria-selected/aria-controls plus roving tabindex are in the port. tabs.ts loses 135 net lines. Gate verified independently: prettier/eslint/tsc clean, 421 tests in 22 files, including 25 tab-strip tests with zero terminal machinery — a layer that was impossible before the split. Not exercised, and the worker said so unprompted: native browser drag, focus-visible styling, real layout measurement.

title: SETTINGS-2: unified control-plane dispatcher — retire the two-listener / 100000-ID-offset workaround
description:
One control-plane dispatcher owning request-ID allocation, pending-request correlation, notification routing, disconnect/reconnect behaviour and typed subscribe/unsubscribe.

Today WSClient (ipc.ts) and ProfileClient (profiles.ts) BOTH listen to every message on the same socket, and ProfileClient starts its IDs at 100000 to dodge collisions. Its own comment (profiles.ts:184-188) states the failure: "an ID collision would make one client swallow the other response, causing the form to never open." A third listener for settings notifications makes this worse.

The disjoint ID ranges are DELETED, not preserved (AGENTS.md: no compatibility shims).

No settings notification in this task. Behaviour is unchanged; this is the seam only.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md section A.3.
close_reason: Verified at commit 608ad61, not from the report. dispatcher.ts:60 holds the only addEventListener('message') in the frontend; ProfileClient has zero references to addEventListener/onmessage/rawSocket, so it no longer touches the socket at all, and '100000' appears nowhere. The two-listener arrangement and the ID-offset workaround are deleted rather than shimmed, as AGENTS.md requires. Reconnect is real (_reconnectTimer, rejectAllPending('ws closed') on close, explicit close()); subscriptions are typed (Map<string, Set<NotificationHandler>>) with separate lifecycle subscribers. Worker reported a scoped gate of 92/92; the coordinator's full-tree gate is green after fixing the tsc break it had escalated about. Delivered by a dedicated worker on task_cff7ab6269c5 — my earlier note calling this out-of-scope overrun was wrong.

title: SETTINGS-3: settings.changed broadcast + connection registry + frontend SettingsObserver
description:
Backend-originated settings.changed {revision, keys} over the JSON-RPC control plane. Precedent: the exit notification is already a method without an id (ipc.ts:443).

- Emitted ONLY after the store operation succeeded — committed state, not write intent.
- Emitted by the settings application service after mutation, NOT by each WebSocket handler, so set/reset/secret/import/migration cannot diverge.
- Plural keys so batch operations do not storm.
- Broadcast to all connected clients: the server tracks per-session subscribers only today, so this needs a connection registry with safe unregister.
- Client treats it as invalidation: expected successor revision -> refresh; gap -> full snapshot; reconnect -> full snapshot; duplicate/older -> ignore. Refetching the whole small snapshot is correct at this scale.
- Secret changes may name the key (secretExists already exposes presence) but never carry a value.

A frontend-only event bus is rejected: it leaves every client except the writer stale and creates a second owner of a truth the backend owns (the nocx-aok failure mode).

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md section A.4.
close_reason: Verified against the diff and a coordinator-run gate, not the report. Emission is centralised on the Registry via a staged commit (prepareCommit captures {revision, notifier, keys}; finishCommit fires after the mutex is released), so a future mutation path cannot forget to publish — this was the explicit requirement, and it is met structurally rather than by convention. Emission is strictly post-persistence: writeDoc must return nil before revision++ and before the notifier runs; TestSettingsChanged_FailedMutationEmitsNothing covers the negative. Connection registry behind connsMu with registerConn paired to a deferred unregisterConn, so a client leaves the broadcast set on every exit path; TestSettingsChanged_DisconnectedClientNotLeaked covers it. settings.changed carries {revision, keys} only — TestSettingsChanged_SecretValueNotInNotification serialises the whole notification and asserts the value is absent while the key is present, matching the design decision exactly. SettingsObserver carries no values and implements successor/gap/duplicate-or-older plus the in-memory revision reset on reconnect. Gate: gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test -race all clean; prettier/eslint/tsc clean; vitest 449 passed across 23 files — matching the worker's claim, which was accurate this time.

title: SETTINGS-1: settings.getSnapshot — values + overridden + revision (retires getAll)
description:
Replace settings.getAll with settings.getSnapshot returning { values, overridden: string[], revision: number }.

- values: effective non-secret values (as today).
- overridden: non-secret keys that have a STORED override. This is the fact the wire currently drops; export/import (nocx-6ek.3) needs it or an exported profile silently pins every default.
- revision: monotonic per backend instance, in-memory, NOT persisted. Bumped only after a successful set/reset/secretSet/secretDelete.

Secret keys are absent from BOTH values and overridden — otherwise the snapshot becomes an existence oracle. Presence stays only in settings.secretExists.

Rejected alternative: per-key {value, source}. "source" invites profiles/policies/workspace/env inheritance that do not exist. A membership set states exactly what the registry knows.

Also fixes nocx-q07f in the same code path: saveSetting must write the saved value into this.values before rerenderRow, and must NOT discard the user input on a validation failure.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md sections A.1, A.2.
close_reason: Landed as fb90d47 on shady2k/settings-state-contract. settings.getAll replaced by settings.getSnapshot returning {values, overridden[], revision}; getAll deleted, not aliased. Secret-class keys absent from BOTH values and overridden, pinned by tests at the registry (TestGetSnapshot_ExcludesSecrets) and the transport boundary (TestSettingsGetSnapshot_ContainsNoSecret). overridden is built from membership in the stored-override map, so it is provenance rather than a value-vs-default comparison. revision is in-memory and deliberately not persisted — settingsDoc has no revision field; commitNonSecret/commitWithRefs write to the store first and only bump on success, so a failed write advances nothing. Reviewed against the acceptance criteria by reading the diff, not the report. Gate verified independently by the coordinator: gofumpt clean, golangci-lint clean, go test -race all packages, prettier/eslint/tsc clean, 397 tests in 21 files.

title: [epic] Authoritative settings state and propagation
description:
Authoritative settings state: a snapshot contract that carries provenance, one control-plane dispatcher, and backend-originated change notifications.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md (Part A).

The settings screen is generated from typed declarations (nocx-9m5/nocx-1ei) and that invariant is binding: no literal setting key ever appears in the frontend.

DONE WHEN: the settings snapshot carries provenance and a revision; one control-plane dispatcher owns request IDs and notification routing; a backend-originated settings.changed reaches every connected client after — and only after — a successful write; and the generated screen shows Customized and Reset from provenance, with no literal setting key anywhere in the frontend.
close_reason:
Epic complete: all four tasks verified against the diff and a coordinator-run gate rather than the worker reports. nocx-r2hf (settings.getSnapshot with provenance and an in-memory revision; getAll deleted, no alias; secrets absent from values and overridden with a Go test), nocx-8q9b (one control-plane dispatcher; the two-listener arrangement and the 100000-ID offset deleted rather than shimmed; real reconnect and typed subscriptions), nocx-t7uh (generated state UX from bucket-1 declarations only, with no literal setting key in the frontend), nocx-lsws (settings.changed broadcast emitted from a single staged-commit point strictly after successful persistence, connection registry with deferred unregister, SettingsObserver carrying no values). Defects fixed along the way: nocx-q07f, nocx-jwkw. Branch shady2k/settings-state-contract at fb90d47, 608ad61, e70b83f; final gate gofumpt/golangci-lint/go test -race clean, prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 449 passed across 23 files.

nocx-3cc was re-parented out of this epic to nocx-pxq (Epic: Terminal core), where its load-bearing half belongs: it needs a foreground-process lookup on the PTY fd via TIOCGPGRP in internal/pty, plus a control-plane identity message and per-program grant state. It is a security feature, not settings-state foundation. nocx-pxq already depends on this epic, which is what it was actually waiting for.

NOT merged: integration with the tab branch and the merge to main are separate steps. The commit message of 608ad61 wrongly attributes SETTINGS-2/SETTINGS-4 to a scope overrun by the SETTINGS-1 worker; they were separately dispatched tasks. Rewording failed because the pre-commit hook regenerates the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl, so a reworded commit conflicts with its successor; the correction goes in the PR description instead.

title: [epic] Tab presentation and content foundation
description:
Tab is a single class with NO subclasses. Chrome and DOM placement move behind a TabStrip port; terminal machinery moves behind a TabContent seam; managerView is deleted outright.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md (Part B and C).

Tabby (~/repos/tabby) solves this by inheritance and its BaseTabComponent has accumulated getRecoveryToken/getCurrentProcess no-ops for non-terminal tabs to override. Orca (~/repos/orca) solves it by data modelling with serializable string content types. We follow Orca.

DONE WHEN: Tab owns neither tab-button DOM nor terminal machinery; managerView no longer exists and nothing asks a tab which kind it is; a fake TabContent can be mounted, resized and disposed with no PTY; closing a tab mid-mount opens no session; and Settings and Connections are both content on the same seam.
acceptance_criteria: Tab owns neither tab-button DOM nor terminal machinery; managerView no longer exists and nothing asks a tab which kind it is; a fake TabContent can be mounted, resized and disposed with no PTY; closing a tab mid-mount opens no session; and Settings and Connections are both content on the same seam.
close_reason:
Epic complete: 6/6. The reported defect is fixed and the foundation under it is real.

nocx-u5og — horizontal TabStrip presentation port; TabManager stopped owning tab DOM, the duplicated button wiring collapsed to one site, roving tabindex and ARIA landed, MRU close adopted from Orca.
nocx-hklg — TabContent seam with a cancellable lifecycle, TerminalContent and ConnectionsContent extracted, managerView deleted, branded surface/singleton identities, and after one rejected round the B.5 geometry authority made real (TerminalRenderer gained fitViewport; content stopped measuring its own container).
nocx-h4e2 — Settings became a dedicated tab. The panel could never have hosted it: 240px with overflow:hidden, 192px of content width, and a .st-label-col fixed at 200px.
nocx-wbtv — modified-only filter surfaced in the rail, driven from provenance rather than value comparison, with state kept single-owner.
nocx-v98h — narrow-viewport layout, keyed off the ContentViewport pushed by the presentation layer rather than a media query, because Settings lives in a pane whose width is not the window's.
nocx-wm1o — 9 integration tests through TabManager.openTab covering the seams the component tests cannot reach.

Two defects in this epic's own work were caught only later and are worth recording: the activity indicator was permanently lost for backgrounded tabs because setActive never repainted (found by e2e, invisible to 494 unit tests and to my diff review), and the geometry authority shipped once as a facade before the revision round.

Owed: visual confirmation of the responsive layout at several widths. jsdom cannot exercise real layout.

Not merged to main — the integration branch is the deliverable.

title: [bug] Successful settings save visually reverts: saveSetting never updates this.values before rerenderRow
description:
frontend/src/settings.ts:319-330 — saveSetting() awaits client.setSetting(), clears/sets this.errors, then calls rerenderRow(key). It never writes the new value into this.values.

rerenderRow (settings.ts:355-362) rebuilds the row via renderControl(), whose control renderers read this.values[decl.key] — renderToggle uses `input.checked = !!this.values[decl.key]` (L234), renderText/renderNumber/renderSelect go through displayValue(this.values[decl.key], decl).

So after a SUCCESSFUL save the control re-renders from the pre-save value and visually snaps back, while the value is actually persisted. Toggle, text, number and select are all affected.

Secondary defect in the same method: on validation FAILURE the rerender also discards the value the user typed, so they cannot correct it — they have to retype from scratch.

Found by a Codex design review of the settings surface, then verified by reading the code. Independent of the settings-as-a-tab work: this is wrong today, in the panel.
close_reason: Fixed in fb90d47 alongside nocx-r2hf, same code path. A successful save now writes the value into the authoritative values map before rerenderRow, so the control no longer rebuilds from the pre-save value and snaps back. A rejected value is preserved in a separate draftValues map read through an effectiveValue() helper, so the user can correct their input without the draft polluting authoritative state. Two regression tests added; the worker disclosed that it implemented before testing and verified both tests fail without the fix.

title: Brainstorming: settings surface — panel vs modal
close_reason: Brainstorm complete. Settled: settings become a dedicated tab (Warp-style), Tab stays a single class with no subclasses, chrome and DOM placement move behind a TabStrip port, terminal machinery behind a TabContent seam. Reference survey of Warp/Tabby/Orca and an adversarial Codex review are folded into .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md. Work now lives in epics nocx-8v51 (settings state) and nocx-v1pr (tab foundation); nocx-d3q depends on both.

title: TABS-3: vertical tab panel, Warp-style
description:
The vertical mode itself, implemented against the TABS-1 seam.

From the Warp reference the owner supplied: search over tabs, a per-row icon, title plus a subtitle (cwd or branch), a status indicator (e.g. the warning marker Warp shows on a running process), and a + in the panel header.

The tabs get their own permanent slot at the left edge. They must NOT be a view inside the activity-bar panel — that is the flaw in the current implementation, where selecting Connections replaces the tab list and the tabs disappear.

What 557e87d already built and can be salvaged: the row markup (title span, close button, activation click) and the tm.onTabsChanged subscription in main.ts. What it lacks: search, icon, subtitle, status, and a slot of its own.
close_reason:
Landed at e772944, verified against the diff and a coordinator-run gate.

The design bet held: the TabStrip port was NOT reopened. When the presentation port was extracted, the whole justification was that a second placement would plug in without reshaping the interface — and it did. Greping the diff for interface changes in tab-strip.ts returns nothing, so the escalation path the brief provided went unused.

The window-chrome question — the part the brief called non-obvious — is answered IN THE CODE, not only in a report. Horizontal placement makes the strip the macOS title bar (.tabbar carries --wails-draggable: drag plus 78px left padding for the inset traffic lights); a vertical strip cannot, because the traffic lights are horizontal. So #tabbar stays at the top as a minimal drag bar keeping both properties, and the vertical strip becomes a side panel alongside #body with no-drag.

tab-strip.test.ts goes 25 -> 51, verified by counting it( blocks. The 26 new tests run with zero terminal machinery, which is what that isolation layer was built for.

Gate: prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 520 passed (25 files), gofumpt clean, go test -race clean — matching the worker's claim exactly.

Provenance worth recording: written by one session interrupted before it reported, then reviewed by a second that made NO changes of its own and disclosed that ('git status --porcelain is clean'). Verified: no new commit, clean tree. It reviewed rather than rewrote, and said so instead of presenting the predecessor's work as its own.

Unblocks nocx-d3q.2 — the placement setting now has two implementations to select between, which is why it was scheduled after this.

title: TABS-2: tab placement setting (horizontal default | vertical), persisted
description:
A user-visible setting choosing tab placement. Default horizontal — the layout on main today, so a fresh install is unchanged. Persisted across restarts through the storage capability work (see the persistence epic nocx-6ek); do not invent a second config store.

Acceptance: toggling the setting switches placement without a restart; the default on a clean profile is horizontal.
close_reason:
Landed at ad64a44 after two coordinator fixes, and the first was severe.

Delivered: one MustRegisterSelect in internal/settings (section Interface, default horizontal), replaceStrip on TabManager, and live application through SettingsObserver — changing the setting repositions the tabs with no restart. Scheduled last on purpose, because a setting choosing between implementations needs both to exist and VerticalTabStrip landed one commit earlier.

FIX 1 — the worker DELETED 'await client.connect(port, host, token)' from main.ts and nothing replaced it. The WebSocket was never opened; the app would not have worked at all. Restored, before the first RPC, since connect must precede getSnapshot.

The tell was in the worker's own report and it waved it away: it described the two eslint findings as 'pre-existing warnings'. They were neither. They were ERRORS, and 'token'/'host' were unused precisely because their consumer had been removed — restoring connect cleared them with no other change. What did NOT catch it: tsc was clean, all 526 unit tests passed (nothing type-checks or unit-tests startup wiring), and the e2e suite runs on a different branch that still had the call. This is the second time on this programme that a lint finding a worker dismissed was the visible edge of a real defect.

FIX 2 — the placement key is now named in the composition root instead of inferred. The worker matched the declaration by section 'Interface' plus control 'select', which reads key-free but resolves to whichever select comes first in declaration order; nocx-8yg.6 (colour schemes) is filed and would add exactly such a select to Interface, breaking placement silently. The generated-screen invariant is about the SCREEN — settings.ts and settings-content.ts still contain zero setting keys, verified by grep, so a new setting still costs one Go call and no frontend change. A composition root acting on one specific setting is a consumer, and a consumer must name what it consumes.

Gate: prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 526 passed (26 files), and the pre-commit hook re-ran it on commit.

title: TABS-1: extract tab rendering behind an interface — TabManager stops owning its DOM placement
description:
ADDITION (restore of the tab bar, nocx-x4z): 557e87d added three members to TabManager purely to feed the hand-rolled sidebar list — getTabs(), findTab(id) and the optional onTabsChanged hook (fired at tabs.ts:1105, 1133, 1172). With the sidebar list removed, getTabs and findTab have zero callers and onTabsChanged has no subscriber.

They were deliberately left in place rather than deleted in the restore commit: this task owns the rendering seam and will either adopt them as the seam's accessor surface or delete them. Do not leave them as-is — AGENTS.md forbids dead code, and an unused public API invites misuse.
close_reason:
Landed at 715e477. The seam half was already delivered by the TabStrip port; this closes the second requirement in the bead body, which had never been done: getTabs(), findTab(id) and onTabsChanged had zero callers outside tabs.ts, and onTabsChanged was fired from three sites with no subscriber. All three deleted plus the invocation sites, nine lines.

The worker argued the choice instead of assuming it, and the argument is sound: the port is a push model — addTab/removeTab/reorder/setActive push state in, intents push events out — so getTabs and onTabsChanged were coarser duplicates of what the port already provides, and findTab leaked Tab past the TabView abstraction that exists to hide it. It also checked whether the coming vertical strip would want an observer hook and concluded the port's intents already cover it. Tests that used findTab(1) now address tabs the way production does.

Scoped verification green (tsc/eslint/prettier/vitest 53); whole-project typecheck correctly NOT run because a neighbour worker was mid-edit, and the worker said so. Coordinator's full gate on the settled tree: prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 494 passed (25 files), gofumpt and go test -race clean.

title: [epic] Configurable tab placement: horizontal by default, vertical Warp-style as an option
description:
Tab placement is a setting, not a fixed layout.

Background, as the code stands: commit 557e87d removed the horizontal tab bar element from frontend/index.html and moved the tab list into the sidebar as a hand-rolled vertical list, as a side effect of unrelated SSH/vault work. The tab bar has since been restored on main, so horizontal is the current behaviour and the default below.

Decision (2026-07-25): tab placement becomes a user setting.

• Default: horizontal, along the top — the layout on main today.
• Option: vertical, down the left edge, styled after Warp — search over tabs, per-row icon, title plus a subtitle (cwd / branch), a status indicator, and a + in the panel header.
• The activity bar does NOT move. It stays on the left in both modes. A setting that relocates a second control breaks spatial memory, and the crowding argument does not hold: the activity-bar panel is collapsible and normally collapsed, so the usual vertical layout is two bands (icons | tabs | panes), which is what VS Code does. If the left edge does turn out to feel cramped once the vertical mode exists, the options are (a) make the activity-bar position its own independent setting, as VS Code does, or (b) follow Warp and drop the vertical strip entirely, moving its icons into the title bar. Choosing between those now, without a mockup, would be speculation — YAGNI.
• In vertical mode the tabs get their OWN permanent slot. They must not share the activity-bar panel: when the panel hosts them, selecting Connections replaces the tab list and the tabs vanish from the screen.

Architectural constraint (AGENTS.md, interface-first): TabManager must stop deciding where it draws itself. The TabStrip presentation port extracted in nocx-u5og is that seam; this epic adds the vertical implementation behind it. Do not keep a hidden element alive to satisfy a constructor.

DONE WHEN: tab placement is a persisted setting; horizontal and vertical are two implementations of the same TabStrip port; switching placement applies without a restart; and e2e covers both placements.
acceptance_criteria: tab placement is a persisted setting; horizontal and vertical are two implementations of the same TabStrip port; switching placement applies without a restart; and e2e covers both placements.
close_reason:
Epic complete: 4/4. Tab placement is configurable, persisted and applied live.

d3q.1 — the seam was delivered early by the TabStrip port; what remained here was the dead accessor surface (getTabs, findTab, onTabsChanged with zero callers), deleted with an argument rather than on assumption.
d3q.3 — VerticalTabStrip, built against the existing port WITHOUT reopening it. That was the design bet when the port was pulled forward into the foundation epic, and it held.
d3q.2 — one MustRegisterSelect in Go, selection at the composition root, live swap through SettingsObserver. Two coordinator fixes were needed: the worker had deleted the app's WebSocket connect call, and had inferred the setting by section+control in a way that nocx-8yg.6 would have silently broken.
d3q.4 — e2e across both placements, 34 passed 2 skipped 0 failed.

Worth recording: the vertical strip shipped with the same setActive repaint bug the horizontal one had been fixed for, because a clean auto-merge combined a fix on one side with a new implementation on the other. I found it by reading both implementations after the merge, on the suspicion that a fix applied to one implementation of two does not apply itself to the other. d3q.4's tests now cover that.

title: gutter glyphs never appear after submit: e2e multi-line landmark assertion gets 0, not 1
description:
e2e/command-editor.spec.ts 'a multi-line command is one gutter landmark, not three' fails on every CI run, on both main and pr-11-boundary: after submitting a 3-line command, expect.poll(...).toBe(1) receives 0 — no .nocx-gutter-glyph elements exist at all.

This is a product bug, not test rot. The feature is live: frontend/src/gutter.ts renders .nocx-gutter-glyph (L183, L193), it is styled in frontend/src/style.css (L1236), and the graph shows the wiring intact — Gutter._paint / visibleGlyphs / setRecords driven by CommandLedger (open -> onMarker -> finalizeOpen). Introduced in ec0ab8e, CSS refined in 155262d.

Deliberately NOT fixed by deleting the test (contrast with the sibling submit-button test, which was deleted because 7204aff removed the feature by design). Deleting this one would erase the only evidence of the defect.

Suspects: the command-ledger -> gutter handoff on submit, or a timing/lifecycle issue where glyphs are created and immediately removed. Root cause not yet investigated.

Found while triaging the 13 e2e failures that predate pr-11-boundary (see nocx-bw2).
notes: Still failing as of PR #13 (2026-07-26), in both chromium and webkit: 'command editor (nocx-4ff) › a multi-line command is one gutter landmark, not three', now at e2e/command-editor.spec.ts:62 (it was :73 before PR #12 shifted the file). Confirmed pre-existing and untouched by the ADR-0011 epic — see the baseline comparison recorded on nocx-bw2.

title: frontend build wipes the //go:embed anchor: vite emptyOutDir:true deletes tracked frontend/dist/.gitkeep
description:
frontend/vite.config.ts sets build.emptyOutDir: true, so every frontend build empties frontend/dist/ — including the tracked .gitkeep that 9a4fa72 established as the anchor for //go:embed all:frontend/dist.

This is the mechanism behind nocx-500, not a coincidence: a developer runs the app, the build silently deletes the tracked file, 'git commit -a' carries the deletion, and every clean checkout after that fails at main.go:21 with 'pattern all:frontend/dist: no matching files found'. That is exactly how a0fab46 lost it. Observed again today: running 'wails dev' in the pr-11-boundary worktree deleted the file within minutes of 74aabfe restoring it.

Restoring the file (74aabfe) fixed the symptom only. The anchor has to survive a build.

Options, in order of preference:
1. Add frontend/public/.gitkeep — vite copies publicDir into outDir on every build, so the anchor is recreated after the wipe. No plugin code, idiomatic. Keep the tracked frontend/dist/.gitkeep too, for a fresh clone that has never built.
2. A vite plugin with a closeBundle() hook that rewrites dist/.gitkeep.
3. emptyOutDir: false — rejected: stale hashed assets would accumulate in dist forever.

Acceptance: run a frontend build, confirm 'git status' is clean afterwards.
close_reason: Fixed in c370250 with option 1: frontend/public/.gitkeep, which vite copies into dist after emptyOutDir wipes it. Verified by running the frontend build and confirming frontend/dist/.gitkeep survives and git status stays clean. emptyOutDir left on deliberately (option 3 rejected: stale hashed assets would accumulate). vite.config.ts carries a comment so the empty public/ dir is not mistaken for a stray.

title: e2e suite: 13 tests fail on both main and branch — Playwright is not in the per-commit gate, so the rot went unnoticed
description:
Verified by diffing the failure lists of three CI runs (main 30162745654, pr-11-boundary 30162351263 and 30163136292), not by reading a summary:

- 13 tests fail in ALL THREE runs — this bead.
- 5 fail reproducibly on the branch and never on main — separate merge blockers, under investigation.
- 2 swap places between the two branch runs (enhanced-input.spec.ts:10 and :38, chromium) — genuinely flaky.
- 1 fails on main and passes on the branch (enhanced-input.spec.ts:38 chromium) — further proof the suite flakes in both directions.

The 13, by file:
  activity-bell.spec.ts:12  chromium
  activity.spec.ts:10       webkit
  click-focus.spec.ts:26    chromium, webkit
  clipboard.spec.ts:46      chromium (copy-on-select)
  clipboard.spec.ts:115     chromium (paste)
  command-editor.spec.ts:61 chromium, webkit  -> RESOLVED in c370250 (stale selector, nocx-m7x)
  command-editor.spec.ts:73 chromium, webkit  -> real product bug, split out as nocx-1y8
  enhanced-input.spec.ts:10 webkit
  enhanced-input.spec.ts:38 chromium, webkit
  enhanced-input.spec.ts:61 webkit

So 2 of the 13 are already gone and 2 more are tracked as nocx-1y8; 9 remain untriaged here.

Root enabler unchanged: the pre-commit hook runs vitest, not Playwright. e2e runs only in CI, only on non-draft PRs to main, and main itself never gets a run — so nothing observes the suite between PRs and dead selectors rot unnoticed. Worth considering whether e2e should gate main directly (nocx-q36 made CI the mechanical gate; e2e is inside it but only for non-draft PRs).

Full per-test evidence: .internal/reports/e2e-inventory.md (note its correction header — its own bucketing was wrong in both directions).
notes:
Baseline re-measured 2026-07-26 against PR #13 (ADR-0011 epic, merged as cb4a427). Numbers in this bead's title are stale: it says 13, the last main CI run showed 14, and PR #13 showed 11.

The drop is not this epic fixing anything, and the rise is not a regression — main's last CI run (30162745654, job 89690608774) is at f3088741 from 2026-07-25 15:00, which PREDATES the PR #12 merge that my branch is based on. PR #12 fixed three of the fourteen: 'the submit button is clickable and submits' in both chromium and webkit, and '[chromium] a bell lights the indicator from inside the alternate buffer'. That is the syncAltScreenClass subscription PR #12 restored.

Name-by-name comparison, not counts: every one of PR #13's 11 failures also appears in main's 14. Zero new failure names. So ADR-0011 introduced no e2e regression, and the remaining 11 are the pre-existing rot this bead exists for.

The 11 still red, by area:
- click-focus.spec.ts:26 (chromium + webkit) — click into pane leaves terminal taking keystrokes
- clipboard.spec.ts:46 and :115 (chromium) — copy-on-select, right-click paste
- command-editor.spec.ts multi-line gutter landmark (chromium + webkit) — this is nocx-1y8
- enhanced-input.spec.ts:10, :38, :61 (webkit) and :38 (chromium) — raw routing
- activity.spec.ts:10 (webkit) — background tab activity indicator

Note the line numbers moved between the two runs (command-editor.spec.ts:73 on main vs :62 on the branch), so anyone comparing must match on test NAME, not on file:line. Comparing by line number here produces a false 'new failure'.
close_reason:
Suite is green: 28 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed — from 13 failures on main. Verified TWICE, and the second run mattered.

My first verification attempt failed on the ENVIRONMENT, not the tests: bare 'npx playwright test' goes through the webServer stanza and therefore 'wails dev', which cannot build here (webkit2gtk-4.0 absent) and burned the full 240s timeout. The green run uses the headless devharness path the worker's own config change added — devharness on 127.0.0.1:9876, vite on 5173, NOCX_WS_PORT plus NOCX_WS_TOKEN. Coordinator re-run: 28 passed, 2 skipped in 57.5s. The 2 skipped are chromium-only clipboard specs skipping under webkit by design.

The last remaining failure was NOT a stale test but a PRODUCT bug in the TabStrip port, fixed at 7274968: setActive() toggled .active on the buttons and never repainted, and paintButton gates on !.active, so a backgrounded tab's pending activity indicator stayed hidden — then stuck, because a later bell found _hasActivity already true and no-opped without reaching onDisplayChange. The indicator was permanently lost for that tab, not merely late.

That is the finding worth keeping: it shipped through a green 494-test unit suite AND a diff review in which I closed nocx-u5og as 'verified against the diff'. A DOM paint-ordering defect is invisible to jsdom and to reading a diff. The suite justified itself on its first green day.

Also accepted here: the harness import migration (see nocx-qkp), keyboard-to-PTY wiring in terminal-content.ts, the SHELL-fallback in pty_local.go (independently confirmed on a live box), and the clipboard and click-focus rewrites.

Coordinator hardening at 64ca1b4: workers default to 1, the wails port comes from env, reuseExistingServer is opt-in so a run cannot silently measure a tree it did not build, and e2e/preflight.ts refuses to start below a free-space threshold. Playwright is still NOT in the per-commit gate — that is nocx-63l, gated on the suite being RELIABLY green, which one green day does not prove.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
COORDINATOR CORRECTION — my framing of the resource incident in this bead's close reason, and in commit 64ca1b4, was WRONG on the primary cause.

I attributed the disk exhaustion to concurrent Playwright runs. It was not that. The disk was filled by CRASH DUMPS: WPEWebProcess (the WebKit content process) segfaults on teardown — heap-metadata corruption surfacing in unlink_chunk during __run_exit_handlers, i.e. a free() inside an exit handler on an already-corrupted heap — and each dump was ~5.8 GB. Around 42 such crashes in a day. Chromium produced zero. With single-digit GB free, ONE crash was enough to fill the filesystem; concurrency multiplied the frequency but was never the cause.

The crash is upstream, in a stripped library (no build-id, all frames n/a inside libWPEWebKit), and is not fixable here. It has been made harmless at the host level by capping core-dump size, which leaves the crash and removes the disk collapse.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, and why:

- The port fix (NOCX_WAILS_PORT, and reuseExistingServer becoming opt-in) stands on entirely different grounds. Two runs sharing a hardcoded 34115 with reuse enabled meant the second attached to the first one's app and reported results for a tree it never built. That is a correctness defect, independent of disk.
- workers=1 stands, with a weaker rationale: the disk argument is void, but CPU and memory contention on a shared box is not.
- e2e/preflight.ts stands, also weaker: a 3 GB floor does not stop a 5.8 GB dump written mid-run, but it does stop a run starting on an already-full disk.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE SUITE, and it is the actionable half: a WebKit failure reported as the browser closing unexpectedly may be this teardown crash rather than a test defect, because the assertions have already completed by then. Do not chase it as a product bug without first checking whether the process died on exit. Chromium is the quieter browser for iteration; WebKit stays because nocx-q18's glyph corruption reproduces in WKWebView and not in Chromium.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: adding Playwright retries to absorb these. This epic just replaced duration-waits with condition-waits to make flakes deterministic; blanket retries would hide the next real one. Documenting the signature beats masking it.

title: CI backend job broken since a0fab46: frontend/dist/.gitkeep deleted, //go:embed all:frontend/dist has no match
close_reason: Restored frontend/dist/.gitkeep in 74aabfe. 9a4fa72 made it the //go:embed anchor; a0fab46 deleted it while leaving the .gitignore negation and its explanatory comment in place, so the intent stayed documented and the anchor did not. Verified both directions against a clean git archive export (build fails without it, succeeds with it), then confirmed by CI: the backend job on run 30163136292 went green, having failed on both main and this branch before.

title: Frontend logging seam: log.ts owns the Wails FFI, kills 46 red tests and the JSON.stringify leak idiom
close_reason: frontend/src/log.ts owns the Wails FFI: window.go guard, structured fields, no floating promises; 36 call sites migrated; tabs.test.ts 46/46 green (was fully red); no test needs a logging mock

title: EDITOR-W6: shell token highlighting — the first visible payoff of the migration
description:
The thin slice of visible value that ships WITH the core migration instead of two epics
later. Without it nocx-2gf pays the whole cost of the swap — 102 KB gzip, a rewritten test
surface, a focus seam reworked — and delivers a editor that looks exactly like the old one.

SCOPE, deliberately narrow: purely SYNTACTIC colouring via a read-only CM6 language layer
over StreamLanguage + the shell mode from @codemirror/legacy-modes. Command name, flags,
pipes, redirects, quotes, strings, paths. Local, synchronous, no resolution, no async
sources, no popup, no validation.

NOT in scope, and these are what stay in nocx-w7h because they need in-band answers from
the session's own shell: is this command on PATH, is it an alias or a function, does this
path exist, is this flag real. That split follows the tiers in the epic description —
tokenising is tier 0 and needs nothing; everything semantic needs the shell to answer.

FAIL-SOFT IS AN INVARIANT, not a nicety. Shell syntax is hostile: quoting, $( ), heredocs,
incomplete multiline input. When the tokenizer is unsure it renders PLAIN TEXT and never
renders red, and nothing about highlighting may influence submission. A false alarm at a
prompt costs more than a missing colour. This mirrors the fail-open rule in ADR-0004 §1.

Colours come from the existing theme, not a second palette. Note serializer.ts already
hardcodes Tokyo Night for frozen blocks; do not add a third source of truth for colour —
if a shared theme source is needed, that is a finding to file, not to solve here.

Blocked by EDITOR-W1: there is nothing to decorate until the view exists.
Splits nocx-4ff.22, which keeps the validation half.

title: EDITOR-W1: swap the editor internals to CodeMirror 6
description:
Spec W1. Replace the <textarea> in CommandEditor with an EditorView, preserving every public member except the textarea getter; drop _grow() for a CSS max-height policy. Pin CM6 versions in frontend/package.json. The extension list is a CONSTRUCTOR PARAMETER, not a literal inside the class — that is the whole of what this epic owes the later per-target decoration work.

First rewrite editor.test.ts against the public API: it currently does querySelector('textarea') and pokes .value/.rows/.selectionStart, so it cannot pass unchanged. Red first, then green.

Verify under visibility:hidden — CM6 measures its own layout and a hidden view can cache wrong geometry, while _shownOnce keeps the editor hidden that way for most of its life so the pane does not jump.
acceptance_criteria: Rewritten unit suite green. Caret placement on click, mid-line edit and multiline behave as before. The submit path is byte-identical to before the swap. show()/hide() keep the _shownOnce layout reservation. Editor is correctly sized and focusable on the show following a hide.
notes:
ABSORBED EDITOR-W0 (2026-07-25, owner call): the de-risk spike is removed. Its output was a findings note, not working software, and it meant doing the integration twice — the decision is already made (CM6, ADR-0010 in W7), so there is nothing left for a spike to decide. W1 behind a flag IS the same experiment, except the code survives and tests catch what the spike would have found by hand.

The spike's checks become acceptance criteria here, in this order — they are the risky seams and they are verified FIRST, before the rest of the swap is polished:

1. FOCUS INTERPLAY WITH XTERM. The whole ownership machine is focus-based (tabs.ts:407-417 focus-bounce, :432-467 global keydown redirect) while CM6 manages focus itself. Verify: the bounce still keeps typing in the editor when the editor owns input; clicking the xterm live region still keeps focus there; rootContains() still resolves through CM6's nested DOM at BOTH call sites (:413 and :457-464).
2. KEYMAP PRECEDENCE. CM6's defaultKeymap binds Enter and Escape. Without Prec.highest, Enter inserts a newline and Ctrl-C stops interrupting the shell — a silent regression in the two most-used keys at a prompt. (Detailed in W2; W1 must not ship a state where they are wrong.)
3. IME COMPOSITION. Zero coverage exists today. The document-level keydown redirect can destroy composition state.
4. HIT-TESTING. document.elementFromPoint over the editor card must return the editor, not .xterm-link-layer — this is the nocx-4ff.16 bug and nocx-0oc says the z-index rule it was fixed with is not actually in the stylesheet.
5. GEOMETRY UNDER visibility:hidden. CM6 measures its own layout, and _shownOnce keeps the editor hidden that way for most of its life. Assert correct size and focusability on the show following a hide.
6. WKWEBVIEW, NOT ONLY CHROMIUM. Playwright drives Chromium; the shipping runtime is WKWebView (AD-3). IME and focus findings are either reproduced on the real WebView or explicitly recorded as unverified — not silently assumed.

If any of these turns out to need a different migration shape, that is a finding on nocx-2gf and W1 is re-planned — same outcome the spike would have produced, with working code already in hand.

title: EDITOR-W5: rebuild the test surface (browser mode decision + first IME coverage)
description:
Spec W5. Rewrite the hit-testing assertions in e2e/command-editor.spec.ts that expect elementFromPoint to return a TEXTAREA, plus clipboard.spec.ts:147 and click-focus.spec.ts:37-45 which assume the active element carries .nocx-editor-input and read selectionStart/selectionEnd. Delete the already-dead submit-button test (see nocx-m7x).

jsdom performs no layout, so every CM6 behaviour depending on measurement — caret coordinates, popup placement, wrapping — is untestable there. That forces the nocx-foz decision rather than leaving it implicit.

Add the first IME composition coverage this repo has ever had: the document-level keydown redirect at tabs.ts:432 can destroy composition state silently.
acceptance_criteria: e2e suite green against the new surface. A composition sequence produces the composed text exactly once. nocx-foz closed with a decision either way and its reasoning recorded.

title: STORE-5: settings registry on DocumentStore — the screen is generated
description:
ADR-0011 + nocx-1ei. Replace internal/config's untyped Get(key) (any, error) / Set(key string, value any) bag, which cannot enumerate what settings exist, their types, defaults or validation — and therefore cannot drive a generated screen.

Typed declarations carrying key, default, label, description, section, validation, data class and control kind. Because Go cannot hold differently-typed declarations in one slice directly, expose a non-generic descriptor interface for enumeration alongside typed keys for get/set. Retires the config Stub (nocx-jap), and makes 'Don't show again' on the OSC 52 gate mean what it says (nocx-3cc).

A secret-class setting generates an editor whose operations are set, delete and exists — never get.
acceptance_criteria: The settings screen is rendered from declarations, not hand-maintained. A user decision survives restart. Adding a setting requires touching one declaration site. No secret-class setting exposes a read operation.
close_reason:
STORE-5 landed across three workers: the typed registry (internal/settings), the generated screen (frontend/src/settings.ts), and the wiring (7 JSON-RPC methods in ws.go, composition-root pairing in app.go). internal/config and its untyped Get(key) (any, error) bag are DELETED, not adapted — that retires nocx-jap.

Acceptance checked rather than taken on report. Screen is generated: it switches on decl.control and groups by decl.section, with no literal setting key anywhere, so a new declaration renders with zero frontend change. A decision made in the screen survives restart via DocumentStore. Adding a setting is one MustRegister* call.

No secret-class read exists, structurally: the registry exposes SecretSet/SecretDelete/SecretExists and there is no GetSecret method at all; GetAll skips secret-class keys; Reset refuses them; settings.set rejects a secret key and directs to settings.secretSet; the UI renders configured/not-configured with Replace and Clear rather than an input.

Two worker fixes were rejected and redone: unchecked type assertions had been silenced with 'x, _ := desc.(*settings.Bool)', which relocates the panic into Registry.SetBool (it dereferences b.key with no nil check) instead of removing it — each site now checks ok and returns a self-diagnosing -32603; and the screen stringified unknown values, so a malformed value rendered as literal '[object Object]' into a field the user could save back — values are now narrowed per control kind with a logged fallback.

Remaining OSC 52 work is tracked on nocx-3cc, not silently carried here.

title: EDITOR-W2: keymap at highest precedence
description:
Spec W2. Bind Enter (submit), Shift-Enter (newline), Escape (clear draft without interrupting), Ctrl-C (copy if a selection exists, else clear + actions.cancel()) inside Prec.highest(keymap.of([...])).

CM6's defaultKeymap binds Enter and Escape. Without explicit precedence, Enter inserts a newline and Ctrl-C stops interrupting the shell — a silent regression in the two most-used keys at a prompt.

Handlers must ignore events fired during IME composition.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests assert each binding's decision including the Ctrl-C selection branch. An e2e asserts one submit produces exactly one block. Composition events do not trigger submit, clear or cancel.

title: EDITOR-W0: CM6 de-risk spike (throwaway)
description:
Spec .internal/specs/2026-07-25-editor-core-codemirror6-design.md, W0. Mount a bare CM6 view in the editor slot behind a flag and exercise, in this order: focus interplay with xterm and the focus-bounce (tabs.ts:407-417, :432-467); keymap precedence for Enter/Escape/Ctrl-C; IME composition; copy-on-select; auto-grow; document.elementFromPoint over the editor card.

The ownership machine is entirely focus-based while CM6 manages focus itself — this is the one seam where a surprise changes HOW we migrate, and it is cheapest to find on day one.

Test the real host: the shipping runtime is WKWebView (AD-3) and Playwright drives Chromium, which cannot establish WKWebView IME or focus behaviour. Reproduce on the actual WebView or record as unverified.

One decision only: can a CM6 adapter preserve the current single-target contract? Spike code is deleted, not merged.
acceptance_criteria: A written findings note on nocx-2gf listing every surprise, and that one decision answered. IME and focus findings either reproduced on WKWebView or explicitly marked unverified. Spike code deleted.
close_reason: Removed on owner's call: a throwaway spike duplicates W1's work and decides nothing that is not already decided. Its six verification items became acceptance criteria on EDITOR-W1 (nocx-5ns).

title: STORE-2: DocumentStore capability (atomic JSON + per-module schema version)
description:
ADR-0011. Bounded, human-recoverable configuration as atomic JSON documents — settings, profiles, groups, credential metadata, tab restore. Extract the mechanism currently private inside profile.JSONStore (temp file + rename, 0700 dir, 0600 file) into a capability others use.

Schema versions are PER MODULE, not app-wide: a single version would couple unrelated releases of settings, profiles, conversations and history, and JSON-document migrations have different transactional properties from SQLite ones. Share the migration protocol, not the version.

Note rename-over-path is the same class as nocx-ab4 (atomic write replacing a symlinked target with a regular file) — verify the target cannot be a symlink the user cares about. Also: the rename is not followed by a directory fsync, so 'atomic' is not fully crash-durable today.
acceptance_criteria: Documents are written atomically with correct permissions. Each module declares and migrates its own schema version through a shared protocol. profile.JSONStore uses the capability rather than its own implementation.
close_reason: STORE-2 landed: storage.DocumentStore (Read/Write) owns path, permissions and atomicity; profile.JSONStore uses it and no longer carries its own temp-plus-rename. Both defects the bead recorded are fixed with dedicated tests: the rename is now followed by a directory fsync (TestDocumentStore_DirFsync), and a write refuses a symlinked target rather than replacing it with a regular file (TestDocumentStore_SymlinkRefusal, the nocx-ab4 class). Schema versions are per module through a shared protocol — each module declares its own monotonic version and ordered migrations, DocumentStore stays format-agnostic — with 7 tests including multi-step, non-monotonic and missing-migration cases. The ProfileStore interface was deliberately left intact; splitting it is STORE-4. app.go wiring was unverifiable while STORE-3 was in flight and has now been confirmed: full build clean, go test -race ./... green.

title: STORE-3: SecretStore capability + the Secret type as the boundary
description:
ADR-0011. Authenticators only, in the OS keychain — never a file we write. Domain records carry an opaque SecretID; the secret behind it is reachable only through SecretStore, backend-side.

Overlaps PR11-T7, which introduces the Secret type for VaultSecret. This bead generalises it into a capability with stable SecretID references, which is what PR11-T6 needs to delete the right secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Secrets are addressed by stable SecretID. No API outside internal/credential and internal/ssh can obtain plaintext. A secret cannot be marshalled or logged.
close_reason:
STORE-3 landed: credential.SecretStore (Get/Set/Delete/Exists) addressed by opaque, stable SecretID, backed by the OS keychain. HashKey, KeyHash and the Identity{User: credentialID} convention are deleted outright — grep confirms zero non-test references. profile.Credential now carries SecretID and PassphraseSecretID as opaque strings; resolver, transport and ssh were rewired onto them. Greenfield per owner decision: no migration of existing keychain entries, no dual-read.

Verified rather than taken on report: 'go build ./...' clean; 'go test -race ./...' green across all 16 packages; no SecretID appears anywhere in frontend/ (zero frontend changes, as designed — the wire API stays credentialId-keyed); and every Secret->string conversion in the tree sits inside internal/credential (the vault encryption callback and the keyring handoff) or internal/ssh/ssh_auth.go:124 (the auth-method handoff), which is exactly the boundary ADR-0011 §2 permits.

title: EDITOR-W7: ADR-0010 — CodeMirror 6 as the editor core (runs before implementation)
description:
Spec W7, ordered FIRST among the code tasks. ADR-0004 section 3 is accepted and says avoid contenteditable; writing W1-W5 against it and documenting afterwards means every intermediate commit contradicts an adopted decision with nothing authorizing the change. AGENTS.md: if an AD is wrong, change it deliberately rather than routing around it.

Record: the contenteditable ban targeted the HAND-ROLLED variant and stays in force for it — CM6 is the mitigation for the very IME, undo and selection problems that motivated the ban. Record the measured bundle cost (321 KB raw / 102 KB gzip, reproduction command in the spec), the two admitted behaviour changes (wrapped lines now grow the box; undo moves from native to CM6 history), and that per-target decoration ownership is deferred to nocx-w7h.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0010 merged and ADR-0004 section 3 annotated as revised, so a future reader cannot follow the old sentence into a hand-rolled overlay.

title: STORE-1: shared storage path resolution (config / data / cache dirs)
description:
ADR-0011. One component resolves where things live, distinguishing OS roles: configuration documents in the config dir, content.db in the application-data dir, disposable indexes in the cache dir, secrets in the keychain. On macOS these may resolve under the same Application Support tree; on Linux the XDG distinction is real.

Removes the os.TempDir() fallback at internal/app/app.go:66, which writes profiles to the fixed shared path /tmp/nocx-profiles.json.
acceptance_criteria: A single injected component returns the four locations per platform. No store computes its own path. The /tmp fallback is gone; failure to resolve a location is an explicit error, not a silent fallback.
close_reason: STORE-1 landed: internal/storage.Paths + NewOSPaths(appName) resolving config/data/cache per OS role, no fallback — an unresolvable role is an explicit error. internal/app/app.go now constructs it at the composition root and propagates the error out of New(); the os.UserConfigDir warn-and-continue branch, the configDir=='' branch and the os.TempDir() fallback that wrote profiles to the shared /tmp/nocx-profiles.json are deleted (grep confirms zero matches in internal/app). profile.NewJSONStore receives paths.ConfigDir()/profiles.json. Tests: 5 Linux subtests covering XDG overrides, XDG-unset defaults, and the HOME-unset error path; macOS subtests skip off-platform.

title: PR11-T10: replace the vault's unauthenticated AES-CBC with an AEAD
description:
internal/credential/vault.go:97-114 persists bare AES-CBC with no MAC, and :274-295 accepts padding after checking only the final length byte. Modified ciphertext can decrypt successfully into altered plaintext — malleable, unauthenticated encryption.

Use an AEAD with versioned parameters so the format can be migrated later. Note the vault is the non-keychain path; PR11-T7 changes the type it stores but deliberately does not touch this.
acceptance_criteria: Ciphertext is authenticated; a single flipped bit in a stored blob fails decryption with a clear error rather than yielding altered plaintext. Parameters carry a version. Existing stored secrets migrate or are re-prompted, decided and recorded.
close_reason: AES-256-GCM replaces the unauthenticated AES-CBC in 2f30116. Format v2 is versioned, AAD binds version/salt/iterations/key length, nonce and salt are fresh per Marshal from crypto/rand, v1 vaults are refused explicitly, and auth failure is indistinguishable from a wrong passphrase. Five tamper tests (ciphertext byte, tag byte, version field, old-format refusal, wrong-password indistinguishability) — verified they fail on the shape of code being replaced, which a round-trip test would not. KDF deliberately untouched, split out as nocx-dcd.

title: PR11-T6: deleting a credential deletes its secrets
description:
Plan v3 Task 6. internal/transport/ws.go:998-1010 deletes metadata only; the keychain entry is orphaned permanently.

Needs T4 first because the reference model must be stable: password saves by credential ID key on Identity{User: credentialID} while key passphrases key on KeyHash, and metadata stores only KeyPath — so once metadata is gone there is no hash left to derive. Load the metadata BEFORE deleting it, derive both keys, then delete metadata first and secrets after (ADR-0011 section 4: a brief unreachable orphan beats metadata pointing at a deleted secret).

INTERIM IMPLEMENTATION LANDED in b9b0485 — deliberately left open, and the remaining dependency is real rather than bookkeeping.

What shipped: credentials.delete derives both secret keys before removing metadata (a passphrase keys on HashKey of the key material while metadata holds only KeyPath, so metadata-first would strand it forever), then deletes metadata and both secrets best-effort with errors.Join, per ADR-0011 §4 — a brief unreachable orphan beats a dangling reference. A missing key file returns an error rather than skipping silently. Four tests, the passphrase one confirmed to fail on the naive implementation.

Why this stays open: it is blocked by nocx-r60 (STORE-3), and that bead says why — it generalises the Secret type into a capability with stable SecretID references, 'which is what PR11-T6 needs to delete the right secrets'. The shipped version derives keys ad hoc: the password from the credential ID, the passphrase by re-reading the private key file and hashing it. That works, but it is exactly the fragility STORE-3 removes, and it is the direct cause of nocx-dm0 — with a stable SecretID there would be nothing to re-derive from a file the user may already have deleted.
