close_reason: INVALID — the premise is false and I should have read the call site before filing it. settings.ts:473 already guards: 'if (decl.control !== "secret" && decl.default !== undefined) controlCol.append(this.renderProvenance(decl))'. A secret declaration therefore renders no provenance badge and no Reset button at all, so the behaviour this bead describes cannot occur. Filed 2026-07-27 from reading renderProvenance() in isolation and reasoning about Declaration.default being optional, without checking who calls it. The nocx-njrx.3 worker found the guard and said so in its round-2 report. Note the guard also makes the dropped hasDefault parameter redundant for a better reason than the one given in the revision brief: the caller has already established it.

title: multi-tab-input:13 fails on the headless e2e path but passes under wails dev
description:
`multi-tab-input.spec.ts:13` ("first tab still accepts input after second tab is created")
fails on the headless devharness + vite path while passing on the `wails dev` path that CI
runs. It is green in CI — main run 30219766801 at e5a4ae2 passed all three jobs — so nothing
is broken for the gate today. What is broken is the cheap local signal.

## Measured

On `main` at e5a4ae2, headless path, full suite, three consecutive runs:

```
run 1: 1 failed [chromium] multi-tab-input.spec.ts:13 · 37 passed · 2 skipped
run 2: 1 failed [chromium] multi-tab-input.spec.ts:13 · 37 passed · 2 skipped
run 3: 1 failed [chromium] multi-tab-input.spec.ts:13 · 37 passed · 2 skipped
```

Run in isolation (`npx playwright test e2e/multi-tab-input.spec.ts`) the same spec passes
4/4 on both engines, so the failure is order- or state-dependent within the suite rather
than a property of the spec alone. Which engine loses also varies: on a branch carrying the
same code it surfaced under webkit instead, and two of three runs were fully green.

## Why it matters

This is the second instance of the same structural problem, and the first one cost a full
investigation (nocx-5zl4): the headless path and the `wails dev` path do not exercise the
same application, so "green locally" and "green in CI" are different claims. Here the
divergence points the other way — headless is redder than CI — which is the less dangerous
direction but still means a developer cannot trust a local full-suite run to be meaningful.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start `cmd/devharness` and `vite`; export `NOCX_WS_PORT`, `NOCX_WS_TOKEN`, `NOCX_BASE_URL`.
2. `npx playwright test` (whole suite, not the single spec).
3. `multi-tab-input.spec.ts:13` fails; the same spec passes when run alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

Either the spec passes on both e2e paths, or the reason it cannot is understood and written
down — and if it genuinely depends on the wails runtime, it says so and skips on the headless
path rather than failing there. A developer running the full suite locally gets a result they
can act on.

title: Keyboard handling is gated on a CSS class instead of the authoritative active state
description:
`terminal-content.ts:280` gates keyboard handling on `target.classList.contains('active')`
— a CSS class read as control flow.

The authoritative value already exists. `Tab.setActive` (tabs.ts:91-92) sets `this._active`
and then toggles the class on the very next line. The fix reads the class rather than the
state, so ownership is re-derived from presentation.

Three reasons this matters more than style:

1. **It crosses the nocx-njrx migration boundary.** `tabs.ts` sets the class and WILL be
   rewritten in Solid. `terminal-content.ts` reads it and stays imperative under AD-6.
   That is the single seam most likely to break silently during the migration: a Solid
   rewrite that names the class differently, or stops setting it on the same element,
   breaks keyboard input in a file the migration never touched, with no type error.
2. **ADR-0012 forbids exactly this shape.** It states that state crosses the terminal
   boundary through explicit imperative methods, never by inspecting markup.
3. **`'active'` is a bare string in eight places across four files** — sidebar.ts,
   tabs.ts, tab-strip.ts (four occurrences), terminal-content.ts — with no shared
   constant. A rename in one file silently changes behaviour in another.

WHY IT SHIPPED ANYWAY, so nobody re-argues it: `TabContent` exposes only `mount`,
`viewportChanged`, `focus` and `dispose`. There is no activation hook, so the worker had
no explicit channel to use. Blocking a P0 input fix on widening that interface was the
wrong trade; fixing it properly afterwards is the right one.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not a runtime symptom today. To see the coupling:

```bash
grep -rn "'active'" --include=*.ts frontend/src | grep -v test
sed -n '88,95p' frontend/src/tabs.ts        # the authoritative _active, and the class
sed -n '278,282p' frontend/src/terminal-content.ts   # the class being read back
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- `TabContent` gains an explicit activation signal — for example
  `setActive(active: boolean): void`, delivered by the presentation layer the same way
  `viewportChanged` already is — and `TerminalContent` keeps its own flag from it.
- `terminal-content.ts` no longer reads any CSS class to decide whether to handle input.
- The e2e coverage from nocx-4ff.28 still passes, and a unit test asserts the handler is
  inert for a non-active content instance.
- Whatever remains of `'active'` as a string is presentation only. If a shared constant is
  worth introducing for the rest, say so; if not, say why.
- Coordinate with nocx-njrx: if the Solid migration is already underway on `tabs.ts`, this
  seam change belongs to that work rather than beside it.
notes: In scope for the shell rewrite: keyboard handling gated on a CSS class is the same defect class as the sidebar reading DOM for state. The ownership table (nocx-82l9.7) names the authoritative active-tab slice; this bug is fixed against that slice, not against .active.
close_reason: BaseTabContent records the active flag when setVisible is called, and TerminalContent's keyboard handler reads it instead of classList.contains('active'). The class remains for styling. Verified: 777 unit tests, and multi-tab-input, click-focus and command-editor pass 12/12 in both engines. Note: the ownership table specified this fix and nobody applied it — the bead read as handled because it was described.

title: Dead code: createRegistry() in input-target.ts has no production caller
description:
Found while reviewing nocx-njrx on 2026-07-26. Standalone deliberately: input-target.ts stays imperative under AD-6, the SolidJS migration never touches it, and this must be fixed on its own merits rather than ride along with a migration.

createRegistry() in frontend/src/input-target.ts has no caller outside tests. TerminalContent instantiates ShellInputTarget directly (terminal-content.ts:178) and calls submit() on it (line 199). The InputTargetRegistry abstraction from ADR-0004 section 3 is unused.

The tests are what hid it — a test calling createRegistry looks exactly like a real caller to a linter. Our deadcode gate (nocx-ckoy.1) is Go-only, which is why nothing flagged it.

Decide, do not just delete on sight: either the registry is the intended design and something should be using it, in which case wire it and say where; or ADR-0004 section 3 describes an abstraction the product did not need, in which case delete the code and amend the ADR so the document stops describing something that is not there. 'Clean-only: no dead code' in AGENTS.md points at deletion, but the ADR makes it a decision rather than a chore.
acceptance_criteria: createRegistry is either reachable from the composition root or deleted; if deleted, ADR-0004 section 3 is amended to match; frontend tests referencing it are updated or removed; gates green.

title: Delete the frontend spikes — 1,657 lines nothing imports
description:
Free reduction of the migration surface, isolated in its own directories, takeable by anyone at any time.

frontend/src/spike/dom-scrollback.ts (810) and frontend/src/spikes/gutter-spike.ts (476) plus gutter-spike.test.ts (371) are referenced by nothing outside themselves. Measured 2026-07-26: grep for importers returns only the spike files and the spike's own test.

They are also absent from the epic's own accounting — the description totals 4,731 migrating + 4,344 staying = 9,075, against 10,593 real non-test lines under frontend/src. The spikes are most of that gap, so removing them makes the epic's numbers true as well as making the work smaller.

Note the two near-identical directory names, src/spike/ and src/spikes/ — both go.

OWNS FILES: frontend/src/spike/, frontend/src/spikes/. Nothing else.
acceptance_criteria: Both directories are gone; build, typecheck, lint, vitest and the e2e suite are green; no remaining file references them.
notes:
WAVE-1 OWNERSHIP RULING 2026-07-27 (coordinator). The bead said 'OWNS FILES: src/spike/, src/spikes/. Nothing else.' Measured, that is not enough to satisfy its own acceptance criterion 'no remaining file references them'. Two references live outside those directories: frontend/spike.html (its only content is a script tag for /src/spike/dom-scrollback.ts) and frontend/eslint.config.js:13 (ignores 'src/spike/**'). Ruling: spike.html is ADDED to this bead's ownership — nothing else references it. The eslint ignore entry is NOT: nocx-njrx.1 owns that whole config file and is rewriting it in parallel, so the stale ignore is removed by the coordinator after both branches land. An ignores entry pointing at a deleted directory is harmless in the interim.
REVIEW 2026-07-27 (coordinator). Worker diff accepted: 1,844 lines deleted (1,657 TS + 187 HTML), vitest 26 files/539 tests -> 25/517, delta exactly gutter-spike.test.ts. Merged as f4a88a2.

One inaccuracy in the worker's report, corrected by the coordinator rather than sent back: it stated 'the only code-level reference is eslint.config.js'. Not so — the ROOT directory spike/dom-scrollback/ (24 tracked files, the nocx-4ff.17 spike artifact) held five Playwright drivers (validate.ts, validate.mjs, perf-test.mjs, screenshots/capture.mjs, screenshots/capture-dynamic-padding.mjs) that all navigate to VITE_URL/spike.html — the page this bead deleted. They could no longer run at all. Deleted in a3f1ceb (863 further lines), keeping REPORT.md, DESIGN-NOTES.md and the screenshots as the record of the spike's findings, with the report amended to say the code is gone and why. That directory was never in this bead's ownership list, which is why the worker did not look there.
close_reason: Both spike directories and frontend/spike.html deleted (1,844 lines); coordinator additionally removed 863 lines of orphaned Playwright drivers in the root spike/dom-scrollback/ that could no longer run, keeping REPORT.md and the screenshots as the record. Gate on the merged trunk: typecheck, eslint --max-warnings 0, 544 unit tests, build, prettier all green; e2e 18/18 webkit and 19/20 chromium, the single chromium failure being a pre-existing flake reproduced on origin/main and filed separately.

title: [epic] The left panel is a real multi-view sidebar, with a local file tree as its first view
description:
The left panel becomes a real multi-view surface, modelled on Orca's sidebar, with a
working local file tree as its first view.

## Where this came from

The sidebar shell exists (nocx-8yg.9, closed 2026-07-24): activity bar plus collapsible
panel, Ctrl/Cmd+B, persisted collapse state. It was built early and deliberately —
"cheap now, avoids restructuring". Its intended MVP content was the SSH host list, which
the owner descoped at the time into nocx-eab. What shipped was the shell plus a
placeholder view labelled "Sessions" that nothing was ever designed behind. Owner
clarified 2026-07-26: the intent is a panel like Orca's.

Reference: /home/dev/repos/orca, src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar/.

## Scope measured, not guessed

Orca's file explorer alone is **41 non-test files, ~6,900 lines**, and that is only the
explorer — the whole sidebar directory is 458 files / 4.1 MB. What those 41 files buy:
drag-and-drop, undo/redo, virtualised rows, an fs-watcher reconcile loop, keyboard
navigation, batch deletion with classification, auto-reveal, name-filter projection, a
selection model, and a background context menu.

nocx's frontend is vanilla TypeScript with no framework; Orca's is React. A 1:1 port is
not on the table. This epic must therefore define the MINIMUM USEFUL SLICE and name
everything it is not doing, or it becomes an area rather than a deliverable and never
closes — the exact failure that forced nocx-6ek and nocx-k0xk to be split.

## What the reference screenshot actually contains

- An activity icon row: files, blocks, git, tasks, plus a panel-toggle.
- A project header with the repo name and per-view actions (collapse-all, refresh, overflow).
- A filter box, "Find files", with a Names / Contents segmented toggle.
- A file tree: folders then files, git status markers in the gutter (`M`), an ignored/
  excluded entry rendered dimmed and italic (`build`).

## In scope

- The panel hosts SEVERAL named views, switched from the activity bar, each owning its
  own header actions. Today `SidebarImpl` supports one panel view and mixes in
  `action: 'tab'` entries that have no panel content at all — that mixing is the direct
  cause of nocx-rp2j.
- A local file tree view for the active tab's cwd: expand/collapse, lazy directory
  listing, click to reveal, respect for .gitignore.
- The name filter with its Names/Contents toggle, at least for Names.
- Git status markers, read-only.

## Explicitly out

- Remote / SFTP browsing. That is nocx-9le.5 and stays there.
- Drag-and-drop, undo/redo, batch delete, rename, background context menu — the bulk of
  Orca's 6,900 lines. File MUTATION is out entirely for this epic; the tree is read-only
  plus reveal.
- Contents search. The toggle may ship disabled with the Names half working.
- The blocks / git / tasks views from the screenshot. This epic delivers the multi-view
  MECHANISM plus ONE view; further views are their own beads.

## Decide first, in an ADR, before any code

1. **Does a file tree belong in a terminal at all?** This is not in docs/vision.md's
   roadmap, which orders the work editor core -> command blocks and shell integration ->
   terminal core, terminal UI and SSH client -> vault -> Warpify. A file explorer competes
   with every one of those for the same frontend. vision.md section 5 does not list it.
   The wedge is stated as "renders agent TUIs flawlessly AND is comfortable to live in,
   with no cloud" — an argument that it serves the second half is available but must be
   made, not assumed.
2. **Virtualisation.** A tree over a large repo without virtual rows will jank. Orca
   needed `FileExplorerVirtualRows`. Decide whether the first slice virtualises or caps
   the visible node count, and say which.
3. **Where the tree state lives.** This lands squarely on nocx-ycet — a second surface
   keeping its own private copy of "active cwd" is the pattern that epic exists to end.
4. **Which cwd.** Per active tab, or per window? Tabs can sit in different directories,
   and OSC 7 already reports cwd per tab.

## Relationships

- nocx-i74e (the "Sessions" placeholder means nothing) is resolved BY this epic — the
  placeholder becomes a real view or is removed. nocx-rp2j (empty CONNECTIONS panel at
  cold start) is caused by the same one-view-plus-tab-actions mixing.
- nocx-eab (SSH host list in the panel) becomes one of the views this mechanism hosts.
- nocx-vxqj (UI kit) owns the tree row, filter box and toolbar as components; this epic
  must consume that kit rather than hand-roll a third vocabulary.

## Success Criteria

The activity bar switches between at least two real panel views with no empty-panel state
at cold start; a local file tree renders the active tab's cwd, expands and collapses
directories lazily, hides .gitignore'd entries or marks them dimmed, filters by name, and
shows read-only git status markers; every control comes from the UI kit; tree and cwd
state is read from the shared store rather than a private copy; and the ADR recording the
four decisions above is merged before the first line of implementation.

title: PinnedOriginPolicy is dead code: production runs the policy the code calls development-only
description:
`PinnedOriginPolicy` exists, is tested, and has no production caller. Every running
instance uses `LoopbackOriginPolicy` — which the code itself documents as "the development
policy" (`internal/transport/ws_auth.go:72`).

Both wiring sites choose the loopback policy unconditionally:

- `internal/transport/ws.go:177` — `origins: LoopbackOriginPolicy{}` in `NewWSServer`
- `internal/transport/ws_auth.go:208` — same fallback inside `authorize` when `s.origins` is nil

`WithOriginPolicy` is never called outside tests, so nothing can select the pinned policy.

## Why it matters

The Origin check is the second of two controls in front of `/session`, behind which `open`
creates a PTY. With the loopback policy, ANY page served from an http(s) loopback origin
passes it — a local dev server, another local web app, anything the user happens to be
running on 127.0.0.1. The per-launch token is then the only thing left refusing that page.

This is not an exploitable hole today: the token is 32 bytes of crypto/rand, offered as a
subprotocol, compared in constant time, never logged and never written to disk, and a page
cannot guess it. The defect is that defence-in-depth designed as two independent controls is
running as one, silently, and the type that was written to be the production control is dead
code.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn "PinnedOriginPolicy" --include=*.go .` — definition and tests only, no caller.
2. `grep -rn "WithOriginPolicy" --include=*.go . | grep -v _test` — no production call site.
3. Read `internal/transport/ws.go:177`: the loopback policy is hardcoded at construction.

## Related backlog correction

`nocx-d1zq`'s description asserts that OriginPolicy is "already injected per runtime mode
(LoopbackOriginPolicy for development, PinnedOriginPolicy for production), so the distinction
exists in one place and needs generalising rather than inventing". That premise is false —
there is no injection to generalise. The epic should be re-read against the code before it is
worked. This is the same failure mode AGENTS.md check 5 describes for the vault: tests
calling a constructor look exactly like a caller that matters.

## Acceptance Criteria

The composition root selects the Origin policy deliberately by runtime mode, a packaged
build runs `PinnedOriginPolicy` with the origins the shipped webview actually sends, and a
test proves a loopback http origin is refused in the production configuration. `nocx-d1zq`'s
description is corrected to match what the code does.

title: Root prettier scope reformats Go test fixtures — testdata is input, not source
description:
The root prettier scope added by nocx-0fx reformats Go test fixtures. Commit 8d10616
rewrote `internal/importer/testdata/tabby-config.yml`, changing every double-quoted
scalar to single-quoted:

```
-  - id: "ssh:custom:prod-web1:11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"
+  - id: 'ssh:custom:prod-web1:11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555'
-  contents: ""
+  contents: ''
```

Not a correctness bug today — YAML treats the two forms identically, and
`go test ./internal/importer/...` passes. That is exactly what makes it worth a bead
rather than a shrug: the test stays green while the fixture stops being what it claims
to be.

The fixture's entire value is FIDELITY TO AN EXTERNAL FORMAT. It is supposed to be a
sample of what Tabby actually writes, and Tabby emits double-quoted YAML. It is now a
prettier-normalised artifact that no real Tabby installation would produce. The next
person to extend it will copy the house style rather than a real export, and the
importer will be tested against a format nobody emits.

The failure mode this sets up is worse than cosmetic: if a future fixture needs a
construct prettier rewrites more aggressively — block scalars, anchors, specific
escaping — the formatter will silently change the input under a test that keeps passing.

Fixtures are inputs, not source. They should be outside every formatter.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
git show 8d10616 -- internal/importer/testdata/tabby-config.yml
```

Observed: the fixture is reformatted to house style.
Expected: files under testdata/ are never touched by a formatter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `**/testdata/**` is in `.prettierignore` (and any equivalent formatter scope).
- `internal/importer/testdata/tabby-config.yml` is restored to double-quoted form, i.e.
  to what Tabby actually emits.
- A note in the importer package or the fixture itself records that it mirrors real
  Tabby output and must not be normalised.
- Check for other fixture directories caught by the same sweep before closing —
  `git show 8d10616 --stat` is the list to walk.

title: Test stubs live in non-test files — classify each, then move or delete
description:
Test doubles live in non-test files, which is the only reason they are visible
to reachability analysis at all — `deadcode` ignores `_test.go` by default.

From the sweep in nocx-ckoy.1:

- `internal/pty/pty.go:47` — `NewStub`, `Stub.Read/Write/Close/Resize/Done` (6)
- `internal/ssh/ssh.go:190` — `NewStub`, `Stub.Connect/Close`, `NewStubChannel`,
  `StubChannel.Read/Write/Close/onceClose/Done/Resize` (10)
- `internal/transport/transport.go:22` — `NewStub`, `Stub.Start/Stop` (3)

For each, establish which of three it is before touching it:

1. Used by tests in the same package -> move to a `_test.go` file. Disappears
   from the analysis, keeps working, and stops advertising itself as production
   API.
2. Used by tests in ANOTHER package -> it must stay exported and in a non-test
   file, or move to an `export_test.go`-style helper. Say so in the baseline
   entry with the consumer named; this is a legitimate permanent entry.
3. Used by nothing -> delete it. AGENTS.md: no dead code.

Check each individually. The three packages are unlikely to all be the same
case, and assuming they are is how a real test double gets deleted.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
deadcode ./... | grep -E "Stub"
grep -rn "NewStub\|StubChannel" --include=*_test.go .    # find the real consumers
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every stub is classified into one of the three cases above, with the evidence
  (the grep result) recorded in the bead.
- Case 1 and 3 stubs no longer appear in the deadcode baseline.
- Case 2 stubs remain with a baseline entry naming the cross-package consumer.
- `go test -race ./...` still passes — a stub deleted in error shows up here.

title: ADR: where UI state is stored, and how it differs from settings
description:
Two stores that both remember things will be confused for each other, so draw the line in writing before building the second one.

Must be settled:
- The distinction: the settings registry (internal/settings, nocx-8v51) holds what a user DELIBERATELY chooses and is versioned and exportable. UI state is what the app remembers WITHOUT being asked. Say why they are not the same store, or decide that they are.
- Where it is written: Go-side via internal/storage DocumentStore, or webview localStorage. Window geometry is only knowable to the Go/Wails side, which argues for Go; sidebar collapse is only knowable to the frontend, which argues the other way. A split is allowed but must be justified.
- Whether UI state is exported/imported by nocx-oqof's export surface. Probably not — restoring someone else's window position is wrong — but say so.
- Write policy: debounce interval during drag/resize, and what happens on an unclean shutdown.
- The missing-display fallback rule.

Depends on the store decision in nocx-ycet: if a central frontend store lands, the frontend half of UI state is a slice of it, not a parallel mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR in docs/decisions/ records where UI state is written, why it is separate from the settings registry, and the write/debounce/fallback rules; it is merged before geometry persistence is implemented.

title: Settings screen is nearly empty — inventory what should be a setting and file it to the owning epics
description:
The Settings screen holds exactly two settings — "Suppress OSC 52 clipboard
warnings" and "Tab placement" — because those are the only two ever registered.
Both live in the declaration block in internal/settings/settings.go (~L440-490);
no other package registers anything.

That is not a defect in the settings machinery. nocx-8v51 delivered a working
authoritative registry with a screen generated from it, and it does its job. The
gap is that the features which should be configurable never declared their
settings, so the screen the user opens looks like a stub.

The owner's reaction on 2026-07-26 — "in settings there is only nonsense" — is
about this, not about the two settings being wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An inventory exists of what SHOULD be a setting, and each item is either
  registered or has a bead in the epic that owns it. Known candidates and their
  owning epics:
  - font family, size, line height, theme — nocx-8yg
  - keyboard shortcuts — nocx-8yg (and nocx-2gf for editor keymap conflicts)
  - default shell and startup working directory — nocx-5mn
  - SSH defaults: keepalive, ready timeout, agent forwarding — see nocx-49x,
    which reports four SSH options already editable and never applied
  - vault unlock/lock behaviour on app start — nocx-25k9
  - UI language — nocx-dej6
  - transport verbosity — nocx-d1zq
  - update channel and auto-check — nocx-nfu5
- This bead does NOT register them itself. It produces the inventory and the
  beads, filed into the epics above, and then closes. Registering a setting is
  the job of the epic that owns the feature behind it.

title: Window size and position are not remembered — every launch is 1024x768
description:
The window opens at 1024x768 on every launch, whatever the user last set.

main.go:43-46 hardcodes `Width: 1024, Height: 768, MinWidth: 640, MinHeight: 480`
and nothing anywhere reads or writes window geometry.

First child of this epic and the one that proves the mechanism: it needs the
UI-state store decided (where geometry is written), debounced writes so dragging
a window edge does not hammer the disk, and the missing-display fallback.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the app, resize the window, quit.
2. Launch again.

Observed: 1024x768.
Expected: the size (and position) the window had at quit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Size and position restore across a restart, on the same display.
- Maximised and full-screen states restore as such, not as a raw pixel size.
- Geometry saved on a display that is no longer attached falls back to a
  visible default on the primary display — never restores off-screen.
- Writes are debounced during a drag/resize, not one write per resize event.
- Tests cover save-on-change, restore-on-start, and the missing-display
  fallback.

title: The Sessions activity-bar view is an empty placeholder that means nothing
description:
The activity bar ships a "Sessions" icon that opens an empty, unlabelled panel.
It is a deliberate placeholder — frontend/src/main.ts:182-184 says so: "Sessions:
placeholder, as on main. It is deliberately empty: the tab list lives in the tab
bar."

That comment was written when the sidebar could plausibly have become a second
home for the tab list; nocx-d3q since settled that question (the vertical strip
is the tab list, and the activity bar does not move). So the placeholder now
stands for nothing decided.

A user cannot tell a placeholder from a broken feature. Either it means
something or it should not be in the shipped activity bar.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the app, click the middle (terminal) icon in the activity bar.

Observed: an empty panel. No explanation, no empty-state text, no content ever.
Expected: either a feature, or nothing in the activity bar.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Decide with the owner, and record the decision in the bead before coding:
  (a) Sessions means saved/restorable terminal sessions — then it gets its own
      bead or epic and this one closes as superseded;
  (b) Sessions means the list of open tabs as an alternative to the strip —
      then it is scoped against nocx-d3q, which already settled placement;
  (c) it means nothing yet — then the view is REMOVED from the activity bar
      until it does.
- Whichever is chosen, no icon remains in the shipped activity bar that opens a
  blank panel.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN FRAMING 2026-07-26. The owner clarified the intent: the panel is meant to be a multi-view sidebar like Orca's, and 'Sessions' was never a designed feature — it is the placeholder left behind when nocx-8yg.9 shipped the shell and the SSH host list was descoped into nocx-eab. So the three options this bug offered (make it saved sessions / make it a tab list / remove it) were all the wrong question.

The answer is decided by the new epic: the placeholder either becomes a real view or is removed as part of building the multi-view mechanism. This bead now depends on that epic rather than standing alone.
close_reason: The Sessions placeholder is deleted (nocx-82l9.6). The activity bar now holds a view registry with no entries yet — Explorer, Git and Servers are their own beads — plus the settings gear in the actions zone. No icon opens a blank panel.

title: [epic] The app reopens as you left it: window geometry and UI layout persist
description:
Observed 2026-07-26 on main: window size is not remembered. main.go L43-L46 hardcodes Width 1024 / Height 768 / MinWidth 640 / MinHeight 480 and nothing reads or writes geometry, so every launch is 1024x768 regardless of how the user left it.

The owner asked whether we have a store for remembering component state. Partly: nocx-6ek landed internal/storage (DocumentStore) and internal/settings is an authoritative registry with revisions — but those hold SETTINGS (things a user deliberately chooses), and UI state is a different class (things the app should remember without being asked). Nothing persists the second class today; SidebarImpl reaches straight into localStorage for one key ('nocx.sidebar.collapsed', sidebar.ts L34) which is exactly the ad-hoc pattern this epic replaces.

SCOPE: a UI-state store distinct from the settings registry — window geometry (size, position, maximised, full-screen, display identity), sidebar collapse and active view, active tab. Decide where it is written (Go-side storage vs webview localStorage) and make every surface use it instead of its own key. Debounce writes so a drag does not hammer the disk.

EXPLICITLY OUT: restoring the tab SET and live PTY sessions across restarts — session restore is a much larger deliverable and is not in this epic. Only which tab was active, if a tab set is present.

DEPENDS ON A DECISION in the frontend-state epic: if a central store lands, UI state is a slice of it rather than a parallel mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Resizing, moving, maximising or full-screening the window and restarting restores the same geometry on the same display; sidebar collapse state and active view, and the active tab, restore too; geometry off a display that no longer exists falls back to a visible default rather than restoring off-screen; a test covers save-on-change, restore-on-start and the missing-display fallback.

title: [epic] Auto-update: finish the product surface — version, restart action, user control
description:
The update MECHANISM is done and closed under nocx-a75: ed25519 manifest verification, a transactional bundle swap with a journal, auto-rollback after three launches without a health confirmation, darwin and linux Platform implementations behind a seam, CI release builds and macOS notarization. This epic is NOT that. It is the product surface around it, which is unfinished in ways a user meets directly.

Verified gaps, each read from the code rather than assumed:

1. THE PENDING-RESTART NOTICE LIES BY OMISSION. main.ts calls showPendingRestart(('')) with an empty string and a comment saying "version unknown here; Go can enrich later", so after a successful apply the user is shown "nocx  installed — restart to apply" with a hole where the version belongs.

2. THERE IS NO WAY TO RESTART. showPendingRestart renders text only. The app tells the user to restart and gives them nothing to click, while ApplyUpdate already has the machinery to do it.

3. THE USER HAS NO CONTROL. The only declaration in internal/settings today is ClipboardOSC52Suppressed. There is no toggle for automatic checks and no channel selection, so a user cannot decline updates or opt into pre-releases. This became cheap only now: the typed settings registry, the generated screen and live application through SettingsObserver all landed in nocx-8v51, so each of these is one MustRegister call plus a consumer.

4. THE CADENCE IS HARDCODED. main.ts checks on start and then every 24 hours, with the interval written into the composition root.

Deliberately OUT of scope, so this stays a deliverable:
- Windows Platform implementation. That is platform coverage, a different axis, and belongs in its own epic if wanted — the seam from nocx-kv0 already exists to receive it.
- Any change to the verification, swap, journal or rollback machinery. It works and is tested; this epic consumes it.
- Release infrastructure and signing. Closed under nocx-a75.

## Success Criteria

A user can see which version is pending, restart into it from the notice itself, turn automatic checking off, and choose an update channel — and every one of those settings is declared in internal/settings, so it appears on the generated screen with no frontend change and survives a restart. No update-related interval or policy remains hardcoded in the composition root.

title: [epic] Localisation: the UI speaks a second language, including the generated settings screen
description:
The UI is English-only and hardcoded. Every user-facing string is a literal at its point of use — button captions, empty states, error text, tooltips, the update notice — and there is no catalogue, no locale selection and no plural or date handling anywhere in the codebase. A grep for i18n, gettext or Intl finds nothing.

THE NON-OBVIOUS PART, and the reason this is not a frontend-only job: the settings screen is GENERATED from typed declarations in internal/settings, and the label and description of every setting are English strings in Go. Translating only the TypeScript would leave the settings screen in English while the rest of the app changed language — a worse result than not starting. So the declaration registry is in scope, and how a declaration carries its translations is the first design question this epic has to answer, not an implementation detail to discover halfway.

Second design question, to be settled deliberately rather than by default: where the catalogue lives and who owns it. The registry is Go and the screen is TypeScript, so a single source shipped to both beats two drifting copies — but that is an assertion to test, not a conclusion.

Deliberately OUT of scope, so this stays a deliverable and not an area:
- Right-to-left layout. It is a real requirement and a different one; file it separately if wanted.
- Translating terminal CONTENT. The terminal renders whatever the program emits; that is not ours to localise (AD-6).
- POSIX locale for the PTY. That is a different meaning of the word and was already handled in nocx-5hs.
- Actually producing translations for any particular language beyond the one used to prove the mechanism.

## Success Criteria

The UI renders end to end in a second language, INCLUDING the generated settings screen, and adding a further language requires no code change — only a catalogue. A string that has no translation falls back visibly to the source language rather than rendering blank or as a key. No user-facing literal remains at its point of use in either the frontend or the settings declarations.

title: Settings tab has no narrow-viewport layout: the rail floors at 240px and the label column cannot shrink
description:
The Settings tab has NO narrow-viewport branch, and this is the original defect class reappearing rather than a cosmetic gap.

Measured on the integration branch: the only @media rules in frontend/src/style.css are prefers-reduced-motion. `.st-rail` is `flex: 0 0 clamp(240px, 28vw, 360px)`, so the rail has a HARD FLOOR of 240px, and `.st-label-col` is still `flex: 0 0 200px` with no shrink.

So at a ~500px window the rail takes 240px and the content column gets roughly 260px minus padding, where a 200px fixed label column plus a control squeezes — the same arithmetic that produced the reported bug in the 240px sidebar panel, just at a different breakpoint.

Required, per Part C of the design: the layout is WIDTH-responsive (never content-count-responsive). Below the breakpoint the rail collapses to a category picker or a search-first overlay, and the content column takes the full width. The breakpoint is chosen by whether BOTH columns remain usable, not by copying a reference screenshot.

Also reconsider `.st-label-col: flex: 0 0 200px` while here: a fixed no-shrink column is what made the original failure possible. It is safe in a wide pane and unsafe in a narrow one, so it should either shrink or the row should stack below the breakpoint.

NOTE ON EVIDENCE: jsdom cannot exercise real layout, so this cannot be proven by unit tests. It needs either e2e with a resized viewport (see the test-suite epic) or a deliberate manual check at several widths — state which was done.

The TABS-C worker did not implement or disclose this; found by the coordinator reading the merged stylesheet.
close_reason:
Landed at 25d77f1, and fixed structurally rather than cosmetically. .st-label-col is now flex: 0 1 200px with min-width: 0 — it can shrink, which removes the arithmetic that caused the original defect (a fixed 200px column inside 192px of content). Below the breakpoint the rail collapses and the section nav hides; four .st-narrow rules carry it.

Worth recording because it is better than the brief asked for: the breakpoint is NOT a media query. It keys off the ContentViewport pushed down by the presentation layer (NARROW_BREAKPOINT_PX = 640, toggling .st-narrow on the container). A media query reads the WINDOW width, but Settings lives in a tab pane whose width is not the window's — the sidebar panel takes space now and the vertical tab strip will take more — so the pushed pane rectangle is the only correct signal. This is the B.5 geometry authority, which cost a rejected round to get right, paying off in a way nobody planned.

STILL OWED, disclosed by the worker and confirmed: the layout is unverified by automated tests because jsdom cannot exercise real layout. The reasoning at 640px is recorded in the code comment; visual confirmation at several widths is owed and belongs to e2e or a manual check.

title: Resolve two stale in_progress claims by reading the code, not the tracker
description:
nocx-q36 ('Restore CI on PR to main') is in_progress and assigned to shady2k, inside nocx-xx56 which is blocked on nocx-rdkh. The owner does not remember whether it is live work or a claim left over from an earlier session, and said it needs checking against the code.

Same question was open for nocx-5mn.4 (OSC 133 shell hooks) until nocx-5mn was unparked; it is no longer a contradiction, but the claim may be equally stale and is worth checking in the same pass.

WHAT TO CHECK, in the repo rather than in beads:
- nocx-q36: does .github/workflows/ci.yml currently have a pull_request trigger for main? The bead says commit 0adab78 narrowed triggers to release/**, v* tags and workflow_dispatch, and that nocx-q36 restored them. If the trigger is there, the work is done and the bead should be closed, not left claimed.
- nocx-5mn.4: does the shipped rc script emit OSC 133 A/B/C/D markers? internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash and the zsh equivalent. Note nocx-4ff.16 recorded a version bump 6->7 and a __nocx_preexec_done change, so part of this may already be in.

Beware the trap this backlog has already been burned by: nocx-4ff.16 lists nine items as 'FIXED + tested' that were never committed, and nocx-0oc proves at least one of them is absent from main. A bead saying work is done is not evidence. Read the file.

DONE WHEN: both claims are either closed with the commit that satisfied them, or released back to open with the in_progress claim removed — and in both cases the answer came from the code.

title: Modified-only filter in the Settings tab: wire it to snapshot provenance once the branches are integrated
description:
The modified-only filter in the Settings tab is not implemented, and the reason is a branch artefact of how this programme was sequenced: TABS-C was cut from origin/main, where the settings snapshot has no "overridden" field. That field exists on the settings branch (SETTINGS-1, fb90d47) and carries provenance.

So this is not a design gap — it is work that becomes possible the moment the settings branch and the tab branch are integrated. Do it AFTER that merge.

Required shape, unchanged from the design: Customized/Default comes from PROVENANCE (key present in the overridden set), never from comparing the value to the default. An explicit override that happens to equal the current default is still customization, because it pins the value against future default changes — which is exactly the distinction export/import depends on. Secret rows never claim modification; they have no default.

The filter itself: a modified-only toggle in the rail with a live count, plus per-section counts, all derived from the snapshot rather than from any frontend list of keys.
close_reason:
Landed at 25d77f1. The filter logic already existed in SettingsViewImpl; this surfaces it in the tab's rail with a live count and per-section badges, which became possible only after integration brought the 'overridden' field and SettingsContent together.

The risk I flagged did not materialise: state remains SINGLE-OWNER. modifiedOnly still lives in SettingsViewImpl, and the rail drives it through new accessors (setModifiedOnly / isModifiedOnly / getModifiedCount / getModifiedBySection) plus an onStateChanged callback for badge recomputation. The worker described this as 'bidirectional sync', which reads worse than what it built — it is one owner and an observer.

The binding requirement holds, verified rather than taken on report: Customized derives from PROVENANCE ('control !== secret && overridden.has(key)'), and grep finds NO value-vs-default comparison anywhere in settings.ts or settings-content.ts. Secrets are excluded from the counts. No setting key appears as a string literal in the frontend.

title: SettingsContent integration tests: singleton dedup, Cmd+comma from alt-screen, deep-link reveal-and-focus
description:
The TABS-C worker (nocx-h4e2, landed c30cea5) did not write the integration tests its brief listed under "tests that matter more than rendering assertions". The feature works and the gate is green, so this is a coverage gap, not a defect — but it is the coverage that would catch the regressions this surface is most exposed to.

Write them:
- opening Settings twice yields ONE tab (singleton dedup through the registered SingletonKey, not an ad-hoc check)
- Cmd/Ctrl+, focuses an EXISTING Settings tab from a terminal tab and from alternate-screen state
- closing and reopening Settings creates a fresh view
- a save while a filter is active does not make the row vanish unexpectedly
- a deep link into a filtered or scrolled section reveals AND focuses the control
- Settings never enters a restore record

Note for whoever picks this up: jsdom cannot exercise real layout, so do not attempt to assert the 192px overflow fix here — that belongs to e2e (see the test-suite epic).
close_reason:
Landed at f2e235a: 9 integration tests in settings-content.test.ts driving SettingsContent through TabManager.openTab — singleton dedup (through the manager, not merely asserting the constants export), Cmd/Ctrl+comma, close-and-reopen creating a fresh view, the null restore descriptor, the save-while-filter-active interaction between SettingsContent and SettingsViewImpl, and scrollToKey deep-link behaviour.

These are the seams the 24 pre-existing component tests do not reach. No production code changed, which is exactly what a test-only task should look like — the worker had an explicit instruction to escalate rather than change production code to make something testable, and did not need to.

Test count 526 -> 535, verified by running the suite, not from the report. Gate: prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 535 passed (26 files), Go clean.

Still owed and unchanged: the 192px overflow fix is unverified by automated tests, because jsdom cannot exercise real layout. That belongs to e2e.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
COORDINATOR UPDATE — partially overlapped by the rail work (25d77f1), but this bead stays OPEN.

The nocx-wbtv/nocx-v98h worker created settings-content.test.ts with 24 tests. Checked what they
actually cover, rather than assuming the overlap:

COVERED (component level, so remove these from this bead's scope):
  - surface/singleton constants are exported
  - two-pane layout renders with rail and content
  - rail contains search input and section navigation
  - section nav lists every section in declaration order
  - modified-only toggle with count; count excludes secrets
  - toggle drives the SettingsViewImpl filter; content filter bar stays in sync
  - per-section modified counts
  - st-narrow class applied and toggled at the 640px boundary
  - search filters rows and sections
  - dispose removes the container from the DOM

STILL NOT COVERED — this is what remains, and it is integration level, not component level:
  - opening Settings TWICE yields ONE tab. The existing test only asserts the singleton CONSTANTS
    are exported; it does not exercise dedup through TabManager.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+, focuses an EXISTING Settings tab, from a terminal tab and from alternate-screen state
  - closing and reopening Settings creates a fresh view
  - a save while a filter is active does not make the row vanish unexpectedly
  - a deep link into a filtered or scrolled section reveals AND focuses the control
  - Settings never enters a restore record

The distinction matters: everything covered so far tests SettingsContent in isolation. What remains
needs TabManager, the singleton registry, the global keybinding and the restore descriptor — the
seams where this surface actually integrates, and where the regressions would hurt.

Still true and worth repeating for whoever takes this: jsdom cannot exercise real layout, so do not
attempt to assert the overflow fix here. Visual confirmation at several widths is owed separately
(see nocx-v98h's close reason).

title: [epic] SSH port forwarding: local, remote and dynamic tunnels
description:
An isolated feature on top of the SSH client (nocx-9le), not a child of it: the SSH client epic delivers 'connect to a host and get a shell', and forwarding is a separate capability with its own UI, its own lifecycle and its own failure modes. Bundling them would make nocx-9le unfinishable, which is the pattern this backlog just moved away from.

This is squarely on the differentiator. docs/vision.md section 2 names Tabby as the tool with 'the ergonomics developers love ... strong SSH', and forwarding is a large part of what that means in practice — reaching a database behind a bastion, exposing a local dev server to a remote box, or running a browser through a SOCKS proxy without touching a config file.

SCOPE:
- Local forward (-L): a local port reaches a host:port on the far side.
- Remote forward (-R): a port on the far side reaches something local.
- Dynamic forward (-D): a local SOCKS proxy over the connection.
- Lifecycle bound to the session, server-authoritative like the session id (AD-7): a tunnel dies with its connection and never outlives it silently.
- Configured per SSH profile and persisted through the storage capability (ADR-0011) — no second config store.
- Visible state: which tunnels are up, which failed and why. A forward that silently did not bind is the single most common way this feature wastes an afternoon, so 'address already in use' has to reach the user rather than a log line.

OPEN, decide in this epic: whether a forward can be added to a live session or only at connect time.

OUT: anything requiring a relay or a cloud endpoint — that is nocx-if6 territory and stays there.

DONE WHEN: all three forward types work against a real sshd, are configured from the UI and survive a restart with their profile, a tunnel's state and its bind errors are visible to the user, and every tunnel is gone when its session ends.
acceptance_criteria: all three forward types work against a real sshd, are configured from the UI and survive a restart with their profile, a tunnel's state and its bind errors are visible to the user, and every tunnel is gone when its session ends.

title: [epic] Program-scoped permission grants, starting with OSC 52 clipboard
description:
Homeless child given its own epic. nocx-3cc was parented to the renderer epic while chasing a dependency, which was wrong: a permission model is not a rendering concern.

nocx-3cc: clipboard writes are denied by default and the banner offers 'Allow clipboard writes', but the grant is bound to the whole app rather than to the program that asked. Allowing vim to set the clipboard should not silently allow anything else that runs afterwards.

The generalisation is the point and is why this is an epic rather than a stray task: OSC 52 is the first program-initiated action needing consent, and it will not be the last. The grant model — what a grant is scoped to, how long it lives, where it is stored, how a user revokes it — is decided once here.

DONE WHEN: a clipboard grant is bound to the requesting program rather than the app, survives a restart, is revocable from the UI, and the scoping rule is written down so the next program-initiated action reuses it instead of inventing a second model.
acceptance_criteria: a clipboard grant is bound to the requesting program rather than the app, survives a restart, is revocable from the UI, and the scoping rule is written down so the next program-initiated action reuses it instead of inventing a second model.

title: [epic] Gate coverage: everything that ships is formatted, linted and checked
description:
Carved out of nocx-k0xk. Housekeeping with a real edge: the gates today have holes, and a hole in a gate is indistinguishable from a passing gate.

- nocx-0fx: prettier and eslint run only inside frontend/, so playwright.config.ts and all of e2e/ are checked by nothing — and prettier currently rejects all four root TS files.
- nocx-4iy: the pre-commit hook checks the working tree, not the staged snapshot, so a partially staged commit can pass locally and fail CI.
- nocx-5vi: devharness listens on a random port, forcing a socat bridge in the VM-to-Mac dev loop; honouring NOCX_WS_PORT drops it.
- nocx-u4b: evaluate gremlins for Go mutation testing — does the suite assert behaviour or merely execute it.

DONE WHEN: every file that ships is inside a format and lint gate, the pre-commit hook checks what is actually being committed, and the mutation-testing question is answered either way.
acceptance_criteria: every file that ships is inside a format and lint gate, the pre-commit hook checks what is actually being committed, and the mutation-testing question is answered either way.
notes:
EDGE REMOVED 2026-07-26: nocx-ckoy no longer depends on nocx-xx56.

The criterion in AGENTS.md is file collision — 'two people cannot hold these at once' — not sequence. These two do not collide: nocx-xx56 is GitHub branch protection, a repository-configuration deliverable that makes an EXISTING check required; nocx-ckoy edits .githooks/pre-commit, the prettier/eslint configs and frontend/package.json scripts. Two agents can hold them simultaneously without landing in the same files.

The edge encoded 'make the check required first, then widen what it checks'. That is a schedule, and AGENTS.md records that 13 of 20 epic-level edges turned out to be exactly this and were removed. It is also arguably backwards: widening the gate BEFORE it becomes required is the safer order, since making a check required and then immediately broadening it breaks everyone at once.

Raised with the owner in the same session; they had asked for the prettier/eslint hole to be fixed, which this edge was preventing.

title: [epic] A PR to main shows a required green check
description:
Carved out of nocx-k0xk.

nocx-q36 restored ci.yml pull_request:[main] and it fires, but the check is not required — there is no branch protection on main, so nothing mechanically stops a red merge. nocx-63l enables it.

Deliberately separate from the suite-health epic: making a check required is a repository-configuration deliverable with a different owner and a different failure mode from fixing tests. It does depend on the suite being green first, which is a blocks edge, not a reason to merge the two.

DONE WHEN: a pull request to main shows a required check, and a red check blocks the merge.
acceptance_criteria: a pull request to main shows a required check, and a red check blocks the merge.

title: [epic] Export, import and backup: the user-facing surface
description:
Carved out of nocx-6ek.

internal/export implements all four ADR-0011 section 7 modes and is tested, but nothing reaches it: no export/import JSON-RPC methods in internal/transport/ws.go, no wiring at the composition root in internal/app/app.go, no UI entry point. The capability exists and no user can invoke it.

Deliberately its own epic rather than a child of a persistence bucket: it is a complete feature with a visible outcome, and it needs the settings-tab surface to land first.

DONE WHEN: a user can export their configuration, import it back, and take a backup from the UI; the RPC methods are wired at the composition root; and a round-trip export-import test passes.
acceptance_criteria: a user can export their configuration, import it back, and take a backup from the UI; the RPC methods are wired at the composition root; and a round-trip export-import test passes.
close_reason:
Epic complete: 1/1, and now unblocked — the nocx-v1pr edge it waited on is closed, because the export UI lives in the settings surface that epic delivered.

nocx-6ek.3 landed at 03cb36e: JSON-RPC methods, composition-root wiring and UI for the four ADR-0011 section 7 modes on top of an internal/export package that was implemented and tested but unreachable. The durable win is that the no-secret guarantee became structural — TestExportDoesNotImportCredential inspects production imports via 'go list -json' and fails the moment the dependency appears, so no wiring mistake can hand an export mode a resolved secret.

A defect caught in review would have shipped broken: portable encrypted export downloaded the JSON wrapper instead of raw bytes while import base64-encoded the JSON text rather than the ciphertext, so decryption could never have succeeded.

Owed: a real export -> file -> import round trip. Only the encoding path is covered by a Blob test; the full journey needs e2e.

title: [epic] Secrets vault: the user-facing vault on top of ADR-0011
description:
MVP scope, by owner's decision 2026-07-26. NOTE THAT docs/vision.md SECTION 5 SAYS OTHERWISE — it still lists the secrets vault under PHASE 2 (deferred). The tracker is right and the document is stale; see nocx-mqav's close reason for why sections 5 and 6 are not maintained.

The differentiator is the combination, and the vault is the half of it Ghostty and the other engines do not have — Tabby has a vault with a weak engine, Warp has the UX but needs the cloud. Shipping the combination without the vault ships neither half of the wedge, which is why this moved into MVP.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this epic does not rebuild it: nocx-6ek (ADR-0011) landed the storage capability, secrets as opaque references, an AEAD-encrypted store (nocx-1vr replaced the unauthenticated AES-CBC), a non-serializable Secret type (nocx-l7o), and the credential delete cascade (nocx-7l4). The SSH client already stores passwords and key passphrases through it. What is missing is everything a user touches.

SCOPE: a vault surface a person can actually use — list, add, edit and delete credentials; attach one to an SSH profile from the UI rather than by editing a profile; unlock/lock semantics and what happens on app start; and an honest answer for where the master key lives. vision.md section 11 records the settled constraint: single-machine, no sync. It leaves open whether the store is OS-keychain-backed or app-managed, and that decision belongs in this epic as an ADR before any UI work.

EXPLICITLY OUT: cloud sync and any form of shared vault, now and later (vision.md section 10). That non-goal is unaffected by the move into MVP.

RELATED, NOT OWNED HERE: nocx-dcd (hand-rolled PBKDF2 in the vault) and nocx-23v (redaction of known secrets in scrollback, ledger and clipboard) sit in nocx-6ek and stay there — both are storage-layer, and blocking them behind a UI epic would strand a standing crypto risk behind feature work.

DONE WHEN: a user can add, edit and delete a credential without leaving the app; an SSH profile can be pointed at a vault entry from the UI; the master-key decision is recorded as an ADR and implemented; and no secret value is serializable or reachable from the frontend as plaintext.
acceptance_criteria: a user can add, edit and delete a credential without leaving the app; an SSH profile can be pointed at a vault entry from the UI; the master-key decision is recorded as an ADR and implemented; and no secret value is serializable or reachable from the frontend as plaintext.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-07-26, verified against main: the 'WHAT ALREADY EXISTS' paragraph above overstates the starting point. The AEAD-encrypted store exists as code but is NOT wired — internal/app/app.go:81 constructs credential.NewKeychain(), and NewVault()/NewCredentialStore() have no non-test callers anywhere in the repo. The SSH client does NOT store passwords 'through it' as that paragraph claims; it stores them through the keychain.

So this epic is not 'backend done, build the UI'. Its first child nocx-25k9.1 is the wiring-and-ADR question, and it blocks the UI work: which store the product actually uses decides what the UI unlocks, whether there is a master passphrase at all, and whether lock/unlock semantics exist to expose. Do not start vault UI before it is answered.

title: Delete the wterm renderer — the bake-off is settled, and it degrades the TerminalRenderer contract
description:
Delete the wterm renderer. The bake-off is over and xterm.js won (ADR-0001); keeping a second implementation costs more than it buys, and it actively degrades the interface.

SCOPE, measured:

- frontend/src/renderers/wterm.ts — delete.
- frontend/src/renderers/index.ts — RendererName collapses to a single value, so the union, the case wterm branch, the ?r=xterm|wterm parsing and the "diagnostics escape hatch" comment all go. If the factory becomes vestigial, collapse it too — AGENTS.md forbids dead code. KEEP the TerminalRenderer interface: ADR-0001 value is that the VT frontend is replaceable, and that survives having one implementation.
- frontend/src/renderers/types.ts — two comments concede interface shape to wterm ("@wterm/dom never fires", "has no equivalent event — the callback is never"). Those concessions can now be removed, and doing so is what actually retires nocx-au6.
- frontend/package.json — drop the @wterm/dom dependency.
- Types ripple into tabs.ts and terminal-content.ts wherever RendererName is threaded.
- Docs mentioning wterm: docs/vision.md, docs/architecture.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-23-warp-command-experience-m1-foundation.md, docs/decisions/0005-linux-webkitgtk-forced-refresh-pump.md, and docs/decisions/0001-xterm-js-as-vt-frontend.md.

ADR-0001 is the sensitive one: it recorded that wterm stays switchable behind TerminalRenderer for re-testing. Removing wterm changes that decision, so amend the ADR deliberately with a superseding note rather than quietly editing the sentence. AGENTS.md is explicit that a wrong decision gets changed on purpose, not routed around.

RETIRES: nocx-au6 (TerminalRenderer advertises capabilities wterm silently does not have) and nocx-id3 (wterm translates wheel to arrow keys). Both close when this lands.

Also removes a live wart: wterm fitViewport approximated cell width as FONT_SIZE, i.e. a full em advance, where monospace advance is nearer 0.6em — so its computed columns were materially wrong. That approximation disappears with the file.
close_reason:
Landed at c2f6bee, verified against the diff. The interface survived; the second implementation and everything shaped around it did not: wterm.ts and the vestigial renderers/index.ts barrel deleted, RendererName and createRenderer collapsed, terminal-content.ts constructs XtermRenderer directly, @wterm/dom dropped from package.json and the lockfile.

What actually retires nocx-au6 is the second half: types.ts lost 8 @wterm/dom concession comments AND 8 members stopped being optional (registerMarker, cellHeight, viewportTopLine, onScroll, onRender, paneElement, getBufferLine, clearViewport). The interface no longer advertises what an implementation cannot honour. The payoff shows downstream in gutter.ts, which dropped its optional-call guards and its magic 'cellHeight ?? 15' fallback — that constant existed only because wterm might not supply a value.

ADR-0001 got a visible superseding note rather than a quietly rewritten sentence, which is what AGENTS.md requires of a changed decision. ADR-0005 references corrected. The historical plan under docs/superpowers/ deliberately left intact.

Also removed a live defect, not just dead code: wterm's fitViewport approximated cell width as FONT_SIZE — a full em, where a monospace advance is nearer 0.6em — so its computed columns were materially wrong.

Gate on the combined tree: prettier/eslint/tsc clean, vitest 427 passed (22 files), gofumpt clean, go test -race clean. The worker correctly did NOT run a whole-project typecheck and said so, because a second worker was editing the same worktree; the coordinator ran it at the phase gate.

title: One command to reconcile GitHub with beads: state, sub-issues, dependencies, board
description:
Everything currently on GitHub was put there by hand. `bd github sync --push-only` covers creation, bodies and labels — and nothing else. Measured gaps, each verified today:

| Step | bd covers it? |
|---|---|
| create issue, body, labels | YES |
| closed state | NO — 12 issues had to be closed by hand; until then subIssuesSummary.completed was 0 and epics showed 0% against a real 56% |
| sub-issue hierarchy | NO — bd pushes flat; links made via GraphQL addSubIssue |
| blocked-by dependencies | NO — GraphQL addBlockedBy (the field is blockingIssueId, not blockedByIssueId) |
| project membership + Status field | NO |
| milestone assignment | NO |

Extend cmd/roadmap with a github-sync mode that runs after `bd github sync --push-only` and closes those gaps. It already reads .beads/issues.jsonl and needs neither bd nor Dolt, so the same binary works locally and in CI.

HARD RULE: push only. `bd github sync` is BIDIRECTIONAL by default, and per the beads docs the local Dolt DB is canonical — a pull would let a GitHub edit overwrite the source of truth.

Two of the five steps disappear if the board built-in workflows (item closed -> Done, new issue -> add to project) are enabled in the board UI; they cannot be set from the CLI. Record whether they were enabled, because the sync must not fight them.

Caveat from the beads docs to note in the tool: the JSONL export cannot detect deletions or pruning, so a pruned bead may linger in a generated view.

DONE WHEN: one command brings GitHub into agreement with beads — state, hierarchy, dependencies, board membership and Status — and it is idempotent, so running it twice changes nothing.
close_reason: Not needed — see nocx-lg6r. The goal was 'the team sees where we are', and 'bd epic status' does that with one built-in command and zero maintenance. Automating the five gaps in bd github sync (closed state, sub-issue hierarchy, blocked-by dependencies, board membership, milestones) would mean maintaining our own field mapping over an API surface the docs deliberately leave unspecified. GitHub issues, milestones and the board were deleted at the owner's request.

title: Split docs/vision.md: strategy and non-goals stay, the duplicated roadmap moves to the generated view
description:
docs/vision.md holds two different kinds of content, and only one of them is duplicated by beads.

DUPLICATED, and must go: section 5 'MVP scope' (IN v1 / PHASE 2 / OUT) and section 6 'Strategic roadmap'. Epics in beads are the same facts, kept current by the work itself. Two places holding one fact is how a roadmap becomes visibly wrong and then stops being read.

NOT duplicated, and must stay: sections 1-4 (positioning, problem/motivation, target users, differentiator) and 7-11 (tech stack, platform and distribution, success criteria, NON-GOALS, open questions). A tracker holds work; it does not hold why we are building this, for whom, or what we deliberately refuse to do. Non-goals in particular have no representation in a task tracker — there is no status for 'we will not do this'.

REPLACE SECTIONS 5 AND 6 WITH A POINTER TO THE COMMANDS, NOT TO A FILE. There is no generated roadmap file and there will not be one: nocx-lg6r was closed WON'T DO by the owner on 2026-07-26. An earlier version of this bead told its implementer to point at docs/ROADMAP.md, which has never existed on main — do not do that, it would put a dead link in a document AGENTS.md names as a source of truth an agent reads first. The pointer is:

  bd epic status                      per-epic progress, live from the dependency graph
  bd ready --exclude-type epic        the queue
  docs/vision.md section 0            what is active now and what is parked

Section 0 already exists and already carries the active/parked state, so this task is a deletion plus a three-line pointer, not new prose.

Fold anything load-bearing from section 5's OUT list into section 10 rather than deleting it.

This matters operationally, not just tidily: a bead says 'add vertical tabs'; vision says what we are and what we are not, which is the only thing that stops an agent building a well-made unnecessary thing.

DONE WHEN: vision.md contains no scope list or roadmap that beads also owns, nothing from the OUT/non-goals content is lost, no link points at a file that does not exist, and AGENTS.md still correctly describes what vision.md is for.
close_reason:
WON'T DO — owner's decision, 2026-07-26, together with nocx-lg6r.

Both halves of the roadmap-projection idea are now closed: no generated docs/ROADMAP.md (nocx-lg6r) and no split of docs/vision.md (this bead). The human view of the roadmap is permanently 'bd epic status' plus 'bd ready --exclude-type epic', and docs/vision.md section 0 for what is active and what is parked.

ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCE, recorded so nobody rediscovers it as a bug: docs/vision.md sections 5 (MVP scope) and 6 (Strategic roadmap) stay, and they duplicate facts that beads also owns. They will drift, because nothing updates them when work lands — section 6's three phases are already coarser than the 15 epics in the tracker. Anyone reading vision.md for CURRENT scope should read section 0 and the bd commands instead; sections 5 and 6 are the original strategic intent, not a live status.

If that drift ever becomes actively misleading, the fix is this bead's original plan — delete sections 5 and 6, keep 1-4 and 7-11, fold anything load-bearing from section 5's OUT list into section 10 (non-goals), and point at the bd commands. Reopening is cheap; the work was never started.

title: cmd/roadmap: generate docs/ROADMAP.md from beads so the human view cannot drift
description:
The backlog is the source of truth for work, but nothing renders it for a human. The maintainer cannot see the volume and colleagues cannot see which milestone is active. A prototype proved the shape (Phase 1 at 43/80 tasks across 9 epics, 76 ready, 15 blocked) — this task makes it a repo artifact that cannot drift.

Build cmd/roadmap in GO — not Python or a shell script. The repo holds every language to the same gate (gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test), so a third language would arrive ungated.

It shells out to bd, aggregates, and writes docs/ROADMAP.md. Two bd calls are needed because neither alone is sufficient: `bd list --status all --json` carries labels but NOT dependencies; `bd query "status=<s>" --json` carries parent and dependencies but NOT labels. Merge them by id.

The page must show, per phase and per epic: closed/total children, the epic DONE WHEN criterion (every open epic now has one), how many children are ready, how many are blocked. Plus a global summary, a Take-next list of unblocked work by priority, and a mermaid flowchart of EPIC-LEVEL dependencies (that graph is genuinely useful; a fake mermaid progress chart is not — use a unicode bar in a table for progress, which renders everywhere).

It must also render, honestly and prominently, what the view cannot tell you: tasks belonging to no epic, epics whose children are all closed but which are still open, and any epic with no DONE WHEN. A roadmap that hides its own gaps is the kind people stop trusting.

Wire it as `make roadmap`.

Derived, never hand-edited: docs/ROADMAP.md carries a generated-file header naming the command that produces it.

DONE WHEN: `make roadmap` regenerates docs/ROADMAP.md from beads with no hand edits, the file shows per-epic progress and DONE WHEN criteria, and cmd/roadmap has tests that pass under go test -race.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-07-26. Two things in the close_reason turned out to be wrong, and one condition changed.

WRONG: 'A worker did finish an implementation (cmd/roadmap/main.go + test + Makefile target + a generated docs/ROADMAP.md) on branch shady2k/roadmap-projection.' That branch does not exist — not locally, not on origin, and 'git log --all -- cmd/roadmap' returns nothing. The work is gone. Whoever writes this now writes it from scratch; do not go looking for the branch.

WRONG, downstream: nocx-mqav was left open telling its implementer to point docs/vision.md at docs/ROADMAP.md. That file has never existed on main, so taking nocx-mqav before this bead would put a dead link in a document AGENTS.md names as a source of truth an agent reads first. nocx-mqav is now blocked on this bead.

CHANGED: the close_reason argued 'bd epic status prints the same thing with zero maintenance', which was correct when the only reader was the owner, who has bd installed. There are now colleagues who need to see what is happening and why feature work is paused, and requiring them to install a Go issue tracker to read a status page is not reasonable. The close_reason anticipated exactly this: 'If a repo-visible progress page is ever wanted — the one thing a community UI cannot give, since it needs no install and renders on GitHub — that branch is where it lives.'

Scope is unchanged from the original description. It must also render the parked tracks and why they are parked, which is new since the close: the backlog now encodes parking as epic-level blocks edges (nocx-k0xk.1), and a roadmap that showed 11 epics as merely 'open' would hide the single most important fact about the current state.
close_reason:
WON'T DO — owner's decision, 2026-07-26. No repo-visible roadmap page.

This closes the bead a second time, on different grounds than the first. The original close said the generator was redundant because 'bd epic status' prints the same thing; that reasoning was then undermined when the branch it pointed at turned out not to exist, and by colleagues needing a view without installing bd. The owner has now decided the page is not worth building at all. That settles it — no further reopening on the 'a colleague cannot read it' argument.

CONSEQUENCE, handled: nocx-mqav was blocked on this bead precisely so it could not put a dead docs/ROADMAP.md link into docs/vision.md, which AGENTS.md names as a source of truth an agent reads first. Closing this unblocks it, so nocx-mqav's description has been rewritten to point at 'bd epic status' and 'bd ready --exclude-type epic' instead of a generated file. Anyone taking nocx-mqav should read the current description, not the pre-2026-07-26 one.

The human view of the roadmap is therefore, permanently: 'bd epic status' for per-epic progress, 'bd ready --exclude-type epic' for the queue, and docs/vision.md section 0 for what is active and what is parked.

title: SETTINGS-4: generated state UX — Customized/Reset, modified filter, dataClass, bounds, honest load states, search
description:
Everything here is bucket 1 — derivable from existing declarations. NO literal setting key may appear in the frontend.

- Customized/Default from PROVENANCE (key in overridden), not value-vs-default comparison. An override equal to the current default is still customization: it pins the value against future default changes, which is exactly what export depends on.
- Reset per row. The RPC already exists (profiles.ts:295 -> settings.reset) and the UI has never exposed it.
- Modified-only filter with a count.
- dataClass-driven privacy/export treatment. It is declared in both settings.ts:15 and Go and currently IGNORED by the UI.
- Declared bound display (min/max), not only the HTML attributes.
- Distinct loading / load-failed / zero-declarations / no-search-match states. Fixes nocx-jwkw: refresh() swallows every failure and render() then prints "No settings declared", so a dead RPC is indistinguishable from an empty registry. Parallelise the sequential secretExists for-await loop while here.
- Search over label, description, section, key and select-option labels, with section breadcrumbs and keyboard operation.
- Stable per-row DOM id derived from the key. Do NOT interpolate a raw key into a CSS selector as rerenderRow does today (settings.ts:356) — assertValidKey (settings.go:440-449) only checks non-empty and uniqueness. Use a key->element map.

This ships INSIDE THE EXISTING SIDEBAR PANEL. The move to a tab is TABS-3. Do not change where settings are mounted.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md, three-bucket rule and Part C.
close_reason:
Verified at commit 608ad61. Bucket-1 only, no frontend key knowledge: Customized/Default from provenance (overridden set, not value-vs-default comparison), reset wired to the existing settings.reset RPC via st-reset-btn and gated on decl.default !== undefined so secrets and defaultless declarations do not claim modification, modifiedOnly filter, st-search bar, dataClass treatment, declared bound display, and a LoadState enum separating loading/ready/failed/empty. Binding invariant holds: grep finds no dotted-key literal in settings.ts. keyToDomId is 'st-setting-' + encodeURIComponent(key) — injective because decodable, with a regression test at settings.test.ts:881 covering a.b vs a_b. rerenderRow no longer interpolates a key into a CSS selector; a key->element rowMap replaces it.

CARRY-FORWARD for TABS-C deep links: encodeURIComponent does not escape '.', so an id like st-setting-clipboard.osc52Suppressed is valid HTML5 but splits into id+class in a raw CSS selector. getElementById and hash routing are safe; querySelector('#'+id) is not. Use getElementById or CSS.escape.

Worker disclosed it could not verify real browser layout or the 240px panel constraint, and that it ran prettier --write on its three owned files. Delivered by a dedicated worker on task_b8e9a1cd4169.

title: [bug] Settings screen shows 'No settings declared' when the RPC fails — load error is indistinguishable from an empty registry
description:
frontend/src/settings.ts:46-70 — refresh() wraps describeSettings()/getAllSettings() in a try with `catch { // Keep existing state on fetch failure }` and then renders unconditionally.

On the FIRST load there is no existing state: this.declarations is still [], so render() (L77-83) takes the empty branch and prints "No settings declared." A transport failure, a backend error and a genuinely empty registry all produce the same screen, and the user is told something false.

Needs distinct states: loading (skeleton), load-failed (message + Retry), zero declarations (neutral explanation), and — once search lands — no-matches.

Related, same method: secret existence is fetched sequentially in a for-await loop (L54-63), one round trip per secret-class declaration. Fine at one declaration, not at ten.

Found by a Codex design review, verified by reading the code. Independent of the settings-as-a-tab work.
close_reason: Fixed in 608ad61: a LoadState enum separates loading / ready / failed / empty (settings.ts:32-34, 55, 71, 100-103), so an RPC failure surfaces an error with a retry path instead of rendering 'No settings declared'. Verify the sequential secretExists for-await loop was also parallelised when reviewing nocx-t7uh.
